structured_checks.task: Code can be exported (GitHub or zip) and data downloaded
structured_checks.detail: run on 26 September 2026: the project zip export held the full source and its git history, but no database contents. Outside Replit it installed and built with pnpm 10 (pnpm 12 refused) once PORT and BASE_PATH were set, and ran against our own empty Postgres: schema created, a booking accepted and counted, admin login refused with a wrong password. sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 19 November 2026 on a Shopify development store, with the interface in English. We installed the app, switched on its theme embed and went through the seven step wizard for the free campaign up to the last screen. We did not submit the campaign, so no reviewer ordered or filmed anything, and we paid nothing.
findings: Install: no payment screen appeared. The permission screen asked to view customer and staff data and to edit customers, products, orders, discounts and the Online Store. The wizard was ready about 2 minutes after install.
Setup: campaigns stay locked until the Reviewers core script is switched on in the theme editor and saved. After that the app showed the embed as active.

Wizard: step 1 picks the product and the number of items to give away, 10 by default, and lists only products with at least 15 units in stock. Step 2 sets age range and gender, and the reviewer location is fixed to the US. Later steps set the request timing and optional screening questions and a brief of up to 750 characters.
Last screen: the summary showed 10 items, women 18 to 65 in the US, a review request 7 days after fulfillment, and the billing line Free. We did not press Submit for approval.

How reviewers get the product: they order it from your store with a free discount code that includes shipping, and you process the order like any other. You pay for the product and the shipping yourself.
Plans: the app listing shows a free first campaign of up to 10 videos and 1 campaign a month at $150. Inside the app of our development store the plan screen said no plans were available.
not_tested: submitting a campaign, real reviewer orders and received videos
exporting videos to other review widgets
the paid plan, billing and cancelling
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

Uninstall: the dialog asked for a reason, said app data is deleted and said a request to delete customer data goes to the developer within 48 hours.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 26 November 2026 on an existing Pabbly account, with the interface in English. We opened Pabbly Connect, built a webhook to text formatter workflow, added an API step, ran it live twice, read the task counter and opened the upgrade dialog and the Standard monthly checkout. We paid nothing.
findings: Start: Pabbly Connect opened from the Pabbly apps page with one click, no card and no extra form. The dashboard showed 100 tasks allowed and 0 used.
Free steps: the Free Task tooltip said Pabbly does not charge tasks for triggers and internal application steps. Run 1 with trigger and formatter used 0 tasks and counted 2 free ones.
Task count: after run 2 with an API step on our own robots.txt, the dashboard showed 1 task used, 99 left and 4 free tasks used.
Speed: the first result appeared after 3.3 minutes and the first live run after 3.7 minutes.
Email: the email step could not be used without our own SMTP server details; the only built in choice, SMTP (Pabbly), asked for them too.
Upsell: the first click on Create Workflow opened a full page lifetime offer with a countdown, and the upgrade dialog opened on the 3 year plan.
Plans: Standard $19 a month for 10,000 tasks, Unlimited $79; the Standard monthly checkout showed Pay $19 with card or PayPal and no VAT line.
not_tested: paying, the 30 day refund and cancelling
exporting or re-importing workflows
a support reply
team members and roles
email steps with our own SMTP server

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 22 November 2026 on a Shopify development store, with the interface in English. findings: Install: the permission screen lists customer data, staff data and store data such as orders. The app then opened straight on its dashboard, with no plan screen, no charge and no card. The dashboard said 300 free tracked orders every month, renewing monthly and not a one time trial.
Tracking: after we fulfilled the test order, it showed up in BestTrack within about 10 seconds with UPS detected. Within about a minute the status was Delivered, with the carrier's full history.
Warning gap: that history ran from a pickup on 12 June 2025 to a delivery on 5 December 2025, for an order placed on 16 November 2026. The app showed it as Delivered and gave no warning.

Emails: every customer status email, such as In transit and Delivery failed, was switched off by default. Mail sends from noreply@support.besttrack.app until you verify your own domain, and free email addresses cannot be verified.
Dropshipping mode: it starts paused and bundles region blocking, custom checkpoints and checkpoint emails. We did not switch it on.
Quota: our one new fulfilment counted as 1 of 300 and the estimated charge was $0.00.
Export: a CSV with 19 columns came down at once, including pickup, fulfilment and delivery dates.
not_tested: the customer facing tracking page, because the test store is password protected
sent status emails and the Klaviyo connection
dropshipping mode switched on with a real shipment from China
the Pro plan and what happens above 300 orders
product recommendations and reorder links on the tracking page

The checkout of Core was viewed without an address and nothing was paid. Account and start: the account on the Free plan was created by us, who was signed in; our AI assistant ran the test in its own Chrome tab of our browser, starting at 13:44. The interface was already in English; only the Locale in Profile settings (date and decimal format) said Dutch and was changed to English (United States), which showed Settings updated. The dashboard said Subscription: Free, 1,000 credits / month, usage resets on Dec 16, 2026. The dossier name is Make and the review is on OSM (make-review). Core action: a scenario with a Custom webhook, a Data store module (Add/replace a record) and a Router with two branches (Leads with the filter type = lead, Invoices with type = invoice), each ending in a Tools Set variable module. It took about 6 minutes and about 25 clicks to the first result. The data store Test Inbox was made with the structure Name, Email and Type, generated from a JSON example; the storage size is fixed at 1 MB on Free, and after 5 records it showed 567.0 B / 1.0 MB. The dialog was cancelled. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Easy-Peasy.AI in our existing free account: a Medium blog post about a made-up product came out at 1,772 words in about 30 seconds, left out the 12-hour battery fact from the prompt and added features that were not in it, and then the free word allowance was closed. Only these two tools were tried, and no plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing Easy-Peasy.AI our account, on the Free plan, with the interface already in English. No sign-up was done in this test. The test started at 08:53 on the dashboard, which showed Free and 3 credits left (also at the bottom of the left menu). The dossier name is Easy-Peasy.AI and the review page is on AIBM (b2b/easy-peasy-ai-review); the folder of the notes is easy-peasy and the review slug is easy-peasy-ai, so they differ. Core action, text: Home, All Tools, Instant Blog Post Generator (a guessed direct address gave a 404 page). Input: the topic Lumio X2, a made-up solar desk lamp with wireless charging and a 12-hour battery, 3 keywords, length Medium, language English, no tone of voice. Steps: 5 (open the tool, topic, keywords, length, Try Free). The first text appeared after about 10 seconds and the post was done after about 30 seconds (clock 08:54). The result was about 1,870 words by the tester count and 1,772 words in History, for a length that was set to Medium; at the bottom it said Generated with the free Standard model. and offered Regenerate with Advanced AI. The sidebar stayed at 3 credits left. Quality of the text, read critically: the stated fact of a 12-hour battery appears nowhere in the post (it says endless hours of light and hours of uninterrupted lighting). The post adds features that the prompt did not contain: adjustable brightness, color temperature modes, touch-sensitive controls, recyclable components, works even in low-light conditions and smart charge management. It contradicts itself with zero reliance on electricity next to a lamp that has a battery and a wireless charger. It leans on stock marketing phrases such as a Swiss Army knife of desk lamps and a beacon of innovation, it is long and repeats itself, and the comparison table against Traditional Desk Lamps is filled with assumptions such as Limited Settings and No Additional Features. Word limit: a click on Regenerate with Advanced AI gave at once Your plan has reached its word limit. To continue, please upgrade your plan., and a second Try Free gave the same notice. The free allowance of 1,000 words was therefore closed only after the first generation, which had produced 1,772 words; the check seems to happen before a run and not during it. The euro prices match the dossier; the checker page shows dollars and says the trial renews automatically to the monthly Premium plan, and the dossier misses AI Visibility Tracking (Beta) and the daily tool limit. No plan was bought and no account was made. Account and start: NO account was made and none was used. The first scan was started at 10:23:58 and the result was there at the next look 5 seconds later, so a scan, including the screenshot of the page, took under 10 seconds. sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested EmailOctopus in our new free account (called Starter in the app): an inline sign-up form was ready in about 5 minutes and still shows Powered by EmailOctopus, a second form was refused (Your Starter plan is limited to one form), a campaign on the Announce template was made and previewed with nothing sent, and a welcome automation was made as a draft and not started, with no limit seen on Starter. Saving a campaign needed at least one contact, and a DMARC warning said that without a verified domain EmailOctopus sends from an address of its own. The Pro price matches the dossier ($9 a month billed yearly, $18 at 2,500 subscribers with 25,000 emails); the 10,000 emails apply only at 500 subscribers, and the Starter limits of the dossier are not visible in the app. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used a new EmailOctopus our account on the free plan, already signed in, with the interface in English. The free plan is called Starter in the app. The test started at about 11:20; the dashboard opened at once with no login step and no bot check, with the welcome line Welcome aboard! Start by adding your contacts. Setup and branding had been done before the test and nothing about an address or a person was filled in during it. The account has one single audience (Contacts, 0 subscribed contacts); the menu has Contacts, Grow, Campaigns, Automations, Reports and Brand, and no separate lists. Core action 1, a sign-up form: Grow, Forms, Create a form. The styles are Inline, Pop-up, Hello bar and Slide-in, with five templates. An inline form on one template was chosen, renamed Test form, with the title Join the Garden Notes list and one line of text. Editing inline worked at once and the form was ready in about 5 minutes (11:25 to 11:30). The preview (Desktop and Mobile) shows Powered by EmailOctopus. The settings show the success message Thanks for subscribing!, an optional consent box and a hidden Google reCAPTCHA that is on by default. A second form was refused: Upgrade to add more forms, Your Starter plan is limited to one form. Core action 2, a campaign (nothing was sent): Campaigns first asks to add contacts. The setup did not go on without a contact (None of your subscribed contacts match this selection, and saving fell back to Untitled), so one placeholder contact on example.com was added (accepted, status Subscribed, no email went to it). Sender Test Co, subject Three herbs for your balcony. Saving showed Warning: verify your domain: because of a DMARC policy on the domain, mail from that address is unlikely to be delivered, so EmailOctopus would send from an address of its own sending domain instead; the choice was Continue, not Verify domain, and no domain was linked. The design step offers Branded templates (Announce, Birthday, Explore, Share, Update, Welcome), Inspirational, Start from scratch (Drag and drop or Code your own) and Past emails; Announce was chosen and takes the brand logo over. exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Zapier under the automatic 14 day Professional trial, which needs no card: a form feeding a table through a Zap went live a little over 5 minutes after the start, ran 5 times without a failure and used 0 tasks, but the table records stayed empty because the whole submission was mapped to one column, and the Copilot only titled the form without adding its fields. The plan page shows euros: Professional €18,62 a month billed annually or €27,93 billed monthly; the public page in US dollars gives $19.99 and $29.99, so the $19.99 in our dossier is the yearly price. The checkout was opened and nothing was paid. Account and start: the account was created by us, who was signed in; our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab of our Chrome, starting at 14:07. The interface was already on English. The profile page said that the current account address needed to be confirmed; the account worked anyway. Onboarding: the role Business Owner (the list had no Founder or Owner), the team size 1-49 (the smallest option; Just me does not exist) and Skip question for the apps. Right after that the home page said 14 TRIAL DAYS LEFT, Plan tasks 0 / 1.000 and Zapier Pro trial ends Dec 2: an automatic Professional trial of 14 days started without a card, while the plan page still calls the account Current plan: Free. Everything that was built therefore ran under the trial and does not prove what Free allows. The dossier name is Zapier and the review is on OSM (zapier-review). The pain that was tested: telling one app when something happens in another, without paying for it. No external app was connected, only the built-in apps Forms and Tables. Core action: a form was built with Home, Form, Blank form. The Copilot said Done! Your form is now titled Test Handoff with three required fields but only set the title; the fields name, email and type had to be added by hand (Add field, a label, Insert field), about 12 clicks and a few failed tries, because the label was only kept after Insert field. The Zap: Automate form, Build your own automation opened a new browser tab with the Zap editor: step 1 Zapier Forms, Form Submission Created, step 2 Zapier Tables, Create Record. Create Table inside the step made a table with a generic name and one column Text Field, so the columns name, email and type do not exist; Form Submission Values was mapped to Text Field. The trigger test found a sample Form Submission A; the test of the Tables step was skipped. Publish said Success! Your Zap is live! (version v1). Time: the Zap went live at 14:12:16 and the first run was at 14:12:29, a little over 5 minutes after the start at 14:07, including the onboarding, the form and the Zap. Five test submissions were sent through the public form page (made up names Test Lead 1 to 5, made up addresses on example.com, type trial), each answered Form submitted!. Zap history showed 5 runs, all Successful, between 14:12:29 and 14:12:49. The run details said Found 1 new Form Submission in Zapier Forms and Sent 1 new Record to Zapier Tables, but the record in the data out had only empty f1 and f2: the column Text Field stayed empty because the whole Form Submission Values block was mapped to one column. So the handoff ran and the data did not arrive in the table. Whether separate fields work with extra columns was not tried. Tasks: Zap history showed a dash for the tasks of each run, Plan tasks stayed 0 / 1.000 after 5 runs, also on Billing & usage, and the tab Task usage said No results found. That is 0 tasks a run for Forms plus Tables; the built-in apps do not seem to count as a task, which is our reading of the counter and was not checked in the help text. Nothing in this Zap needed a paid plan. The plan page lists Multi-step Zaps, Unlimited Premium apps, Webhooks, AI fields and Conditional form logic under Professional. Webhooks by Zapier (Catch Hook) was not tested because Forms worked. The form page showed Free next to the Forms name with View plans and Upgrade, but Forms worked under the trial without a prompt. A second tab of the Zap editor gave a warning about overriding current edits (UpdateBlocked). Plans: The plans were read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 on the plan page in the app (euros, because the app detected the Netherlands) and the public page zapier.com/pricing was read again just before this delivery the same day with the currency set to USD. In euros: Free €0 with 100 tasks /mo; Professional €18,62 /mo billed annually (€27,93 struck through) or €27,93 /mo billed monthly at 750 tasks /mo; Team €64,26 billed annually or €96,40 billed monthly at 2,000 tasks /mo and 25 users; Enterprise on request; Save 33% for annual billing. In US dollars on the public page: Professional $19.99 a month with yearly billing and $29.99 with monthly billing, Team $69 with yearly billing and $103.50 with monthly billing. So the $19.99 in the dossier is the yearly price; the page does not say which billing period the starting price assumes unless the switch is used. Free lists unlimited Zaps, Tables and Forms, two-step Zaps and Copilot with a daily limit; Professional adds multi-step Zaps, unlimited premium apps, webhooks, AI fields and conditional form logic. Checkout: on the plan page Checkout was opened for Professional with 750 tasks. Monthly: Total due today €27,93 and Next monthly charge on december 18, 2026 €27,93 /mo. Annual: Total due today €223,41 and Next annual charge on november 18, 2027; Save 33% and Save €111,76 per year with annual billing. Pay-per-task billing: if it is enabled and the included tasks are exceeded, the checkout says €0,0931 per additional task plus applicable taxes on monthly billing and €0,0311 on annual billing; it can be switched off, and then the Zaps are paused. The checkout showed no separate tax amount: Total due today equalled the plan sum, and plus applicable taxes is only named at the pay-per-task line; the tax probably appears after an address and tax number are added, which was not done. The payment screen offered Card (number, date, CVC, Full name, Country or region Netherlands, Address) and Paypal. Nothing was filled in and nothing was paid. The line Please add a payment method to edit your trial settings. shows that the trial settings need a payment method, although the trial itself started without one. Cancelling: a paid plan can be left through Settings, Billing & usage, Compare plans or Upgrade; this was not tested because there was no paid plan. The trial ends by itself on 2 Dec 2026 without a card. Deleting the account is Settings, Security and data, Delete my account (and Delete my data, which keeps the account); neither was clicked. Not tested: a Zap of more than two steps, Webhooks by Zapier, premium apps, AI steps and their task price, what Free allows after the trial (100 tasks, two-step Zaps), a connection with an outside app, the payment, the tax rule, and cancelling or downgrading a paid plan. Clean up: the Zap is switched OFF (version v1 stays published); the form Test Handoff stays reachable on its public page, the generated table with 5 empty records, the Zap with its 5 runs and the Professional trial until 2 Dec 2026 stay; no card, no payment, no outside apps. Two tabs that the Zapier editor opened by itself fell outside our tab group and could not be closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The plan page calls the account Free while the trial gives the paid features, so a first Zap proves little about the Free plan. The Copilot only titled the form and left the fields to you, and the table that the Zap creates has one generic column, so map the fields one by one. The starting prices depend on yearly billing: monthly billing costs a third more. Pay-per-task billing can charge for tasks above the included number unless you switch it off, and then the Zaps pause. Editing the trial settings needs a payment method.

sessions.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session tested two zastech tools without an account. The free Invoice Maker made a two line invoice of $938.00 in about 2 minutes, with a live preview, local drafts and a small footer Created with zastech.dev that stays in print unless you pay $9. The PDF Redactor & Sanitizer showed the metadata of a made up test PDF and let us draw black boxes by hand (no automatic detection; the first try failed and one box was a few pixels off), with 3 free outputs counted on the server of zastech. The sanitized PDF was not downloaded, so the removal of the text was not verified. Nothing was bought.
findings: Text we checked: "No account required". What we saw: Both the Invoice Maker and the PDF Redactor ran in the browser without signing in; no e-mail address, phone number, password or card was asked at any point of the test.

Text we checked: "Professional documents with a small zastech footer". What we saw: The free invoice shows Created with zastech.dev, free invoice maker at the bottom in small light grey text, and the print style sheet always shows this block in print. Removing it costs $9 once (Remove branding $9).

Text we checked: "Subtotal $938.00". What we saw: Two made up lines (2 x $349.00 and 2 x $120.00) gave $698.00 and $240.00 and the preview showed Subtotal $938.00 and Total $938.00, the right sum, about 2 minutes after the page was opened. The fields were filled by a script, so typing by hand takes a little longer.

Text we checked: "Drag across the preview to create a black redaction. Click an existing black box to remove it". What we saw: Redaction is manual with no detection of e-mail addresses or phone numbers. The first try failed because the page moved about 100 pixels during the drag; after Clear page redactions the second try made 2 boxes, but the box over the phone number started a few pixels too far right and the first letter of the word phone stuck out.

Text we checked: "3 free results on every tool, then a lifetime license". What we saw: The PDF Redactor showed Free outputs available and 3 free outputs left with no signup, and a paid license unlocks unlimited exports on up to 3 browser activations, as on the pricing page.

The PDF Redactor & Sanitizer showed the metadata of a made up test PDF and let us draw black boxes by hand (no automatic detection; the first try failed and one box was a few pixels off), with 3 free outputs counted on the server of zastech. The sanitized PDF was not downloaded, so the removal of the text was not verified. Nothing was bought. Account and start: NO account was made and none was used. The tools of zastech run in the browser without signing in; our AI assistant ran the test in our own tab of our browser, starting at 13:15. Nothing was installed and no e-mail address, phone number, password or card was typed in anywhere. The dossier name is zastech and the review is on OSM (zastech-review). Core action 1, Invoice Maker (zastech.dev/tools/invoice-maker): the page says you can create and save a professional invoice without an account, with unlimited free exports and no signup, and shows the cards No account required, A4 PDF unlimited free and Drafts stay on this device. It was filled with made up data: seller Example Snowboards Ltd, buyer Sample Store Inc., currency USD (the default) and two lines, Freestyle snowboard 2 x $349.00 = $698.00 and Snowboard bindings 2 x $120.00 = $240.00. The live preview showed Subtotal $938.00 and Total $938.00, which is the right sum. A usable invoice was on screen about 2 minutes after the page was opened, with one form and two lines; the fields were filled by a script and not typed, so typing by hand takes a little longer. The preview updates while you type, without a generate button. Footer: the free invoice carries the line Created with zastech.dev, free invoice maker, small and light grey at the bottom, and the print style sheet of the page always shows this block in print. The buttons are New, Save, History, Remove branding $9, License / Activate and Print / Save PDF. Saving is local (Draft saved locally, Private, saved only on this device). Document type (Invoice or Estimate / Quote) and Upload logo (PNG, JPG or WebP, at most 150 KB) are free. The print preview and the PDF export itself were NOT opened: the print dialog of Chrome cannot be operated by the browser tool and nothing was to be saved on our laptop. The print style sheet was read: it hides the header, the editor and the buttons and leaves only the invoice. Core action 2, PDF Redactor & Sanitizer (zastech.dev/tools/pdf-redactor-sanitizer): the cards say Flattened into page pixels, Original metadata not copied and PDF stays in this browser. A made up test invoice of 2 KB and 2 pages was uploaded with the file picker; it holds a made up buyer line with a contact e-mail address and a phone number. The inspection panel showed Pages 2, Metadata fields 7, Attachments 0 and JavaScript actions 0, plus the original metadata (title, author, creator, producer, creation date and more). Redaction is MANUAL: you drag across the preview to create a black box and click a box to remove it. There is no automatic detection of e-mail addresses or phone numbers. The first try failed (the page moved about 100 pixels during the drag and the boxes landed above the line); Clear page redactions said Page redactions cleared. The second try made 2 boxes and the counter said 2 redactions. The box over the phone number starts a few pixels too far right, so the first letter of the word phone sticks out. In the preview the boxes are half transparent and the text shows through; the site says the export is flattened into pixels. Download sanitized PDF was NOT clicked, because it would save a file on our laptop and use one free result. So whether the text is really gone from the output was not verified. Free results: the Trial / License window said Free outputs available and 3 free outputs left, no signup needed; the small print says 3 free sanitized exports need no signup, free outputs are counted on the server of zastech, and a paid license unlocks unlimited sanitized exports on up to 3 browser activations. So the counter lives on the server, next to the claim that the PDF stays in the browser; the network traffic was not inspected. Plans: The pricing page zastech.dev/pricing was read on 18 Nov 2026 by the tester and read again just before this delivery the same day, with the same prices: Free forever, $0 always, with a small zastech footer, for Invoice Maker, Proposal Builder and Client Report Builder; white-label, once, Invoice Maker $9, Proposal Builder $15 and Client Report Builder $19; the other browser tools give 3 free results and then cost $15 to $29 once (PDF Redactor & Sanitizer $19), no subscription or renewal, up to three browsers per license; API packs $15 or $19 prepaid; Freelancer Kit $39 once (Invoice Maker, Proposal Builder, Contract Workspace and Client Report Builder; team of 10 $149, team of 25 $299), Finance Ops Kit $79 once and Starter Kit $99. Prices are in USD and any sales tax or VAT is shown at checkout by Lemon Squeezy before you pay. The dossier matches the pricing page; the PDF Redactor at $19 falls within its range of $15 to $29. Clean up: there is no account and no file was saved on the laptop (no download). The invoice draft sits only in the local browser storage of the test tab (Draft saved locally). All our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The free invoice carries a small zastech footer that the print style sheet always shows, so a clean invoice costs $9 once. The boxes look half transparent in the preview, and we could not check that the downloaded file is clean. The app opened without an account, password, demo or call. In the app it is called BSure Checkout Rules. A banner says: You are on free Development plan. Test all features for free. Core action, the rule Hide shipping methods: about 1.5 minutes after the install (13:05 to 13:06:30) and 9 steps: Create rule, Hide shipping methods, Select rule, a name, Add shipping method, the word Standard typed (Contains) and Save. The list then shows Checkout rules 1 Active with the row Hide Standard shipping for all orders, Status Active, Type Shipping, Subtype Hide and Activated on November 17, 2026. No Shopify Plus and no paid plan was needed on the development store. Our first name for the rule did not fit the condition Always and was changed before saving. The onboarding card stayed at 0 of 2 tasks complete even after an active rule was saved, because it asks for the status Testing. All paid plans say FREE TRIAL FOR FIRST 5 DAYS, and a switch Monthly or Annual carries Get 2 months free. The app names one extra cart rule on each paid plan, which the App Store listing does not. Checkout: the Select plan button of Premium was greyed out, and a click on Select plan for Starter did nothing: no Shopify Approve subscription screen came up, so nothing was approved and no card was asked. The app does not say why; probably it is blocked on a development store. Cancelling: no paid plan or trial existed, so there was nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall BSure Checkout Rules? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. Not tested: the rule in a real checkout, a PO box rule, hiding or reordering payment methods, validation rules, discount rules, the cart rule, the paid plans, the trial, the annual prices, the asterisk at Premium and whether a rule works within 1 minute. Clean up: the app was uninstalled; no theme change was made. Other apps were not touched. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

After looking at the preview, one click on Generate All 5 PDFs (.ZIP) Free produced the batch in about 6 seconds (not timed precisely) and the counter went from 25 to 20 of 25 left this month. The bottom of the certificate has a small line Made with BulkCertPDF. At the end a box asks for an email address for templates and a monthly newsletter; it was not filled in. sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested ShopTrueProfit as a web tool in the session that we were already signed in to, using only the built-in sample data of a fictional Etsy shop: one click gave a profit dashboard (net profit $506.61 on net sales of $2,171.00) in about a minute. The prices match the dossier. No own CSV files were uploaded, so how the tool reads real exports, Cloud Sync, export, checkout and the claim that files are never uploaded were not tested. Account and start: ShopTrueProfit is not a Shopify app but a web tool without an install, where Etsy, eBay and Amazon CSV files are dropped in. We were already signed in (the top bar showed an account mail address, which is covered in the pictures); no account was made in this test, no Shopify route exists and no store was used. The test started at 08:58 in our own tab on the home page. The page title says Etsy, eBay & Amazon profit in 60 seconds. The home page says Files never uploaded and No store login, and has the buttons Choose CSV files and Try with sample data. Core action: no own Etsy CSV files were uploaded, because no real shop data was available and the file format could not be made up without real exports. One click on Try with sample data gave the dashboard within a few seconds, about 1 minute and 1 click to the first result. It is labelled SAMPLE DATA (fictional shop) not saved. Overview: Net sales $2,171.00 (40 orders, 58 items), Etsy fees $850.19 (39.2% of sales), Product costs $814.20 (all orders costed) and Net profit $506.61 (margin 23.3%). Ads ROI: Etsy Ads spend $146.20, Offsite Ads fees $50.10, Sales per $1 of ads $11.06. The fees tab splits the fees into Shipping labels $420.10, Etsy Ads $146.20, Transaction fees (6.5%) $141.17, Payment processing $79.62, Offsite Ads $50.10 and Listing fees $13.00, which add up to the $850.19. The sample numbers are internally consistent (net sales minus fees minus product costs gives the net profit), but they say nothing about how the tool reads real exports, because only the built-in data was used. Product costs: the tab says per unit: materials + packaging + POD and Type a cost and press Enter. Saved in this browser (and in your account if Cloud Sync is on). The demo came with costs already filled in ($26.25, $6, $11, $8.75 on the first four listings); nothing was changed. The tabs are Overview, Orders, Listings, Fees and Product costs. Plans, read up to the payment step: Free $0 (Full sample-data demo, Your latest month, Etsy, eBay & Amazon fee calculators, Files stay in your browser), Monthly $7 /month (Everything in Free, full history, date ranges, comparison with the previous period, profit per order, product and month plus ads return on spend, Cloud sync and backup for Etsy data, CSV exports, Cancel anytime) and Lifetime $59 one time with $99 crossed out, Founding member price and Discount applied at checkout. The page says that payments, receipts and sales tax are handled by Lemon Squeezy and that you get a license key by email after buying. The prices match the dossier (Free $0, Monthly $7, Lifetime $59 with $99 crossed out); there is no deviation. The account menu shows Activate Pro and the window says No synced Pro history yet for this email; no key was entered. Checkout: NOT reached. The buttons Get Monthly and Get Lifetime were not clicked, so no tax, total, license key mail or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: not tested because nothing was bought; the site says Cancel anytime and a window points to the Lemon Squeezy receipt email for it; the account was not deleted. Not tested: own Etsy, eBay or Amazon CSV files, the eBay and Amazon beta, Cloud Sync, CSV export, the checkout and Lemon Squeezy, and whether the promise Files never uploaded is true (the network traffic was not measured). So the claims about local processing, cloud sync and exports are not tested here. Clean up: nothing was installed, no test products were made, nothing was bought; the tab was closed. The sample data is not saved by the tool.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 31 October 2026 on the 14-day trial that starts with a new account, without a card: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We answered the onboarding questions, imported a two-row CSV of made-up contacts, and tried to export them again. We connected no mailbox, calendar or phone, sent nothing, invited nobody and paid nothing. The session took about ten minutes.
findings: After sign-up Cloze asked four onboarding questions (industry setup, what to call people, what to call deals, and whether to track an active stage). We chose sales and services and left the defaults. The next screen said it was analysing our history and would email us when done, 'a few minutes to a few hours', although no mailbox was connected. The mailbox dialog offered Google, Microsoft 365, Exchange, iCloud, Yahoo and other email, and we connected none.

Settings showed the trial ending on 16 November 2026, which is 16 days after our account date of 31 October. Cloze's help page promises 14 days without a card. We were not asked for a card in the steps we recorded, but we did not count every sign-up screen, and we cannot say every account gets 16 days.

The CSV importer read the two rows and the sample values correctly, including accents and a line break inside a note, but detected no columns on its own, not even the email column. The 'Add person' field list runs to dozens of fields, and custom fields could only be mapped onto fields that already exist in the account. We mapped four columns by hand (display name, note, email, tags) and left the rest unmapped.

The import offered a dry run and a plain import; we ran the import and got 'Imported 2 of 2 records successfully', with the option to download our mapping. The two contacts did not show in the list until we searched for 'TEST', although the counter had already moved.

The email address and the multi-line note arrived intact. Our tag 'aibm-test|alpha' became one tag, '#aibm-test-alpha': the pipe turned into a hyphen and the tag was not split in two. That matters if you keep several tags in one spreadsheet column.

Settings > Import / Export offers CSV or Excel for people, companies and deals. The Dutch interface translated 'Excel' as 'uitmunten' (the verb 'to excel'). We pressed 'Export now' twice, at 21:21 and 21:24. Both times a loading spinner ran for about 30 seconds with no download, no message and no file, and the network log showed no export request. We do not know whether the file would have come by email later, so we do not call this a failed export. The export window points to support@cloze.com for help.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 13 November 2026 we tested the Seonix free plan (onboarding, site scan, issues, keywords). On 14 November 2026 we tested Starter, which the vendor set to free for us until 12 January 2027, so no card was needed: integrations, the planner, one AI article and the billing page. Nothing was connected or published.
findings: Free plan: the site scan took under 10 seconds and gave a health score of 95 with 8 active issues. It checked 100 of our 285 sitemap pages. Generate Content said AI is not available on the Free plan.

Starter: the first two clicks on Generate Content did nothing on screen (the network call returned 409, with no message). The third attempt started at about 08:09:50 and the draft was ready at 08:16:52, about 7 minutes, against the 30 to 60 seconds shown on screen.

The draft, Apollo Pricing Explained for Small Sales Teams, has 2,076 words, 13 subheadings, key takeaways and an FAQ, and scored SEO 90, Readability 87 and AI answers 86 (Excellent). For a site without a CMS the only publishing route is the REST API option, which needs your own endpoint: a POST for create and update keyed on external_id, and a GET that lists the articles on the site. The calendar said auto-plan, drag and drop and slot scheduling work only once a channel is connected; auto-publish was off.
The Title Too Long issue lists 7 of our review pages and says Seonix will fix this itself. With no channel connected, nothing was fixed. Whether a connected channel fixes them was not tested.

Billing showed Starter at $49 a month, Active, renewing on 12 January 2027, with a Cancel subscription button and Save 20% for yearly billing. We saw no charge because the vendor set the plan to free. Tax and the final total are unknown because no checkout was opened.
Without our asking, Seonix had already planned 12 articles for 15 to 26 November and written a draft that reused facts from our own site.

findings: Setup: no AIOSEO account or licence key is needed for Lite. The last wizard step said you are using AIOSEO Lite and no licence is needed.

Extra installs: step 3 of the wizard had Broken Link Checker, MonsterInsights, OptinMonster and Universally ticked by default, plus the Pro addons Image SEO and Author SEO. We unticked each one, and afterwards only AIOSEO was installed.

Data sharing: step 4 had email reports set to Yes, and step 5 filled in the site admin email to connect the site to the AIOSEO SEO API with usage sharing switched on. We turned reports off and skipped step 5.

Titles and descriptions: the AIOSEO panel under the post editor updated its search preview as we typed. After saving, the page head carried our title, our meta description, a canonical link and matching Open Graph and Twitter titles.
Schema: without any setting from us, the post page carried BlogPosting, BreadcrumbList, Organization, Person, WebPage and WebSite markup.
Free and Pro: Search Console statistics, Link Assistant, Local SEO, Index Now and video and news sitemaps were marked Pro in the wizard. The general XML sitemap was switched on by default in Lite.

Checkout: on 22 November 2026, shown in euros from the Netherlands, Basic was €49.50 for the first year for one site (normally €99). The checkout added 21% VAT for a total of €59.90 and asked for an email, name and password for a new AIOSEO account. AIOSEO's terms say discount codes apply to the first term only. We did not pay.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested MailVeri in the account that we made: a CSV of 20 made-up addresses showed 16 unique emails and 4 skipped rows, was verified in 19 seconds in 3 clicks for 16 credits (1,000 to 984, taken at once and not given back after the list was deleted) and came back as 13 invalid and 3 disposable, with a CSV export that worked. Every test address was bad on purpose, so missed good addresses, role detection and the accuracy claim were not measured. The app limit is 100,000 emails per list against 1 million rows in the dossier. The pack prices match the dossier and no pack was bought. Account and start: we made the MailVeri account before the test. The test started at 07:44 in our own browser tab on the dashboard of the app (interface already in English, no language setting found). The dashboard showed CREDITS: 1,000, 1,000 lifetime, the Free Plan, TOTAL VERIFIED 0 and no mail lists. The dossier names three audiences (marketers cleaning a one-off big list, developers checking sign-ups in code and teams that want proof of accuracy) and no alternatives. Core action, list verification: a test file adressen.csv with 20 made-up addresses was prepared on purpose: four with a syntax error, two on a domain that does not exist, three on burner domains (mailinator, guerrillamail and 10minutemail), role addresses (info, sales, contact, admin, noreply and a help address) on example domains and six made-up personal names at four large free mail providers. It was uploaded on Upload Files, which says Maximum emails per list: 100,000 and Maximum file size is 10 MB. After the upload the page said 16 unique emails and 4 rows without a valid email were skipped, so the four syntax errors were filtered in the browser and were not processed or charged. Verify was clicked at 07:44: the credit counter went from 1,000 to 984 at once (PENDING: 16), the page showed 1 mails/s and the list was Completed after 00:19s, about 07:45. That is 3 clicks from the file to the result. The result was 0% Deliverable: Deliverable 0, Risky 0, Undeliverable 16 (100%) and Unknown 0. The detail window split it into INVALID 13 (Non-existent address) and DISPOSABLE 3 (Temporary burner address); VALID, ROLE_ACCOUNT, CATCH_ALL, FULL_INBOX and UNKNOWN were 0. Per address (the All Results export with the column MailVeri Status): the two made-up domains were INVALID, the three burner domains DISPOSABLE, the role addresses on example domains INVALID and not ROLE_ACCOUNT, and all made-up names at the big free mail providers INVALID. Honest reading: every test address was bad on purpose, so the test did not measure whether the tool misses good addresses, and no address came back valid, role account, catch-all, full inbox or unknown, so those five categories were not exercised. The role addresses are INVALID because example domains have no mail server, so the role detection itself is not proven. Export: Download Results offers the presets Deliverable Only (Recommended), Deliverable + Risky, All Results and Custom Selection, the category boxes and the output columns Original File + Status Column, Email + Status and Email Only; there is also a Download ZIP with one file per category. The All Results export to a CSV file (553 bytes) worked and was kept as a result file. Credits after the test: 984 (16 used, one per verified address). The credits were taken when Verify was clicked, and after the list was deleted they were not given back. Plans, read up to the checkout button: the Buy Credits page has nine one-off packs, $9 for 10,000 credits, $19 for 25,000, $39 for 60,000 (50,000 shown struck through, plus 20%, Best Seller), $59 for 100,000, $119 for 250,000, $199 for 500,000, $299 for 1,000,000, $599 for 2,500,000 and $999 for 5,000,000, with 1 credit = 1 email verification and Credits never expire. There is no monthly subscription. The Summary showed the $39 pack with a Total of $39.00 and a promo code field that was left empty; Checkout was not clicked. An offer of +1,000 free credits per honest post on LinkedIn, X or Quora was not used. All prices match the dossier. Differences with the dossier: the dossier says file upload of up to 1 million rows, while the app says Maximum emails per list: 100,000, so the dossier figure is ten times too high. The 7-status report matches the app (VALID, ROLE_ACCOUNT, CATCH_ALL, FULL_INBOX, INVALID, DISPOSABLE and UNKNOWN). The upload types CSV, XLSX and TXT of the dossier match the app, which also names XLS. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, Checkout was not clicked, no promo code was entered and no card, total with tax or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: there is no subscription, so nothing to cancel; the test list was deleted through Delete List in the row menu after the confirmation Are you sure you want to delete this list? and the page then said No email lists found. Lists are Automatically deleted after 30 days. An account deletion was not looked for and the account stays. Not tested: the REST API, MCP, webhooks and API keys (the audience of developers), Single Mail, big lists, real good mailboxes, catch-all, role and full-inbox detection, the accuracy claim of 99% or more, and payment or refund. Clean up: the test list was deleted, the account stays on the Free Plan with 984 credits, the downloaded result file was moved to the notes folder and our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested MailVeri in the account that we made: a CSV of 20 made-up addresses showed 16 unique emails and 4 skipped rows, was verified in 19 seconds in 3 clicks for 16 credits (1,000 to 984, taken at once and not given back after the list was deleted) and came back as 13 invalid and 3 disposable, with a CSV export that worked. Every test address was bad on purpose, so missed good addresses, role detection and the accuracy claim were not measured. The app limit is 100,000 emails per list against 1 million rows in the dossier. The pack prices match the dossier and no pack was bought. Account and start: we made the MailVeri account before the test. The test started at 07:44 in our own browser tab on the dashboard of the app (interface already in English, no language setting found). The dashboard showed CREDITS: 1,000, 1,000 lifetime, the Free Plan, TOTAL VERIFIED 0 and no mail lists. The dossier names three audiences (marketers cleaning a one-off big list, developers checking sign-ups in code and teams that want proof of accuracy) and no alternatives. Core action, list verification: a test file adressen.csv with 20 made-up addresses was prepared on purpose: four with a syntax error, two on a domain that does not exist, three on burner domains (mailinator, guerrillamail and 10minutemail), role addresses (info, sales, contact, admin, noreply and a help address) on example domains and six made-up personal names at four large free mail providers. It was uploaded on Upload Files, which says Maximum emails per list: 100,000 and Maximum file size is 10 MB. After the upload the page said 16 unique emails and 4 rows without a valid email were skipped, so the four syntax errors were filtered in the browser and were not processed or charged. Verify was clicked at 07:44: the credit counter went from 1,000 to 984 at once (PENDING: 16), the page showed 1 mails/s and the list was Completed after 00:19s, about 07:45. That is 3 clicks from the file to the result. The result was 0% Deliverable: Deliverable 0, Risky 0, Undeliverable 16 (100%) and Unknown 0. The detail window split it into INVALID 13 (Non-existent address) and DISPOSABLE 3 (Temporary burner address); VALID, ROLE_ACCOUNT, CATCH_ALL, FULL_INBOX and UNKNOWN were 0. Per address (the All Results export with the column MailVeri Status): the two made-up domains were INVALID, the three burner domains DISPOSABLE, the role addresses on example domains INVALID and not ROLE_ACCOUNT, and all made-up names at the big free mail providers INVALID. Honest reading: every test address was bad on purpose, so the test did not measure whether the tool misses good addresses, and no address came back valid, role account, catch-all, full inbox or unknown, so those five categories were not exercised. The role addresses are INVALID because example domains have no mail server, so the role detection itself is not proven. Export: Download Results offers the presets Deliverable Only (Recommended), Deliverable + Risky, All Results and Custom Selection, the category boxes and the output columns Original File + Status Column, Email + Status and Email Only; there is also a Download ZIP with one file per category. The All Results export to a CSV file (553 bytes) worked and was kept as a result file. Credits after the test: 984 (16 used, one per verified address). The credits were taken when Verify was clicked, and after the list was deleted they were not given back. Plans, read up to the checkout button: the Buy Credits page has nine one-off packs, $9 for 10,000 credits, $19 for 25,000, $39 for 60,000 (50,000 shown struck through, plus 20%, Best Seller), $59 for 100,000, $119 for 250,000, $199 for 500,000, $299 for 1,000,000, $599 for 2,500,000 and $999 for 5,000,000, with 1 credit = 1 email verification and Credits never expire. There is no monthly subscription. The Summary showed the $39 pack with a Total of $39.00 and a promo code field that was left empty; Checkout was not clicked. An offer of +1,000 free credits per honest post on LinkedIn, X or Quora was not used. All prices match the dossier. Differences with the dossier: the dossier says file upload of up to 1 million rows, while the app says Maximum emails per list: 100,000, so the dossier figure is ten times too high. The 7-status report matches the app (VALID, ROLE_ACCOUNT, CATCH_ALL, FULL_INBOX, INVALID, DISPOSABLE and UNKNOWN). The upload types CSV, XLSX and TXT of the dossier match the app, which also names XLS. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, Checkout was not clicked, no promo code was entered and no card, total with tax or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: there is no subscription, so nothing to cancel; the test list was deleted through Delete List in the row menu after the confirmation Are you sure you want to delete this list? and the page then said No email lists found. Lists are Automatically deleted after 30 days. An account deletion was not looked for and the account stays. Not tested: the REST API, MCP, webhooks and API keys (the audience of developers), Single Mail, big lists, real good mailboxes, catch-all, role and full-inbox detection, the accuracy claim of 99% or more, and payment or refund. Clean up: the test list was deleted, the account stays on the Free Plan with 984 credits, the downloaded result file was moved to the notes folder and our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The dossier says up to 1 million rows, but the app limit is 100,000 emails per list. The credits are taken when Verify is clicked and are not given back after the list is deleted. Rows with a syntax error are dropped in the browser before the count, so they are not shown in the result. Role addresses on a domain without a mail server come back as invalid, so the role status was not seen.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested AddressHero on a Shopify development store: the install, the Format Validation switch in the onboarding, the Format Validation page with its in-app example, the tab In Checkout Validation that needs Shopify Plus, the plan choice with Minimal and Pro, the Shopify Approve subscription screen for Minimal with a test charge that was approved without a card, and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. No real checkout was seen blocking an address. Install: the App Store listing (English) says Free to install. Free trial available. and lists three plans: Pay per Address (14 days free, then US and CA $0.01, DACH $0.02, UK $0.04, other $0.03 per address), Pay per Order ($0.04 per order, 14 days free) and Minimal ($9.99 / month). The dossier only knows Lite at $9.99 and Pro at $0.04 per order, so the listing has one extra plan. The install form was sent at about 13:11; the first Install click opened a new tab outside our own tab group, and the second attempt showed the Install app dialog asking for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, which was approved. The app stood in Settings, Apps at once and opened without an account, password, demo or call. Core action, Format Validation: the onboarding step Detect address issues in checkout opened by itself; the switch Format Validation was turned on and the toast said Saved successfully. That took 3 clicks (Start onboarding, the switch, Next) and about 2 minutes after the install (about 13:13). The step Fix address issues after checkout (Add AddressHero to your thank you page) was skipped. The page Format Validation then shows Active with the points No orders without a house number, Blocks special characters carriers can't print and Customer fixes it before paying, the settings Missing House Number and Special Characters are on, and there is a tab Packing stations / PO Boxes. An example in the app shows the address 5th Ave with the error Please add your house number to continue. and a greyed out Pay now button. This is an example inside the app: no real checkout was seen blocking an address, because the store has a password and no test order was placed. Tabs on the free setup: the tab In Checkout Validation says In-Checkout Validation is only available on Shopify Plus, with a greyed out switch labelled Upgrade plan and an example card We found an address that might be more accurate; the tab General shows its options (for example House number in line 2, Skip ZIP+4 code correction (US only) and Hide Extension for Format Errors) with the label Upgrade plan. The dashboard shows Address Error Rate 0 %, Total Addresses Edited 0 and Saved Support Tickets 0, with a note to switch to Pro for email typos, suspicious names and advanced address issues. Plans: the in-app plan choice shows Minimal (Basic address validation for every order) at $9.99 / month with Start 14 day free trial, with Format checks on and Address validation and Automatic address correction crossed out, plus 24/7 Live Chat on and Done-for-you setup and Money-back guarantee crossed out, and AddressHero Pro (Advanced address checking billed per order) at $0.04 / order, also with Start 14 day free trial and every feature on. The app calls the cheap plan Minimal, the dossier calls it Lite. Pay per Address from the listing was not offered in the app. Checkout: Minimal was chosen as the cheapest plan. The Shopify screen Approve subscription said You will not be billed for this test charge. and You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., with a subtotal of $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, a total of $9,99 due 1 Dec and $9,99 USD every 30 days. The row Add payment method was on the screen but nothing had to be entered. The test charge was approved (Approve) without a card or payment method; nothing was billed. Cancelling: Settings, Apps, the menu of the row AddressHero (Open app, View details, Get support, Uninstall). The dialog Uninstall AddressHero ? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Testing multiple apps). The plan cannot be cancelled apart from the app; uninstalling ends it. The app was uninstalled at about 13:19 and is gone from the installed apps. Not tested: real address validation in a checkout or a test order, Shopify Plus In-Checkout Validation, post-checkout validation, automatic correction, the Pro plan, Pay per Address, emails and the enterprise demo. Clean up: the app was uninstalled; no theme change was saved and no app embed was switched on. Other apps were not touched. One extra tab opened by the first Install click could not be closed by us. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested LinkShortener.io in our existing free account: two short links to our own sites were made in about a minute and 4 steps; curl showed a direct 302 with the right target in 0.12 to 0.23 seconds, with no interstitial page and no advertisement; a browser click showed in the statistics after about 10 seconds while curl requests were not counted; UTM fields and a QR code per link work on Free. On Free there is no own slug, editing an existing link is behind Upgrade and custom domain, password and social preview are paid; changing the destination of a short link needs Pro. The prices match the dossier, and the app also lists two plans of $6. Deleting the test links gave a server error, so they are still active. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used our existing LinkShortener.io account on the Free plan, with the interface in English (no language setting was found). The test started at 09:48:53. The onboarding (Set up your links the correct way) asked 3 questions, each with a Pro option and a free option (a branded domain, an email when a link breaks, a branded QR code); the free options were chosen (the short domain of the service, You check your links yourself, Plain QR codes, with our name under them), and the page ended with the line Pro adds all three, for $34 a month. Start Pro, which was not clicked. The business name field was filled with our name and was changed to Test Co. Core action: two short links were made, to two of our own sites. The first link was made in about 1 minute and 4 steps (name, destination, UTM fields, Create) and got a short link on the shared short domain of the service. The UTM fields (Source, Medium, Campaign, Term, Content) work on Free, with the text To make use of Google Analytics, the Source, Medium, and Campaign parameters are required.; the UTM table on the link page stayed empty, but the redirect did add the parameter. Redirect check -I: HTTP/2 302 with the right Location (including the UTM parameter on the first link), cache-control no-store, in 0.12 to 0.23 seconds; there is no interstitial page and no advertisement (a direct 302 through Cloudflare). Click statistics: 3 curl requests were NOT counted (filtered as bots); the first browser visit at 09:50:02 showed as 1 click (This Week 1, All Clicks 1) about 10 seconds later, a second visit made it 2, and the second link also showed 1. The country map said No country data available at first and then showed a map; per country and device reports were not checked because the visits came from one browser. Limits on Free: the Random path switch cannot be turned off on Free, so there is no own slug (URL Customisation is Pro); custom domain, country and device redirects are marked Paid feature, and the form shows expiry, password, social preview, time-based redirects and open in app as paid options; the Edit button on an existing link carries the label Upgrade. Every link has a black and white QR code with Download PNG and Download SVG, no logo; the separate QR list was empty (No records found) and no separate QR was made, because it uses the same allowance. The account page says Links and QR Codes remaining: 20/20 (Refreshing in 4 weeks from now) and You have reached your custom domain limit. Plans, read up to the payment step on the Plans page (US dollars, nothing filled in): Free $0 (20 links or QR codes per month, UTM Builder, Basic Analytics); Basic $13 a month ($10.83 a month yearly, Billed annually: $130 a year; 350 links or QR codes, 1 custom domain, edit the destination of a QR code); Pro $34 ($340 a year; 2,000, 3 custom domains, URL Customisation, edit the destination of a short link, broken link checker); Elite $260 ($2,600 a year; 5,000, 10 custom domains); QR code only $6 (20 QR codes per month); Link in bio only $6; Enterprise on request (10,000). The banner says 12 months for the price of 10. Deviations from the dossier: the prices and allowances of Free, Basic, Pro and Elite match. The dossier text says a Free plan and three paid plans; the app also lists two plans of $6 (QR code only and Link in bio only) and Enterprise on request. Basic may change only the destination of a QR code, and changing the destination of a short link needs Pro. The price fields of our pages are not touched. Checkout: NOT reached. No Upgrade or Start Pro button was clicked, so no tax, total or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: Free, no subscription, so nothing to cancel. Not tested: an own domain (not allowed), the paid plans, what happens at 20 of 20, reports per country and device (the map was empty for visits from one browser), the broken link checker, Link in bio, Bulk CSV import and the migration tool. Clean up: the bulk action Delete selected Links gave 500 SERVER ERROR and a second try did nothing visible; the Active switch on the link page could not be operated. So both test links are still active (they redirect to our own sites and were shared nowhere). The business name is now Test Co. All tabs were closed.
findings: Text we checked: "Links and QR Codes remaining: 20/20". The banner says 12 months for the price of 10.

Core action, one question on the demo database: no project and no connection was needed. One click on the suggested question Which plan brings in the most monthly revenue? ran on the sample database. sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Orateur in a test account: the language and region setting, the set-up of the AI receptionist (agent name, instructions and the six language tabs), the plan page in US dollars on the Monthly and Yearly tabs, the Stripe Checkout for Creator (nothing entered) and the place of the Delete Account button. No real call was made and nothing was paid. Start and account: the test started at about 16:06 (Dutch time) in a test our account on the vendor app, already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English and the region was United Kingdom (Settings, Account, Region, Choose your language and region., with the options United Kingdom, France and the Swiss variants in French, German and Italian). There was no separate French interface to switch. The dashboard showed 0 appointments, 0 calls in the last 7 days and No upcoming appointments. No registration, card, phone number or call was asked. Core action, set up the AI receptionist (Receptionist AI, General): the agent name Manon was changed to Test Receptionist and a test text was typed in Instructions (a clinic name, a warm formal tone, parking, and taking a message when the caller asks about pricing); the page said Saving... and saves by itself. Under Languages & voices there are six tabs: French (Default and Active), English, German, Italian, Hebrew and Arabic. English was off and was switched on; its first message is Hello! How can I help you today? with the voice [GB] Clarice. German can be made Active, with the voice [DE] Berta Berlin and the first message Hallo! Wie kann ich Ihnen heute helfen?, and was switched off again. Our typing tool dropped two letters in the instruction text, which is not an app fault. The setup took about 4 minutes and 8 steps (open the settings, the name, the instructions, a language tab and Active); the times may be unreliable because of our tool. The settings stayed saved. No real call was made: the Test call button, the phone number, the calendar link, SMS, the knowledge base, Services, Staff and Clients were not used, and the tabs Call Settings, Rules, Knowledge Gaps and Tools were not opened. Plans: Settings, Billing shows Available Credits 6.000 (about 1h 40m of call time) and the button Add 15 min for $ 3,60. Monthly: Creator $ 49,00 /mo with about 240 minutes, US$ 0,24/min for additional credits and 1 user; Pro $ 99,00 /mo with about 540 minutes, US$ 0,22/min and 2 users; Scale $ 199,00 /mo with about 1,140 minutes, US$ 0,18/min and 5 users; Enterprise Custom; each plan has a free phone number included. Yearly (2 months free): Creator $ 490,00 /yr, Pro $ 990,00 /yr and Scale $ 1.990,00 /yr. The FAQ says 1 credit is about 1 second of AI call time, that phone numbers are temporarily disabled until you add credits or upgrade, and that you can cancel anytime, that unused credits stay on the account and that the phone number stays reserved for 30 days after a subscription ends. The prices are in US dollars, where the dossier has Swiss francs. Checkout: Get Creator opened Stripe Checkout of the vendor company with Subscribe to Creator $49.00 per month, the button Pay and subscribe and the payment choices Apple Pay, Link, Amazon Pay and card. Nothing was entered and we went back. The screenshot of it was thrown away because the page showed an e-mail address that could not be hidden. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Settings, Account has a section Delete Account with a red Delete button; our tool refused the click and it was not tried again, so no account was deleted. A cancellation of a subscription was not seen; the FAQ says cancelling is possible anytime. Not tested: Test call with the browser microphone, a phone number, linking Google or Microsoft, the calendar, SMS (30 credits per message according to the dossier), the knowledge base, Services, Staff and Clients. Clean up: the account stays; the test data is the agent name Test Receptionist, the instruction text and English switched on (German was switched off again). No subscription and no payment. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Petty Cash Manager on its 14 day free trial in the browser: after about 6 steps the first expense with a receipt photo was saved, and 10 test expenses later 8 were approved and 1 rejected, and the november report showed 127.24 for 8 entries, split by category. The CSV export had a header and 10 lines. Everything stays on the device: no account, no cloud, and a banner asks you to download a backup. Cloud sync, which needs an e-mail code, was not tested. The page says Cloud sync costs +$3 a month on any plan, but that is true only for the Monthly plan: Yearly goes from $41.99 to $69.99, which is +$28 a year. Cancelling is only possible after paying. Nothing was paid.
findings: Text we checked: "Try free for 14 days first, no card". What we saw: The app opened with Free trial: 14 days left and no card, account or e-mail address was asked; the setup form and sample data came straight after.

Text we checked: "Balance 495.50". What we saw: The first expense of 4.50 with a receipt photo was saved after about 6 steps and the balance showed 495.50 with 4.50 under Awaiting approval, from a float of 500.

Text we checked: "APPROVED EXPENSES 127.24, 8 entries". What we saw: Of 10 test expenses 8 were approved, 1 was rejected and 1 stayed waiting; the november report showed 127.24 for 8 entries, and the seven categories add up to 127.24. Cash added was 500.00.

Text we checked: "Export to Excel (CSV)". What we saw: The Entries export gave petty-cash-all.csv of 1259 bytes with 11 lines: a header and the 10 expenses, with columns for date, ref, custodian, category, net, tax, total and status. The file was not opened further.

Text we checked: "Your data stays on this device". What we saw: Settings, Backup & restore says the data stays on this device and that browser storage is not protected and may be cleared; a banner said no backup had been downloaded yet. No cloud account was used.

On 17 November 2026 the session tested EditEngine (Bulk Product Editor in the app) on a Shopify development store: the install, a storewide 5 percent price increase with a preview of old and new prices, applying it to 19 products in 8.0 seconds, undoing it, the Select your plan window with greyed out buttons and the uninstall of the app. Nothing was paid, no approval screen was reached and the prices in the store were not checked after the undo. Install: the app is called EditEngine Bulk Product Editor in the App Store listing (English; Free plan available, 4.9 from 162 reviews, Built for Shopify, developer Profitonium), Bulk Product Editor in the install dialog and EditEngine: Bulk Product Editor in the app. The first install attempt at about 13:24 used the wrong form and had no effect; the real install started at about 13:24:40 in our own tab. The dialog Install app warned that Bulk Product Editor doesn't support market-driven shipping and asked for View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, custom data, Shopify admin, other data); the listing also names View customer data and customers, orders, discounts and store credit. The app opened at once without a payment, plan choice, account or demo, with Products 19, Bulk edits 0, Exports 0 and Current plan: Unlimited. Core action, a bulk price change with preview, apply and undo: the start screen offers Ask EditEngine with the line You review a preview before anything is saved. We chose the example Increase all prices by 5% and sent it. The chat Storewide five percent price increase read the request, checked the fields and showed the preview card Raise price by 5% for All products, 19 products and all variants, with examples such as The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard $949.95 to $997.45, four Gift Card amounts and The Minimal Snowboard $885.95 to $930.25 (all agree with a plain 5 percent increase) and Show all 10 preview examples. The card says Nothing changes until you click Apply. You can undo it afterwards. and shows Apply to 19 products, Adjust, Cancel and Preview valid until 01:40 PM. Apply started the edit; after Refresh the job said Completed and a toast said Bulk edit finished. The summary says Processed 19/19 product in 8.0s, No errors, 1:26 PM, Action: IncreaseByPercent. sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Try You on a Shopify development store. The core action, a virtual try-on, was not run, because it needs a photo of a person and we deliberately use no photos of real people. Seen were the install permissions, the two-step onboarding with five models and a safety cap, the Playground screen, the Shopify approval screen with a test charge that was approved without a card (billed 0 dollars), the prices per try-on, the options and the volume tiers, and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing (English) showed the button Install and a rating of 5.0 from 5 reviews. The Install app dialog in the admin asked for View customer data (Device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View store data (Products, orders, store analytics). The install was approved at about 15:05 and at 15:06 the app was open on its welcome screen with the texts $0 today, free to install, Turn your product pages into fitting rooms. and In 30 seconds, your customer uploads a selfie and sees themselves wearing your product. Onboarding: step 2, Pick your model, then put it to the test., shows 10 free credits and five models: Light 1 credit, Medium 1 credit, Pro 1 credit, High 2 credits and Ultra 2K 3 credits, five sample person photos of the app and the auto-detected test product The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard. Step 3, Set your safety limit., says You pay nothing today and that the cap is the limit of the shop and not an amount that is charged, with a standard cap of $10 a month, which on Light means up to about 250 try-ons, and the line that the price drops up to 50% at volume. Core action NOT DONE: the virtual try-on needs a photo of a person (in the Playground 2. Person photo, with Samples or Upload, and in the onboarding a Sample photo). We deliberately use no photos of real people and no real faces, so this step was skipped and the button Generate the try-on was not pressed. No result image was made, so there is no time to a first result and no judgement on the quality, the speed or whether a snowboard is a fitting item. Showing the button in the shop (the block Add to theme) was also not tried, so that no theme change was saved. What was seen: the Playground with You have 10 free tests remaining out of 10., 1. Product to test (My catalog or Custom upload), 2. Person photo and 3. Configuration with Compare 2 configs side by side. Checkout: Activate TryYou ($0 today) opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen with the notice You will not be billed for this test charge., the plan TryYou: pay per try-on, This app bills you for usage charges, and the App spending limit (to a maximum of $10,00 USD per 30 days), with Your next bill: You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it. An optional row Add payment method stood on the screen, no card had to be entered and Approve could be clicked. Because the screen says it is a test charge, the test charge was approved at about 15:09 without a card; nothing was billed. There is one plan, so this is the cheapest. After the approval the app said You are live and Welcome aboard! with 10 free credits left in the Playground and three display options (Classic button, Floating badge, Carousel slide). Prices in Settings, Quality and pricing (Light selected): Light $0.04, Medium $0.12, Pro $0.19, High $0.37 and Ultra 2K $0.58 per try-on. Options: Multi-Image Context (+$0.01 / try-on), Intelligent AI verification (+$0.01 / try-on), which starts a second generation billed at the selected model rate when the AI sees a major error, and Sensitive-content fallback, which was switched ON by default: it retries with a backup model when the main AI refuses a try-on it judges too explicit and is billed at a flat $0.08 instead of the level price. Your volume tiers: Starter full price (0 to 499 a month), Growth -15% (500 to 1,999), Scale -30% (2,000 to 4,999), Pro -40% (5,000 to 9,999) and Enterprise -50% (10,000+). Raising the monthly cap needs a fresh Shopify approval and lowering it takes effect right away. Deviations from the dossier: the volume thresholds ARE published in the app (the dossier says they are not published). The dossier does not name the extra charges of $0.01 a try-on for Multi-Image Context and for AI verification, nor the $0.08 of the fallback that is on by default. Cancelling: the usage plan has no subscription fee and nothing was used. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (the Uninstall button stays grey until one is chosen) and there is a feedback box of 250 characters. There is no cancellation fee or waiting time. The reason Testing multiple apps was given at about 15:16 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: generating a try-on (it needs a photo of a person), so the quality, the speed and the cost per result, the storefront blocks and the capture of e-mail addresses (Klaviyo, Shopify Customers), where the selfies go (the privacy policy names AI providers; this was not checked in the app), and the analytics and the CSV export. Clean up: the test charge approval was the only change; the spending cap stayed at $10 as set by the app on activation; no theme change was saved; the app was uninstalled; all browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: We made one launch film in CrossLoop on 13 November 2026 from our own homepage address, using one of the two credits the account started with. The account is ours, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We downloaded, posted and shared nothing. We did not open Buy credits, so checkout, support and cancellation were not tested.
findings: The dashboard offers a Launch Film at $9 for 1 credit and a Launch Film Studio at $19 for 2 credits. It asks for a page address and a film style, and has an optional box of 400 characters to describe the film. The account started with 2 credits and no card was asked for.

We pasted our homepage address and chose Launch Film in English with the Match my brand style. The status moved from Queued to Reading your site to Rendering videos, and the film was ready after about 16 minutes. The vendor says about 15. Credits went from 2 to 1.

The result was a 61-second narrated film, offered as a 16:9 landscape cut, a 9:16 reel and story cut, a 4:5 portrait cut and a captions file, plus ready-made post text for LinkedIn and Instagram. The pictures and numbers in the film came from our own site. Films are kept for 30 days.

We then asked for a fixed closing line in the description box: 'End with this exact line: Every review shows the date we checked the price.' The form refused it twice with 'We couldn't check your direction right now.' The film only started with the box left empty. We found no script editor or revision button on the result page, so a fixed line could not be tested.

The Studio film, your own voice and other languages
Whether the films can be edited after rendering
