sessions.what: Looked at by our team on 23 October 2026 in a demo account that RoverLead set up for us after contacting us: we logged in and our AI assistant explored it in our browser. The campaigns, statistics and inbox conversations were RoverLead's own demo data. We did not connect LinkedIn and did not approve, resume or send anything, so no number on this page is a result of ours.
findings: Onboarding proposed an ideal customer profile from our own website: software development, IT services and business consulting, 1 to 200 employees, the Netherlands, UK, Ireland, US and Canada, founder, CEO, owner and managing-director titles, with government and education excluded. It then loaded 22 preview leads, each with a 'why now' signal: 13 a recent funding round (October 2026), 4 a new role and the rest recent activity.

Each lead in the demo campaign got a five-step sequence: a connection request without a note, then follow-ups 1, 3, 5 and 7 days later. Every message waited for Approve or Skip, with 'Approve all messages' and 'Generate 50 more' as bulk options.

The AI messages were tailored to us ('Drawn from 2 sources', including a comment the lead had made) and pitched our hands-on reviews and free listing, but also a '2026 B2B software stack guide' that we could not match to any existing page of ours. Read the drafts before you approve them.

After 'Looks good' the Lead Inbox said '21 leads found', one fewer than the 22 in the preview, with a signal per lead (new in role, recently active, recently funded), thumbs up or down for fit, and 'Connect LinkedIn' as the next setup step.

The Unibox sorted the 15 demo conversations into Starred, Hot, Nurture and Follow-up, with a 'Needs reply' filter. Opening one showed an AI reply marked 'Drafted · not sent' with a category; it only goes out when you click Send.
not_tested: Real sending through LinkedIn (not connected) and any acceptance or reply rate: the statistics in the demo account are RoverLead's demo data

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Rewarx AI Product Photography (Rewarx Studio AI in the dossier) on a Shopify development store: the install, one AI photo of a snowboard made with 1 of 10 free credits, the watermark, the offer popup, the Membership Plans, the external Stripe checkout that was opened but not filled in, and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing is Rewarx AI Product Photography by Rewarx Limited. The install form was sent at about 13:32 in our own tab and the Install app dialog asked for View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, Shopify admin), which was approved. The first screen said Session Expired and Click below to reconnect; the button Reconnect via Shopify worked in the same tab and the app loaded. No separate account, phone number or demo was asked. A welcome popup, Welcome to the Studio!, credited 10 free production credits and said we were eligible for 67% OFF the first membership purchase. Core action, an AI product photo of a shop product: Studio, Photography Studio, From Shopify (Import from Shopify Store), the product The Collection Snowboard: Liquid, Use Selected Image, Generate Photos (1 Credits), Confirm Products (Snowboard Top Deck, Confirm Selection (1)) and the question Add a model for better results? answered with No, Keep Simple, so no faces. That was 9 clicks and the result was visible at about 13:35, about 3 to 4 minutes after the install was confirmed. The Library shows the source photo and one result; the viewer shows Photography Studio, Asset Type Photo and Variations 2 / 2. The snowboards stand against a wooden fence in snow with mountains behind them, and the liquid lettering and the graphic stayed recognisable. The photo carries a watermark, rewarx.com, and a banner says Unlock commercial rights & remove watermarks, Upgrade to Pro. The credit counter went from 10 to 9. A file upload runs through a file dialog that we could not reach, so the import from the Shopify store was used. Offer after the first result: a popup First Studio Shot Achievement! showed a one-time Starter Plan offer at EUR 9.90/mo (EUR 29.90 crossed out) with a countdown OFFER ENDS IN 59:20 and the button Claim Discount Now. The popup did not close with the X, Escape or a click beside it; after a reload it was gone and a purple bar STARTER PLAN OFFER: ONLY EUR 9.90 FIRST MONTH stayed. Plans: Upgrade opens Membership Plans in euro with a switch Monthly or Yearly (SAVE 17%): Starter EUR 9.90/mo (EUR 29.90 crossed out, FIRST MONTH DISCOUNT, 100 Credits, No Watermark, Commercial Poster Studio, E-commerce Listing Asset Sets, about 100 Standard Photos or about 33 4K Ultra Photos or 5 Cinematic Videos), Growth EUR 54.90/mo (Save 8%, 200 credits), Scale EUR 129.90/mo (Save 13%, 500 credits, Batch Template Studio, a dedicated manager) and Agency EUR 249.90/mo (Save 16%, 1000 credits, unlimited cloud storage, API access, multi-user access, priority GPU queue, white-label portal, custom style training). The listing names no Agency plan and prices in USD; the amounts for Growth and Scale are numerically the same. Checkout: a click on Subscribe for Starter did NOT open a Shopify Approve subscription screen but an external live Stripe checkout in Dutch (our browser language): Abonneren op Starter EUR 9,37, then EUR 28,29 per month from next month, Starter EUR 28,29, a coupon of EUR -18,92 (66,89% korting voor een maand), Totaal vandaag te betalen EUR 9,37, a choice between EUR and USD (1 USD = 0,9462 EUR), fields for Apple Pay, Link, an e-mail address and a card number and the button Betalen en abonneren. It asks for a card and is not a Shopify test charge, so nothing was entered or paid. The billing therefore runs outside Shopify, in line with the dossier warning that external charges may be billed by Rewarx Limited separately from the Shopify invoice. Cancelling: no subscription was started, so there was nothing to cancel. The uninstall route is Settings, Apps, the menu and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Rewarx AI Product Photography? says you will no longer be able to use the app and that data managed by the app will be deleted, with a required reason (Testing multiple apps) and a feedback field. The app was uninstalled after the test and is gone from the installed apps. Not tested: paying, any plan beyond reading the prices, 4K or 2K upscaling, video, poster, ghost mannequin, model and try-on functions, uploading an own file, downloading, cancelling a paid plan, a refund and credit rollover. Clean up: the app was uninstalled; no subscription and no payment were made; 1 of the 10 free credits was used; no theme change was saved. Other apps were not touched. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Doba twice on a retailer account we created. Without a plan the catalogue hides every price, and the free Doba Pilot gave prices and shipping for three yoga mats for 1 credit. In the Basic trial for US$ 0.99 the prices, the processing time filter and the inventory list worked, and AI Pickr took about 8 seconds and 2 credits. The first charge of US$ 59.99 was set for 27 November, a day after the 7 trial days end. Cancelling took four screens with two retention offers, and the US$ 0.99 was not refunded. Account and start: we created a retailer account. In the morning of 19 November 2026, from about 09:45 to 09:59 CET, our AI assistant tested it in our browser with No Plan and the free Doba Pilot (30 credits). In the afternoon we started the Basic trial ourselves, monthly, US$ 0.99 that day (7:39 AM PST, 16:39 CET), and our assistant tested it from about 16:46 to 16:52 CET in its own tabs. The interface was in English. Promotion popups came up on almost every page and were closed. The review is on MSS (mss/doba-review.html). Round 1, no plan: a search for yoga mat gave 144 results with stock and processing time, but every price read Subscribe to See Price, and Add to Inventory List opened Start Your $0.99 Trial Now. Doba Pilot, at 1 credit a message, answered a request for yoga mats with supplier price, shipping and delivery time in about 1 minute 45 seconds with three products from US$ 14.72 to US$ 33.67, stock, UPS and USPS rates and landed costs. Asked to add a mat to the inventory list, Pilot said Doba has no inventory list it can write to; the counter went from 30 to 28 credits. Round 4, Basic trial: the same search now showed prices (US$ 33.67, 29.46, 29.46, 14.72) with stock and 2 Business Day(s). The filter Max. Avg. Processing Time 2 business days gave 11 results for yoga mat. Add to Inventory List now worked: Add to inventory list successfully, and the Inventory List showed Jute Premium Eco Yoga Mat with 7 variants at US$ 33.67 and shipping US$ 13.69. AI Tool Hub had 300 credits; one AI Pickr run on Sports, Exercise took about 8 seconds and 2 credits (298 / 300 left), with mixed relevance (sunglasses among fitness products). The AI Listing Optimizer needs a product listed to a linked store, and the AI Store Builder starts by linking Shopify; neither was run. Stores: 0/2 stores, nothing linked. The Retailer API needs a Standard or Enterprise plan. Plans and billing: On doba.com/pricing, in USD, with Monthly, Quarterly (5% off) and Annually (15% off) tabs; with Quarterly selected the prices per month are: Limited $28.67, Basic $57.00 with a 7-day Trial for US$ 0.99, Standard $142.67 with a 5-day Trial for US$ 0.99, and Enterprise only monthly or annual. In the trial the plan card lists Storefront Integrations 0/2, Inventory List 0/600, Storefront Products Listings Count 0/250, AI Auto Lister 0/30 and AI Tool Hub Credits 0/300. Pricing Plan shows Basic Trial, Monthly, 7 trial days left, Next Billing Date: Nov 27, 2026 12:00:00 AM (PST) and Next Billing Amount: US$ 59.99; Billing Details show the service cycle from Nov 19 to Nov 26, 2026 7:39:04 AM (PST) and US$ 0.99. The first charge falls about a day after the 7 trial days end. Checkout: in round 1 the trial window was seen and closed with nothing filled in; in round 4 we started the trial ourselves and the checkout was not seen by our assistant. Cancelling, done the same day: Pricing Plan, Actions, Cancel Subscription. A retention screen with Let me think about it and a grey Continue Cancellation link; then a dialog with Cancel immediately (preselected) or Cancel at the end of the current billing cycle and Refund: US$ 0; then One Last Thing Before You Go... with an optional concerns field and a Free for 30 days (worth $90) coupon, declined with Still Leave; then Subscription cancelled successfully! No password and no support contact. The US$ 0.99 trial fee is not refunded. Not tested: linking a store, listing to a store, ordering, the wallet and paid add-ons, the AI Listing Optimizer and a store build, Pay Now, Change Payment Method and the invoice link, and product downloads, which are not included in the trial. Clean up: the account, the inventory list item and the used credits stay; the subscription is cancelled. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested EliteCart on a Shopify development store: the install, the app embed switched on and saved in the theme, a cart drawer in the theme preview (not proven to be EliteCart alone, because the cart apps Cross Sell Auto and Essential Cart were also switched on, and the Buy Two discount came from another app), the plan screen with the order slider, the Shopify approval screen for Essentials (not approved, a payment method was asked) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid. Install: the install form was sent at 14:13 in our own tab; Shopify showed the Install app dialog for EliteCart & Upsell by GEFA Technology with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved. The app opened on Welcome to EliteCart with a Get started list (1 of 4 complete). Step 3, Start your trial, said that as a Shopify Partner development store we have free access and need not subscribe. No separate account, demo or call was asked. Core action, turn on the cart drawer and look at it in the theme preview, about 2 minutes (14:14 to 14:15) and 13 steps: in the theme editor, in our own tab, the app embed EliteCart & Upsell was switched on and the theme was SAVED (Changes saved.), because that was needed to see a result. In the preview we went to The Complete Snowboard and pressed Add to cart. A cart drawer opened with The Complete Snowboard, Color: Ice, a label Buy Two, a price of $629.96 with $699.95 struck through, a row Matching Items with The Collection Snowboard: Liquid $749.95, The Multi-managed Snowboard $629.95 and The Multi-location Snowboard $729.95, and at the bottom Subtotal $1,399.90 USD, Discount -$139.98 USD, Total $1,259.92 USD and a CHECKOUT button. After Activate the Get started list showed 2 of 4 complete. IMPORTANT, this result is not proven to be EliteCart alone: our development store also had the cart apps Cross Sell Auto and Essential Cart switched on in the theme. With EliteCart off, the cart icon showed a different drawer (Cart - 1, You may also like); with EliteCart on, the cart icon still opened that other drawer, and the Matching Items drawer appeared only when Add to cart was pressed. We believe the Matching Items drawer comes from EliteCart because it appeared after the embed was switched on, but this was not confirmed separately in the Cart designer. The Buy Two discount (Discount -$139.98 USD) came from another app and cannot be credited to EliteCart. So we do not claim the drawer as a proven EliteCart result; what is proven here is the install, the plans, the approval screen and the uninstall. Plans: the Plans screen says Free access for development stores. You can access all features for free. Once you switch to a paid Shopify plan or transfer the store, you must select a plan below. A slider How many orders do you have per month? starts at 200: Essentials $29.99 /month, Includes 200 orders / month, Try for free; Professional $79.99 /month, Includes 500 orders / month, Most popular, Try for free; Enterprise Contact us, For an individual quote. With the slider at 5000 orders Essentials showed $199.99 /month and Professional $399.99 /month, both with 5000 orders a month. The ladder between 200 and 5000 orders was not opened step by step, and the dossier example of an extra $10 at 500 orders was not checked. Checkout: Try for free on Essentials opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: You have a 15-day free trial ending on 2 Dec., Subtotal $29,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $29,99 Due 2 Dec, $29,99 USD every 30 days, an app spending limit of a maximum of $229,99 USD per 30 days, and a note that usage charges come on top. The button Add payment method was shown and Approve was greyed out. The sentence You will not be billed for this test charge was NOT on this screen and a payment method was asked, so we did not approve, no card was entered, and we pressed Cancel. Nothing was approved. The listing says a 15-day trial and the dossier pricing page says 14 days; the Shopify screen said 15. Cancelling: no paid plan was ever started, so there was nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the row of the app and the menu (Open app, View details, Get support, Uninstall). The dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required before Uninstall becomes active; we first pressed Cancel and later uninstalled the app with the reason Testing multiple apps, and Shopify confirmed that the app was uninstalled. Not tested: the Cart designer, one-click add-ons, the reward bar, the Upsells flows, Language and translations (multilingual), AI translations, EliteAI Ultra, Analytics, the paid plans and a real charge, the Plus checkout add-ons and the vendor help. Clean up: the theme was saved with the EliteCart app embed switched on (needed for the result; a second save changed nothing); the other cart apps in the store were left as they were. Our own tabs were closed. The app was uninstalled after the files were written. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: We generated one text-to-speech clip in Inworld AI's playground on the free On-Demand plan on 13 November 2026 and read the billing and data retention screens. findings: The playground used the voice Sarah, language Auto and the model Inworld TTS 2, with sliders for delivery and talking speed and MP3 as the download format. Input is limited to 5,000 characters. It offers an Add speaker option and example roles such as Support Agent, AI Companion and Language Teacher. We saw no timeline or video editor.

We entered a support line of 123 characters and pressed Generate. Audio played within about 3 seconds by our eye, not timed, and the playground reported 'First audio in 0.8 s' for a clip of 0:05. The free credit balance went from $1.00 to $0.99 after that one clip. The plan card says 'Up to 70 min TTS included'. We could not tell whether the included minutes or the credit paid for the clip, and we did not measure the allowance beyond one short generation.

Under Billing, the Data Retention setting says Zero Data Retention is available on the Developer plan and above, and the Developer card lists it. The setting could not be changed on the free plan. The Developer plan costs $300 a month on its card.
The plan cards show monthly prices and a yearly option labelled '2 months free'. We did not read yearly prices or open checkout, so tax, renewal terms and the payable total are unknown.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Kedra Checkout Rules and Upsells on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: a payment rule that did not work on the test gateway, a validation rule that blocked a 600 dollar test checkout, the Free plan limit, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid or uninstalled. First rule: Manual Setup, the template Hide COD over an amount, edited into Hide Bogus gateway over USD 100 (order total greater than USD100, then hide payment methods that contain the string Bogus), saved ACTIVE at about 14:44:40. The Hide settings say that Credit card (Shopify Payments) can only be customized on Shopify Plus plans. A test checkout through the theme editor preview used a snowboard of 600 dollars, a made up name, address and email, and no card; nothing was paid. A first check before the rule existed (ski wax at 24.95 dollars) showed the card block Pay with credit card with a Testing instruction. The payment rule did not work: at 600 dollars Pay with credit card and Test Payment Gateway stayed visible, also after changing the string to Test Payment Gateway and then to Credit card. The cause was not established; it may be that the test gateway counts as the card block that is Plus only, but that is a guess. The Free plan allows 1 active rule: creating a second rule while one is active shows ACTIVE Locked with Your Free plan includes 1 active rule and it is in use. The payment rule was set to INACTIVE and a validation rule Block orders over an amount (order total greater than USD500, message Order total exceeds the maximum allowed amount.) was made ACTIVE. At about 14:49 a checkout of 600 dollars showed a red banner at the top that this order cannot be completed with the current checkout details. That is Shopify default text and not the app message; Your own checkout wording is not included on Free. A cart of 24.95 dollars showed no message. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 14:43:00 and a visibly working rule in the test checkout at 14:49:20, about 6 minutes 20 seconds, of which about 3 minutes went on the first rule that did not work; one working rule straight away would have taken about 2 minutes; more than 25 clicks and typing actions including the detour. Uninstall: the app menu offers Manage app, Get support, Pin to your navigation and Uninstall; the Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: post-purchase upsells (a paid plan), hiding, renaming or reordering shipping and payment methods, draft orders, completing a real payment, Plus only features, own wording in the block, and a payment rule with a real second payment method. No kit records were entered.
findings: Vendor claim "7 dagen". What we saw: The Dutch App Store listing named a 7 day trial. The app and the Shopify approval screen showed a 5-day free trial ending on 21 Nov. The trial is 5 days and not 7.

Vendor claim "Your Free plan includes 1 active rule". What we saw: Creating a second rule while one was active showed ACTIVE Locked with this text, so the Free plan really allows 1 active rule over all rule types. A store that needs a payment rule and a validation rule at the same time has to pay for a plan.

Vendor claim "Credit card (Shopify Payments) can only be customized on Shopify Plus plans". What we saw: The Hide settings say so. Our rule that hides the test payment method did not work on the test gateway; whether that gateway counts as this card block is unknown. Hiding or renaming the credit card method of Shopify Payments needs Shopify Plus, so a standard store cannot do that with this app.

Vendor claim "Shopify stores with mixed payment and shipping options". What we saw: The payment rule that should hide the test payment method did not work at 600 dollars, so this audience was not confirmed; shipping rules were not tested and the store only had the test gateway. Whether the app helps a store with mixed payment and shipping options was not shown by this test.

Vendor claim "Shopify merchants with no upsell after checkout". What we saw: Post-purchase upsells are not included on Free or Starter; they come with Starter Plus at $8.99 per month after the first 3 months at 1 dollar, or Unlimited. They were not tested. Post-purchase upsells need Starter Plus or higher.
Vendor claim "Stores that create many draft orders by hand". What we saw: Draft orders were not tested. No evidence for or against draft order help.

Vendor claim "$1 $6.99 /month for your first 3 months then $6.99/month". What we saw: The Starter plan card shows $1 now $6.99 per month for the first 3 months, then $6.99. The Shopify Approve subscription screen for Kedra Starter showed Subtotal $6,99, Discount -$5,99 and Total $1,00 due 21 Nov after a 5-day free trial, $1,00 USD every 30 days, plus any applicable taxes. Card and approval screen agree; tax is unknown and nothing was approved. The yearly price of $58.70 matched the dossier. Starter costs $1 for each of the first 3 months after a 5-day trial and then $6.99 a month, before taxes.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 6 November 2026 on the free trial: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We built one lead form, published it and sent one fictional test lead through it. We did not export the lead and did not open checkout.
findings: The plan page opens in the monthly view: Free at $0.00 with 5 leads a month and Unlimited at $4.99 a month. That matches our read of 18 October. The Free button did not respond, so we used Skip. No card was asked for.

The welcome screen says 'Your free trial of Tapform starts today' and shows decorative cards reading 'Payment successful'. Nothing was paid. Inside the app, a pop-up then says 'You are on free plan' and a banner repeats it, which does not fit a trial that had just started.
A pop-up offering a free call with a sales person appeared twice during the session.

The default form comes with a consent text under it. It says Tapform and its providers may contact you by text or call, some of it automated, once the form is submitted. Check that wording before you put the form on your own site.

Our title and description with the accent in 'Zoë', the quotation marks and the dash were saved and shown correctly. The published form carries a 'Powered by tapform' badge, and its public address is built from the account holder's full name.

The address block took only five-digit US-style ZIP codes. The field is numeric, so the Dutch postcode '3011 AB' was cut to '3011' and then refused with 'Zip must be 5 digit number!', although the country was set to the Netherlands. We typed '30110' to get past it. The lead arrived with that value.

After the submit, the thank-you screen carries an advert, 'Create your Tapform'. The lead list showed our lead and a demo lead that was already there. The counter read 'Leads collected 1/5', so the demo lead does not count.
The lead detail kept the accent and the quotation marks. We could not confirm from the text view that the line break in the notes field survived.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on the free plan in Imagify's web app: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We uploaded three of our own simple test images (a 12 KB PNG, a 50 KB JPG and a 3.4 MB PNG), compared Smart and Lossless and watched the quota counter after each step.
findings: The account started at '0.0KB / 20MB used. You have 100% credit left.' Auto-converting PNG to JPEG is marked 'only for Pro users'; resizing is available on free.
Smart compression took the PNG from 11.8KB to 3.3KB (72.36%) and the JPG from 48.9KB to 12.3KB (74.91%), each within about 8 seconds.

After the first two images the quota counter read 61.44KB of 20MB, much closer to their input sizes than to the compressed results. The later counter increments varied, so we did not establish the exact quota accounting rule.
Lossless took the same PNG from 11.8KB to 5.8KB (51.05%), against 3.3KB with Smart.
The 3.4MB file was refused straight away with 'File size must be under 2.0 MB. Current file size is 3.4 MB' and used no quota.

The summary on the optimizer page is mislabelled: 'You saved 15.5KB out of 60.7KB' gave the size after compression (3.3KB + 12.3KB), while the real saving was about 45KB. The History page showed the right saving per file.
History notes 'Optimized images are available to download for 24 hours' on a free account. End state: 92.16KB of 20MB used after four optimisations and one refused upload.

The resize result (we did not check the output size)
The WordPress plugin and automatic WebP and AVIF conversion (we only used the web app)

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested UserHelp.co in our existing free account: a project was made in about a minute and the widget form was previewed, but Submit does nothing in the preview, so no real report was received and the widget was not put on a site. The free plan shows only the 5 oldest responses (the dossier says unlimited), refuses a second project and lists Categories as an upgrade feature, and the Upgrade page shows an Email add-on without a price that the dossier does not have. The price of $59 one-time matches. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing UserHelp our account, on the Free plan, with the interface in English (the app has no language setting). The test started at 09:01 in our own tab on app.userhelp.co, signed in, with the text Select or create a new project. UserHelp is a feedback widget that you put on your own site; it is not a help desk or a knowledge base, and no AI assistant was seen in the app. Core action: a project called Test Project Acme was made in 1 step (type a name and press Enter), in about 1 minute, with the message Your new project has been created. The project has the tabs Content, Setup, Responses and Settings. Content has the button text (Report a problem), the button color, text color, Dark mode, a language choice, Add category and a privacy policy URL. The preview of the widget form has Name, Email, Description (required), Capture screenshot, Include my browser details, Submit and the line Powered by UserHelp.co. The preview says that features such as submitting a response and capturing a screenshot are disabled during the preview, and Submit did nothing there, so no real report was received. A real test needs the widget code on a site; that was not done, because the code was not allowed on a site. Setup shows two script lines for the head of a page (run.userhelp.co). Limits on Free: the Responses tab says Only the 5 oldest responses are shown. Upgrade with a one-time payment to view all of them. A second project was refused with an alert that the project limit of the Free account was reached and that unlimited projects need a one-time payment; no second project was made. Plans, read up to the payment step: the Upgrade page (Upgrade your account) lists Unlimited projects (Free accounts are limited to one project), Every response (all of your responses, not just the first 5, and search and filter them), Session replay, Technical details (browser, operating system, error logs, network requests and web vitals), Categories, Team workflow, Public discussions, Integrations (Zapier, webhook) and No watermark, with a button to upgrade by paying $59 one-time. Next to it stands an Email add-on (Email support inbox, Reply notifications, Branded emails, with the line Upgrade your account first to add email features) with no price, and a Lifetime deal box with an LTD code field. Nothing was clicked or filled in. Deviations from the dossier: (a) the dossier says Free has unlimited responses, while the app shows only the 5 oldest on Free. (b) A second project on Free is refused. (c) The dossier puts categories on Free; the app lists Categories as an upgrade feature, although the Add category button is in the Content tab (whether adding a category works on Free was not tried). (d) The Email add-on without a price and the LTD code are not in the dossier. The price of $59 one-time matches the dossier. The number of team members, the retention of recordings, the length of the one-time access and the refund rule are not stated anywhere in the app, which fits the dossier. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached. The $59 button was not clicked, so no tax, total, card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: there is no subscription; a project can be removed under Settings, Danger zone, Delete project, which was not clicked, and the profile page only has Log out and Edit profile, with no account deletion. Not tested: a real submission and screenshot (the widget code was not placed on a site), the Pro features, the payment screen, the email functions, the docs site and the terms. Clean up: the project Test Project Acme stays in the account, because Free allows only one project; it can be deleted under Settings. The tab was closed. A first try to make a second project froze the page after the alert; it was restarted by navigating and nothing was made. The profile page, which shows an email address, was not photographed.

sessions.what: A review account in SurFox's review sandbox, given to us by the founder. The sandbox says so on every page: leads, dashboards and results are sample data, messaging is switched off and the AI Learning page is a mock-up. Two things work for real there, the test conversation on a campaign and Surf, the campaign assistant. findings: It did not invent a price. Asked what the product costs, the AI said the price depends on data sources and users and would be given on the call, which matched the knowledge document we gave it. A request to stop texting was honoured at once and classed as an opt-out.

The first test, on 3 October, had visible faults: a placeholder [SLOTS] sent as text, a summary claiming the lead had picked a time slot when they had not, a question answered as unknown although the knowledge document covered it, and openers longer than the 150 characters SurFox aims for. sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested the free GEO scan and the citation probe of CiteRoute on a site of our own, in our existing free account. The scan took about 3.5 minutes in 3 steps and gave 81/100 Strong technical readiness, although Google shows the site hardly at all. It reported 0 JSON-LD detected while the homepage has 3 JSON-LD blocks, and some tips are made up (a placeholder wikidata address and an endpoint /api/agent/catalog). The citation probe gave Verified Citation three times on a question that contains the domain name, with n=1 per engine; Claude said it had no verified information and still got 92/100. The prices match the dossier; the dossier says CiteRoute does not measure citations while the app has a probe, and the scan page says rescans every 7 days while Free has daily re-scans struck through. The tracking tag and the AI bot log were not tested, because they need verification by meta tag or DNS. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing CiteRoute our account, on the Free plan, with the interface in English (no language setting was found). The test started at 09:22 in our own tab. The My sites page showed FREE PLAN and No sites yet. Adding a site needs the CiteRoute Tag and a check of ownership with a meta tag or a DNS TXT record, and the page says that CiteRoute verifies that you control the domain before adding it. That was NOT done, so the tracking tag and the AI bot log were not tested. The scanned site is a site of our own; its domain is not named in this delivery. Core action: the GEO Scanner (the audit page) works without verification. The domain of our own site was typed in at 09:23, the scan was started, and the result came after about 3.5 minutes (the progress bar stayed at 98% for a long time). It took 3 steps: type the domain, start the scan, start the probe. Result: Technical Readiness Score 81 / 100, labelled Strong technical readiness, with sub scores Tabular and FAQ 77, Content depth 86, Schema 73 and Section hierarchy 88. The scan reported JSON-LD Schemas: 0 detected, 1 H1 and 31 H2, 4,703 words, 0 tables and 0 of 15 points for JSON-LD Schema.org declarations. Check of the scan: the homepage has 3 application/ld+json blocks (Organization, WebSite with a SearchAction and an ItemList with 12 items), so 0 detected is wrong. The 0 tables is right; the llms.txt file exists (HTTP 200) and /.well-known/agent.json gives 404, as the scan says. The Schema sub score of 73/100 stands next to 0 of 15 points for JSON-LD, so the scores contradict each other. Google shows our own site hardly at all, so a label of Strong technical readiness is suspiciously optimistic; readiness is not visibility. The recommendations: add Organization, FAQPage and Dataset JSON-LD and a price table. The Organization example uses sameAs links to our own pages; the second patch example has a placeholder wikidata address ending in Q... and a made-up Crunchbase address; the agent.json example has a made-up endpoint /api/agent/catalog. One tip names the Dataset schema as the fix for HTML data tables and says Embed this JSON-LD on a table tip. These tips must not be copied blindly. The live citation probe (via OpenRouter, preset Brand Authority, no verification needed) asked What are the core capabilities and verified offerings of the domain of our own site; the question itself contains the domain name, so a mention is almost certain. Perplexity Sonar: 92/100, Verified Citation, 100% (n=1), 20 source URLs; the answer mostly fits our site. OpenAI GPT-4o Search: 92/100, Verified Citation, 1 source URL; the answer is a generic invention (pre-built AI applications). Anthropic Claude 3.5: 92/100, Verified Citation, while the answer says I don't have verified information about this site in my training data; it still counts as a citation because it named the URL. Google Gemini: 68/100, Brand Mention Only; the description is wrong (a no-code AI app marketplace). A citation on a question that contains the domain name proves nothing, and n=1 per engine is not a measurement. Deviation from the dossier: the dossier says CiteRoute does not promise or measure specific citations, while the app has a citation probe, with n=1 per engine; no guarantee was seen. Second, the scan page says CiteRoute rescans domains every 7 days automatically, while the Free plan has Daily automated re-scans struck through and Pro has them. Plans, read up to the payment step: Free $0 forever (10 GEO scans per month, GEO Radar 1 monitored buyer prompt, 1-on-1 competitor comparison of 2 domains, 3 watchlist domains, community leaderboard, agent.json Studio, basic score report; struck through: Tracking tag and AI bot traffic detection, API key access, Daily automated re-scans, Weekly email performance digest); Pro $79 a month (unlimited GEO scans, GEO Radar 10 prompts 24/7, 5-way competitor benchmark, 1 verified site with tracking tag, 20 watchlist domains, an AI bot and crawler analytics dashboard, API key with 500 requests a day, history and trend charts, Start 14-day Trial, 14 days free, cancel anytime); Agency $249 a month, Most popular (10 verified client sites, white-label PDF, API 10,000 requests a day, 14 days free); Enterprise Custom. API pricing per call: geo-score $0.02, verify $0.01 and ai-traffic $0.05, and requests beyond the daily plan limits are billed at standard usage rates. The prices and the 14-day trial match the dossier. The Free limit of 10 scans a month was not tested (the counter is not visible on the scan page). No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached. The Pro trial was not started and no payment screen was seen. Cancelling: Free has no subscription. The account menu has API Keys, Third-Party AI Keys and Sign Out, and no button for deleting the account or cancelling a plan; the FAQ says you can upgrade, downgrade or cancel (text cut off). No site was added, so nothing had to be removed. sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on a new account, without connecting a website or paying: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We trained the agent on 177 characters of text about a made-up shop (the same facts as in our Tidio test), then asked five fact questions, five rephrased ones and two it could not know. findings: Onboarding has four steps: Train, Brand, Test and Install. Training sources are a website (with linked pages on the same domain, or a sitemap), files, text or YouTube, against a counter of '0 / 500K characters'. Our 177 characters of text were trained in about 10 to 20 seconds.
The dashboard only opens after the onboarding: going to the app sent us back to the get-started steps. The first sign-in magic link returned 'INVALID_TOKEN'; a second one worked.

The guardrails slider starts on 'Max (default): Most sophisticated', which refuses off-topic questions and answers in the user's language; Chatwith warns that 'customizing or overriding the guardrails is difficult'.
All five fact questions were answered correctly, and four of the five rephrased ones, such as 'No. The Lila-17 is purple.' when we asked whether it was red.

Asked whether a fault after one month was covered by the 37-day warranty, it answered 'No. The Lila-17 warranty is 37 days, so it is still covered after one month.': it starts with no and ends with yes.

Asked about Sunday opening, which our text did not cover, it said 'I do not know the answer to this question.' and made nothing up. Our last question, on return costs, stayed at 'Not sent. Retry', also after a retry; we did not find out why.
The test chat made suggestion buttons from the knowledge itself (Product, Color, Pickup, Warranty) and shows 'Powered by Chatwith'.

On 16 November 2026, 26 days after the test, the same agent on our unpaid account answered two questions only with 'This assistant can't reply right now.' That day the pricing page listed no free plan: the cheapest plan was Starter at $9 a month.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Optery in an existing Free Basic our account without entering personal data: the dashboard with its coverage of 0 / 621 data brokers and the list of 396 sites, the plan page on the Monthly and Yearly tabs, the countries in the help article, the cancel and pause text in the FAQ and the place of the Delete Account button. The scan was not run because it needs real personal data, and the checkout was not reached. Nothing was paid and nothing was changed. Start and account: the test started at 16:15 (Dutch time) in the existing Optery our account on the Free Basic plan, already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English (only the cookie bar was in Dutch and it was not confirmed). The hard limit of the test was that no personal data was entered, no scan was started and nothing was changed. The dashboard opened about 15 seconds after the address was loaded (16:16:13 to 16:16:28), after an empty first screen, in 1 step. Onboarding: the button 4 / 4 What to do next lists the Onboarding tasks: look at the screenshots and View links, upgrade for removals (the app says removal of profiles starts in 1 - 3 business days), Update your Profile (the more info, the better) and Share Optery. The profile form was only read for its labels and nothing was typed: the tabs Basic Info, Emails, Phones, Addresses, Addt'l Info, Relatives, Power of Attorney and Safety Program; in Basic Info the fields First Name, Last Name, Middle name (recommended), Birth Year, Birth Day (recommended), Birth Month (recommended) and Gender; a reCAPTCHA stands on the page. The profile page itself was not kept as evidence because it shows a name, an e-mail address and a birth year that cannot be covered cleanly. Core action, the data broker overview and the coverage of the plan: the dashboard says Data Brokers Covered by Your FREE BASIC Plan 0 / 621. The list All Sites (396) has 8 pages of 10 and the columns WEBSITE, PLAN COVERAGE (FREE BASIC), EXPOSURE RISK, RE-EXPOSED, LINK TO PROFILE and MORE INFO; the rows read Core Upgrade for coverage and some have a View link; the tabs are PRIMARY SCAN, CUSTOM SCAN and EXPANDED REACH, and Buy Custom Scan is greyed out. The empty results area says that screenshots of exposed data appear once the vendor finds them. The list has no country column or filter (only With re-exposures and Without re-exposures). The scan was NOT tested, because it needs real personal data. The dashboard also showed Your scan is about to start with a countdown of 35 minutes, the advice to complete the profile first and the buttons Postpone Scan by 45 mins and Scan Now: the scan starts by itself with the profile that already exists in the account. We did not postpone it and did not start it. Countries: the help article of 09/25/2026 says Optery is available to residents of the United States, Canada (excluding Quebec), Australia, New Zealand and South Africa at this time; other countries can make an account and are told when their country is supported; business customers on enterprise plans can cover non-U.S. residents. The Netherlands and the rest of Europe are not served for private persons. The footer has a link Pricing - Canada. Plans: Free Basic lists a Personalized Exposure Report with Screenshots, a Custom Scan of Your Google Search Results, Self-Service Removal Tools, a Phone and Email Scan Preferences Tool, Profile Visibility at Hundreds of Sites with Patented View Links, Unlimited Name Variations (for the same person), Unlimited Past Cities and States and standard e-mail help. Yearly: Core $3.25 a month ($39.00 billed yearly, automated removal from 377+ sites), Extended $12.42 ($149.00 billed yearly, 554+ sites) and Ultimate $20.75 ($249.00 billed yearly, 623+ sites, MOST POPULAR); the page says Save 17%, which ~ 2 free months. Monthly: Core $3.99, Extended $14.99 and Ultimate $24.99. Core: automated removals from 377+ sites (or 152+ without enabling Expanded Reach), with a maximum of 1 name and city and state per user, monthly automated scans and removals and a Bot Only approach with no human Privacy Agent for QA or special cases. Extended: 554+ sites (or 329+), unlimited name variations, unlimited past cities and states, a Humans and Machines approach with an assigned human Privacy Agent and removal reports with before and after screenshots about every 90 days. Ultimate: 623+ sites (or 398+), Unlimited Custom Removal Requests for 1,360+ sites total (eligible after 30 days), the Google and Bing outdated content tool and priority e-mail help. The refund text says to cancel the account within 30 days of the first purchase and then send the refund request to the vendor help address, to be processed within 5 - 10 business days. The Account page says AI Model Preferences (Internal (default) or External (OpenAI)) and Maps Preferences need Extended or Ultimate. Differences with the dossier: the Ultimate yearly price is $20.75 in the app (249 divided by 12) where the dossier has $20.70; the site counts in the app are 377+, 554+ and 623+ (152+, 329+ and 398+ without Expanded Reach) where the dossier has slightly different numbers; the custom removals are 1,360+ sites in the app where the dossier has 940+; the dashboard names 621 data brokers in the coverage box and 396 sites in the list; Free Basic also lists Unlimited Name Variations and Unlimited Past Cities and States, and the Google scan on Free Basic is a Google Search Results scan. Checkout: NOT reached. No payment method was added (the Account page says no payment methods have been added yet) and Upgrade was not clicked, so no total, tax or renewal term was seen. Cancelling: the FAQ on the Plans page says a paid plan can be paused through Pause Subscription on the Account page, and cancelled by downgrading to Free Basic from the Plans page or through the button Cancel Subscription on the Account page, after which billing stops and the plan stays active for the rest of the paid period (the end of the text was cut off). The Free Basic account has no Cancel Subscription button, so no cancellation was seen. The Account page has a section Delete Account: This will permanently delete your Optery account, you lose your optout progress and profile info and there is no turning back, with a red button Permanently Delete My Optery Account that was not clicked. Not covered by the service (FAQ): blogs, news, forums, social media (LinkedIn, Facebook, TikTok and others), legal registers, documents online and the dark web. Not tested: the scan, filling the profile, the exposure report with screenshots, the Custom Scan, Expanded Reach and the power of attorney, real removals and the time until a listing is gone, a paid plan, the checkout page, Cancel Subscription, the family plan, the business plan and the mobile app. Clean up: the account, the profile and the plan (Free Basic) were left unchanged and the cookie bar was not confirmed. The hiding of the name and the avatar on the dashboard was done only temporarily in the page and nothing was saved. All our tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026: we created the account and our AI assistant finished the onboarding and ran the test in his browser. The sign-up put the account on a Plus trial, so we first logged two phone notes on a made-up customer and added tags and saved replies, then switched the account to Free and pushed tags and saved replies past the documented limit of 10.
findings: Signing up did not start on Free. The account landed on a Plus trial ('Trial Period Oct 20 - Nov 03', 1 user, $54/user, 'First monthly payment on Nov 4, 2026') plus a 92-day AI Answers trial, without asking for a payment card.

Switching to Free needed two clean-ups first. Free allows no private Docs site, so the empty knowledge base Help Scout had created had to be made public, and Free allows 0 workflows, so the two '[Try me]' example workflows had to be deleted. The confirmation screen then listed the Free limits, including 10 tags and 10 saved replies.

The 10-tag limit was not enforced right after the switch: an eleventh tag was accepted without any message and Settings > Tags showed '11 tags'. Only a lighter style on the conversation set it apart. Two of the ten were 'welcome' and 'practice', which Help Scout had created itself.

The 10-saved-reply limit was enforced, but with a generic error: 'Could not create saved reply draft' when opening a new one and 'Could not create saved reply' when saving, with no mention of a limit. An example reply Help Scout added counted as one of the ten.
Editing a saved reply worked: changing only the number of warranty days from 37 to 41 left the rest of the text unchanged after a reload.

Two phone notes for the same email address joined one customer profile, and the second showed the first in the sidebar. Help Scout filled in the company on its own ('Internet Assigned Numbers Authority' for example.com), and timestamps did not follow our Europe/Amsterdam time zone: 5:53 am was shown at 07:53 local time.

sessions.what: A new account, which starts on a 14-day trial with paid-plan limits (10,000 sessions a month), not on the Free plan. We put the tracking snippet on a two-page test page of our own, with a sign-up form, a button, a link to a pricing page and an element that looks clickable but does nothing. Then we sent scripted visits whose every step we logged: eight visitors on desktop and phone who clicked, scrolled, filled in the form and gave up halfway, rage-clicked the dead element or left after five seconds, plus two later visits spaced more than a minute apart. We compared the recordings and the friction report with that log.
findings: Recording is off after installation. The dashboard confirmed 'Your tracking code is installed', but nothing was captured until we pressed 'Activate tracking'. Our first round of eight visits was lost that way.

After activation, only the first three visits of the second round were recorded. The other five, and two later visits spaced more than a minute apart, never appeared, while the billing page showed 3 of 10,000 sessions used and the recording rate stood at 100%. All visits came from one address and a scripted browser, so this may be a filter on repeated visits rather than a fault; we could not tell which, and the form, drop-off and rage-click checks could not be scored.

The recordings that did arrive were partly right. The visit that went on to the pricing page showed 2 pages and the phone visit was marked as mobile. The first visitor clicked the main button and scrolled to the bottom over about half a minute, yet the list showed 9 seconds and the friction report counted it as a bounce.
not_tested: the Free plan itself, heatmaps over many visits, funnels, surveys, and real visitors from many addresses
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 22 November 2026 in Namefruits, NameRobot's naming app, with the interface in English. We set up a naming project for a software price comparison website, took the free Thorough Mode and chose Keep trying at every payment prompt. We paid nothing.
findings: Sign-up: only an email and a password, with no card. The app opened straight on a questionnaire with a progress counter.
Mode: after about ten questions it asked us to pick Quick Mode, with payment right at the start, or Thorough Mode, with payment only after a few questions. We took Thorough Mode.
Payment prompts: the first came at 7% of the questionnaire and a second at 10%, right where the first name suggestions would start. Neither screen showed a price.
Names: up to that point we got no name for our own project. The Unused Names list said There are no names in this list yet.

Keywords: the free part collected 35 keywords, all derived from the Software industry we picked. Our own description, comparing software prices, did not show up in the list; you can add keywords by hand.
Language: one label on the mode screen was still in German (Zahlung) in the English interface.
not_tested: the paid name generation and the names it makes; namerobot.com listed $99 per project on 7 October 2026
the automatic domain and trademark checks on names, and the NameReport at the end
NameScore and NameReport bought on their own ($19 per report)
the name idea guarantee, which promises a new run for free

Nothing was billed. Install: the install button of the App Store listing was pressed at 14:34 in our own tab; Shopify showed the Install app dialog with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved. The app opened on a login page and then a plan selection at about 14:35. In the admin the app is called Bold Product Upsell, while the App Store listing says Bold AI Upsell & Cross-Sell. Our development store also had other upsell apps switched on; everything below comes from the Bold app or the Bold install and approval screens. Approval: the plan selection showed one plan, Basic $4.99 /month (Boost your average order value from day one with Bold Upsell), with the button Get Started for Free. This led to a Shopify Approve subscription screen: You will not be billed for this test charge., plan Basic, $4,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $4,99, Total $4,99 Due 24 Nov. An Add payment method row was shown but not required. Because the screen said it was a test charge, we approved it at 14:36; no payment method was entered and nothing was billed. Core action, one upsell offer, about 8 minutes (14:34 to 14:42) after the install and about 12 clicks from Manual Offers: an onboarding Enable the Bold Upsell App Embed in three steps (Configure your theme, Choose your offer type, Configure your offer) was continued without opening the theme editor; then Setting up your Smart Offers and Smart Offers Queued (We're still learning about your store! Under Manual Offers, Create Your First Offer, Choose Offer Type (Cross-sell Buy X Get Y, Upsell, Post-Purchase Thank You Page, Post-Purchase Email, Free Gift, Funnel, Rewards Bar, Bundles and subscription offers), we picked Upsell, then Configure & Style: Offer Name Snowboard upgrade, Location Product Page (Only one location available), Trigger Products All products selected, Offer Products 1 product selected (The 3p Fulfilled Snowboard $2629.95). The preview inside the app, a pop-up, showed Want to upgrade?, Accepting this offer will replace the original item in your cart with the offer below., a button Replace item and a link No thanks, at about 14:41. The banner said App Embed Status: Inactive, Action required to display upsells on your storefront. Please enable the Bold Upsell App Embed in your theme. We did not switch the embed on, so the offer was NOT seen on the storefront; only the preview inside the app was seen, and no theme change was saved. Plans: the app showed only the Basic plan at $4.99 /month, which agrees with the App Store; the other plans of the listing (Grow, Advanced, Plus) were not shown in the app. Cancelling: no payment was ever due and the trial was not cancelled separately. The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps, the row Bold Product Upsell and Uninstall; the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required, we gave Testing multiple apps, and at about 14:48 the app was gone from the installed apps. No separate account, demo, call or phone number was asked. Not tested: the storefront display (the app embed was not switched on), offers in the cart or drawer, post-purchase offers, checkout offers for Plus, Smart Offers (no order data yet), the plans Grow, Advanced and Plus, and a real conversion. Clean up: no theme changes were saved; only the offer Snowboard upgrade existed in the app and went away with the uninstall; other apps were not touched; our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Bold Memberships on a Shopify development store: the install, guided setup of a free membership plan with exclusive access and a discount, the review screen with the price, the Shopify test charge (approved without a card, billed 0 dollars) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The storefront was not seen. Install: the App Store listing (English, now called Bold Memberships & Loyalty) says Free to install. Additional charges may apply., with a rating of 4.4 from 89 reviews. Install was clicked at about 11:36 and the app opened at about 11:38 after the Install app dialog (customer data, staff and contributor data, view and edit store data). There was no plan choice and no price question at install. The welcome screen says Build a membership that brings customers back. and offers Launch with an expert (Book a call, Start a chat) or Build it yourself with Start guided setup. We did not use the call or the chat. Core action: guided setup in three steps. Step one, Free or paid: plan name Test Member (tag test_member), and we chose Free for all customers (Customers join automatically, at no cost). A checkbox offers to add the 6 existing customers now; the text says that if it is left off, existing customers join when they place an order or click Join Now, and that each member counts toward your app plan's member total. Step two, Rewards and benefits: we chose Exclusive access, with the product Bundle Product #1, and Discounts, 10 percent named Member 10 off on All orders. Step three, Finish initial setup: Open theme editor and Create plans page were skipped, so no theme was changed and no store page was created. The review screen Almost done! shows the plan Test Member, the enrollment Free (all customers) and the benefits Exclusive access and Discounts, and says that Bold Memberships is always $0.13 per month/customer, with no transaction fee, no monthly base fee, Free for your first 10 member signups, and Enterprise pricing for over 5,000 customers. After approval the app said You're all set! Your membership plan is live. with a Polish your plan list (1 of 4 done). Timing, approximate tester observations: about 11 minutes from opening the app at 11:38 to the live plan at about 11:49, in about 14 steps. The plan was seen only in the app: the theme embed was not switched on, so the storefront widget and the gated product were not seen. Listing: Scale at $0.13 per member per month, 100% free for the first 30 days, First 10 members are free forever, No flat monthly base fees and No transaction fees. The app agrees on the price, no base fee and no transaction fee; the review screen says free for your first 10 member signups without the word forever and shows no 30 days free. Checkout: the review screen has one button, Start free trial, which opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen for Scale: You will not be billed for this test charge., This app bills you for usage charges, an App spending limit of a maximum of $10.000,00 USD per 30 days, and Your next bill: You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it. The screen shows no price and an Add payment method row. No card was entered and we approved this test charge at about 11:48, which cost nothing. Members: the app text says each member counts toward your app plan's member total, including free members. This was read from the screen only and was not proven with an invoice. Cancelling: we did not look for a cancel button in the app. Cancelling means uninstalling from Settings, Apps. The dialog Uninstall BOLD Memberships? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app such as discounts will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. A Reason for uninstalling is required (we chose Testing multiple apps) and feedback is optional. The dialog has no warning about running charges or a refund. Not tested: a paid plan with member payments through Stripe, the storefront widget and the gated product (theme embed off), the wallet card, loyalty points, store credit, Shopify POS, the chat or call and the free setup with the team. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 11:55 and is no longer in the list of installed apps; the plan Test Member went with it. No theme change was saved, no page or navigation link was made. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

Nothing was paid, approved or published to the store. Install: the app was installed from its App Store listing (called Fleeta LumenCart: AI Photos, vendor Fleeta Limited; the app is called LumenCart in the admin) through the install form, in our own tab. No terms of service box, plan choice, card or phone number was asked. The app opened on Overview with the line See your first product image in a few minutes. and a counter 0/3 successful outputs. LumenCart is an AI product photo generator, not a cart drawer or an upsell app, so the core action is generating one image. Core action: Overview, Start with one product, Studio, the product The Out of Stock Snowboard (1 source image, 80% baseline), the mode Keep product details (the default), Standard at 1 credit per image, then Generate preview, 1 credit. That is 3 clicks after the install. The app showed Generating image 1 of 1 for about 70 seconds and, at about 21:54, a Generated result with the label 99% match, the buttons Image viewer, Download, Replace in Shopify and Regenerate, and the counter 24 credits available. Credits: the Billing screen still showed 25 credits and Credits used 0 after the preview, while the Studio screen showed 24 credits available. The prices match the dossier. exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Kumo (B2B Wholesale Tools) on a Shopify development store: the install, a 20 percent price rule for customers with a tag, the preview price, the Plans page with greyed out Select buttons and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was saved in the theme and nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Kumo B2B Wholesale Tools, from Cloudlift, and says From $15/month. Free trial available., with a rating of 5.0 from 9 reviews and a launch date of 21 November 2024; it names B2B at $15 a month and PLUS at $30 a month, both with a 7-day free trial, and says all charges are billed in USD, with recurring and usage based charges every 30 days. Install was clicked at about 11:52 and asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data (customers, products, discounts, Shopify Functions, Online Store, Shopify admin). The app, called B2B Wholesale Tools in the admin, opened straight on Home with no plan screen and no Approve subscription screen. Home showed a Setup Guide at 0 / 3 completed (Enable the app, Setup your first price config, Test pricing on your store), App not enabled with a button Enable App in theme editor, and an onboarding call with Book a call, which we did not use. Core action: Setup pricing, Create pricing. We named the rule Wholesale 20 percent, type Percentage, discount 20, customer conditions Targets customers with specific tags with the tag wholesale, product conditions Applies to all products, status Active. Save gave Config saved and the rule showed as Active; the Message field filled itself with WHOLESALE_20_PERCENT. Preview product with Bundle Product #1, which the product picker lists at $1,382.31, showed $ 1,105.60 in the app. A 20 percent discount on $1,382.31 is $1,105.85, so the app preview is 25 cents lower than that; we did not find out why. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes from the install click at about 11:52:57 to the preview price at about 11:54:58, in about 10 steps. The theme editor was not used and nothing was saved in the theme; the app was not enabled in the theme, so the price was not seen in the store preview and no customer with the tag wholesale was tried. The menu also has Add Volume pricing, Add Bulk ordering, Add Minimum quantity, Forms, Submissions, Checkout and Price lists; these were not tested. Plans: the Plans page said Your current plan: DEVELOPER and You are on a development store! You are on a unlimited trail plan until this store goes live. B2B $15 a month lists Wholesale pricing, Volume pricing, Registration forms and Approval workflow; PLUS $30 a month lists All of B2B features, Product catalog assignment and Shopify plus checkout integration. The PLUS card shows two Plus features in the app, while the listing names three, including company registration. Both Select buttons were greyed out, so no Shopify approval screen was reached and nothing could be approved. Cancelling: there was no subscription to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, Uninstall; the dialog says that you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. A Reason for uninstalling is required (we chose Testing multiple apps) and feedback is optional. Not tested: a real customer with the tag wholesale in the store, volume pricing, the registration form, the approval workflow, CSV price lists, the checkout settings, the Plus features, any paid plan and the trial. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 11:56 and Shopify confirmed it; the plan and its discounts went with it. Nothing was saved in the theme. Our own tabs were closed, except one tab opened by the install button that could not be closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app preview price is 25 cents lower than a plain 20 percent of the listed price, the Select buttons are greyed out on a development store, and the price rule is only seen in the store after the app is enabled in the theme.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Dynasort (collection sorting) on a Shopify development store: the install, the free Demo plan without a card or billing screen, the first synchronisation (more than 7 minutes, where the app said about 5), the sort rule on Automated Collection (8 products) with the recipe Dynasort Default, the message that Processing had to be switched On in Settings first, the result in Shopify (the sort choice changed from Most relevant to Manually in the order of the app scores, about 8 minutes and 14 steps after the install), the switch back (Shopify stayed on Manually until the sort choice was reset by hand), the plan page with a temporary 50% discount (Basic $49, Pro $124, Enterprise $249 a month) and the uninstall, which asks for a reason. Nothing was paid or approved. Install: the app (App Store name Dynasort Collection Sorting, developer Dyna, Denver; Built for Shopify; rating 4.6 from 14 reviews) was installed from its App Store listing through the install form in our own tab. The install started at 22:12 (clock of the test computer). The permission screen said that the app needs access to view customer data, view staff and contributor data and view and edit store data; it was approved with Install. The app opened as Dynasort from Dyna, the same product as the listing, on its Plans page. Plan choice: the free Demo plan was chosen with the button Go Demo. No card and no billing screen came up. A welcome screen asked for a goal; Better merchandised collections was chosen and Build my setup plan was clicked. Wait: the screen Setting up your store said about 5 minutes remaining and Syncing 3 collections, 23 products, and 2 recent orders. It took more than 7 minutes before it said Your store is ready. Core action: the app listed the collections Hydrogen (3 products), Automated Collection (8 products) and Home page (0), with the recipe Dynasort Default, status Off and the text 0/2 Sorted. Automated Collection, a smart collection, was chosen. In Shopify it was sorted Most relevant before the test. The recipe Dynasort Default weighs Sales (Last 30 Days) (100), Sales (All Time) (50), Inventory Quantity (50), Sold Out (-100), On Sale (-20) and Variants In Stock (100), with the tie breaker Best selling and Sold out items set to Move to bottom, and Revert To (When Off) set to Most relevant. The Dynasort Status was set to Active and saved (Collection saved). The status box is a native select inside an iframe, so a mouse click could not open it; pressing Escape and then typing the first letter (A for Active, O for Off) worked. A message then said that processing is not turned on yet and that Dynasort will not auto-sort the collections otherwise. In Settings, Processing was switched from Off to On (interval 60 minutes) and saved. After Sync now and about 1 to 2 minutes, the page showed Sorting 1 minute ago (about 22:20). The first result therefore came about 8 minutes after the install, most of it waiting for the first synchronisation, in about 14 steps. Result in Shopify: the sort choice of the collection changed from Most relevant to Manually, and the order became The Multi-location Snowboard, The Multi-managed Snowboard, The Complete Snowboard, The Collection Snowboard: Liquid, then the products Hidden, Hydrogen and Compare at Price, equal to the order and scores in the app (150, 150, 127, 127 and so on). The collection holds no sold out product, so the rule Sold Out (-100) with Move to bottom was not seen at work. Switching back: the Dynasort Status was set to Off and saved, but Shopify stayed on Manually; the revert to Most relevant did not happen at once. Of our three facts, the profile kept one ('without the sale of retail bicycles'), blurred one into 'standard weekday business hours' and replaced the third with something we never said: 'By operating as a walk-in facility'. It also set the industry to 'Transportation'.

sessions.what: We did not summarise the marketing. Nextify.ai gave us Pro access for this test (disclosed here and in the video that goes with this review) and nothing else was agreed: no copy approval, and no draft shared before publication. On 7 September 2026 we generated a real ad from a product image inside that account, read the credit cost the app charges for every model it offers, and checked the pricing page both signed in and signed out. Everything below is what the product did and charged, not what the site says it does.
findings: Credits are charged per second of output, not per video. A four-second 720p clip on Seedance 2.0, the model the editor pre-selects, cost 48 credits and took the balance from 3,000 to 2,952. The app's own credit table prices that combination at 12 a second, and the Generate button reads 48 before you commit, so the arithmetic is visible if you know to look for it.

Every tier's video count assumes 20 credits a video. Starter's 1,000 credits are sold as 50 videos, Pro's 3,000 as 150 and Business's 8,000 as 400: all exactly 20 apiece, which is four seconds on the cheapest 5-credit-a-second model. On the model the editor actually opens with, Pro is 62 clips; at the 15-second maximum it is 16.

No image model costs what the image counts assume. Those counts work out at 2 credits an image on every tier, including the free one. The cheapest image model in the table is Nano Banana 2 at 1k for 7 credits, and the pre-selected GPT Image 2 is 10: the button literally reads “Generate Image 10”. Starter's “up to 500 images” is about 100.

The avatar tools are the expensive ones, and they are the reason most people arrive. UGC Product Video and Lip-sync run on HeyGen AV4 at 6.7 credits a second, identical at 720p and 1080p, over 3 to 120 seconds. A 30-second avatar ad is 201 credits and a 60-second one is 402, so a Pro month is fourteen or seven of them.

Free users cannot reach the Seedance models at all. The model configuration marks seedance-2.0, seedance-2.0-fast and seedance-2.0-mini as unavailable on the free plan, so the 50 free credits run on Kling or MiniMax with a watermark: about two three-second clips.

“In seconds” is not what happens, but “three minutes” is fair. Our four-second clip took 126 seconds from submit to finished file, against the app's own on-screen estimate of four minutes. The homepage claim “Product Image to Viral Ad in 3 Minutes” holds up; the “in seconds” line on the same page does not.

The output was accurate to the prompt. We asked for a stainless steel insulated bottle on a kitchen counter in morning light, a hand picking it up, clean styling and no text overlay, and that is what came back: 9:16, 720p, four seconds, with generated audio. Nothing in the result argued against the tool; the argument is with the pricing page.
The pricing page hides the free plan once you sign in. Signed out, Free sits at the head of the ladder; signed in, the same URL starts at Starter.

sessions.what: We created the free account and logged in; everything after that was read inside the workspace on 11 September 2026 -- the credit screen, the plans and billing screen and the upgrade panel -- alongside Bitscale's own credit documentation. Two limits worth stating plainly. We did not run an enrichment: the grid renders in a canvas our browser panel could not drive, so the per-record credit costs below come from Bitscale's published credit table and not from a meter we moved ourselves. And Bitscale is an affiliate partner of ours; their partner manager offered 2,000 bonus credits that same morning, which had not been added when we looked -- the account was on the ordinary free allowance of 200, which is what a new reader gets.
findings: The free tier runs two meters, not one, and the account screen shows both: 200 platform credits and 2,000 search credits, each resetting monthly, with the next search reset dated on the page. Enriching a record spends platform credits; finding one through Find People or Find Companies spends a search credit, one per record. A reader budgeting on "200 credits" is reading half the meter, and it is the half that runs out first.

On Free, nothing carries over. The billing screen states it twice -- "Rolled-Over Credits: Not included in the plan" and "Rollover Limit: Not included in the plan" -- so an unused month is gone rather than banked. Rollover is listed among the things the first paid plan adds, next to credit rollover, the 100+ providers, action columns beyond 20 per grid, and the inbound integrations (RB2B, Factors, Vector).

What one enriched record costs is published, and the range is the whole story: one to twelve platform credits per successful email or phone lookup, depending on how many providers the waterfall is allowed to try. An AI enrichment is one to two credits a run, a BitAgent website scrape one per query, and anything arriving through the API is free. On Growth that turns 15,000 credits into anywhere between 1,250 and 15,000 enriched contacts -- 2.3 cents each at one credit, 28 cents at twelve.

The in-app upgrade panel carries a Growth benefit the public plan cards do not mention: three hours a quarter with a GTM engineer, alongside the 15,000 credits. Worth knowing before you compare the $349 against a pure data vendor, because it is consulting time rather than volume.

The two meters are set to become convertible. Bitscale's documentation announces 1 platform credit = 10 search credits as an upcoming feature, handled manually for enterprise accounts today. Until that ships, a month where you burn the enrichment pool cannot be topped up from the search pool, however much of it is left.
