sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Ava AI on a Shopify development store, but the core action was blocked because no plan was approved: the Shopify approval screen had the test charge sentence and also an Add payment method row. Only the install permissions, the plans, the approval screen, the page Phone numbers and agents without a plan (a number stuck on Setting up) and the uninstall dialog were seen, after which the app was uninstalled. No call was made and nothing was paid. Install: the install form on the App Store listing opened in our own tab; the dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data and was approved. The start was at about 15:58 (Dutch time) and the app was installed at about 15:59 after Install app. The app opened straight on Plans and pricing, with the notice Setting up your phone number, which says the phone number of the AI agent is being provisioned. No account on the vendor site, password, demo, call or card was asked at install. The App Store listing then showed 5.0 stars and 7 reviews, where the dossier has 6 reviews and 4.7. Core action NOT DONE: the core of the app is an AI agent that answers a phone call. No plan was approved, so there was no working phone number and no call was made. Without a plan the button Turn on still opened the page Phone numbers and agents with 0 numbers, 0 agents active and 1 off, the text Setting up number, the agent Main Agent (inbound), the red text Phone number does not match shop numbers followed by nothing, and the notice Agent limit reached (all 1 inbound agent of the plan is in use). The tabs were Inbound and Outbound. The number stayed on Setting up for about 2 minutes. No agent was enabled, no call was answered and no time to a first result could be measured. Plans: the app shows three plans with a Start free trial button each. The entry plan is $29 a month with 100 minutes included, $0.10 per additional minute and 1 call at a time. The middle plan is $99 with 400 minutes, $0.08 per additional minute, 3 simultaneous calls, outbound abandoned-cart calling and a custom voice. The top plan is $499 with 1,500 minutes, $0.07 per additional minute, unlimited simultaneous calls, multiple phone numbers and priority support. Under the cards: All plans: 7 day free trial. No long-term contract. Cancel anytime. The prices and minutes agree with the App Store listing and the dossier; the number of simultaneous calls per plan (1, 3, unlimited) is new compared with the listing. Checkout: Start free trial was clicked for the entry plan. The Shopify screen Approve subscription showed the notice You will not be billed for this test charge, the message that the app bills a recurring subscription and usage charges, the plan at $29,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov, a subtotal of $29,00 plus any applicable taxes, a total of $29,00 due 24 Nov, a note that the subtotal contains only the subscription fee and that usage is charged on top, which is variable, and an App spending limit of a maximum of $200,00 USD per 30 days. The screen also had an Add payment method row, so although it carried the test charge sentence we did not approve it; no card was entered. Cancel was clicked; the screen said Charge declined and returned to the list of apps. Cancelling: no subscription ran, so nothing could be cancelled. The uninstall dialog (Settings, Apps, menu, Uninstall) says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled on 17 November and left the installed list. Not tested: the core action, a working phone number, enabling the agent, a phone call, outbound cart recovery calls, Call Logs, Integrations, Advanced, the amount at the end of the trial and the real minutes used. Clean up: the app was uninstalled; no subscription was approved, no payment method was entered and no theme change was made. Other apps were not touched. No kit records were entered.

Free trial available., with a rating of 5.0 from 243 reviews (the dossier had 232 reviews on 13 October). Install was clicked at about 11:58; the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. The Install button on the listing is a form that opens a new tab; we sent it in our own tab instead. Right after the install the Shopify Approve subscription screen came up, and after approval the app opened (Welcome to Grapevine Surveys, Setup Assistant) at about 11:59. Core action: the Setup Assistant asked What is your main goal? (we chose Understand where customers come from), Where do you want to survey customers? (Post purchase pages) and recommended the Acquisition Insight Survey with 4 questions included. After Use this template the editor said Template loaded and preloaded the questions and channels: 1 How did you first hear about us? with Social Media, Search Engine, AI Recommendation, YouTube, Influencer, Friend or Family, Podcast and Other; 2 What made you decide to buy from us today?; 3 How would you rate your website experience today?; 4 What could we improve about your website experience? The channel is Checkout app block and the display rule is The customer is new. Save gave Survey Saved. The survey page then showed Total impressions 0, Responses 0 and Response rate 0%, and Setup instructions: Make sure you have added the Grapevine checkout block to your thank you and order status pages. So the survey only appears after the checkout app block is added by hand in the checkout editor. We did NOT do that, so nothing was changed in the theme or the checkout, no test order was placed and no answer or attribution data exists. The preview in the editor showed a thank you page for an example name from the app. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes from the install click (11:58) to the saved survey (about 12:00), in 6 steps after the approval (3 assistant clicks, the template, Ok, Save). Checkout: the Approve subscription screen shows the plan Complete at $25,00 USD every 30 days, You will not be billed for this test charge., You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., a subtotal of $25,00 plus any applicable taxes and a total of $25,00 due 1 Dec. An Add payment method row was visible but no card was needed; we approved this test charge, which cost nothing. The price matches the listing. Plan: the Your Plan page shows only one plan, Complete Plan at $25 /month, with Unlimited responses, Revenue reports, Klaviyo integration, Google Analytics integration, POS surveys and more; there is no free tier. Cancelling: Settings, Apps, Uninstall opens the dialog Uninstall Grapevine Surveys? with the notes that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. A Reason for uninstalling is required: the Uninstall button stays grey until a reason is chosen (we chose Testing multiple apps). Not tested: adding the checkout app block and placing a test order (so no real answer and no channel report), Klaviyo, GA4, MCP, one-click email surveys, POS, translation, changing the Display Rules, and the Book a call and Chat with us options. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test and Shopify confirmed it; the saved survey went with it. No theme or checkout change was made and the test charge ended with the app. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The saved survey does not show to buyers until the checkout app block is added by hand in the checkout editor, and the app has one paid plan and no free tier.

The start screen showed the banner We are indexing your products and the usage Plan usage: 0 of 1 feeds, 0 of 100 products, 0 of 300 variants. A promo popup for another product of the vendor had to be closed. There was no plan screen and no Shopify approval screen at install. Core action: Create feed, search Heureka, Select (the market heureka.cz). The app said Saved and regenerated. The feed card says Heureka Live, Heureka, US, en, shows a feed link, Products 12, Variants / items 18, Unlisted / warnings 5 / 36 and Last opened by a service: No opens recorded. Feed preview shows XML with SHOP and SHOPITEM and the fields ITEM_ID, PRODUCTNAME, URL, IMGURL, PRICE_VAT, MANUFACTURER, PRODUCTNO, CONDITION, DESCRIPTION, ITEMGROUP_ID and DELIVERY_DATE; for The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard the PRICE_VAT is 949.95. Feed issues (click on 5 / 36): unlisted Product excluded: Out of stock; critical Product not published in Online Store or Store is Protected (your product is not published to the online store or your store is password protected); critical Standardized product type missing. Not done: loading the feed in Heureka itself, Glami, a second market. No one has opened the feed, so we do not know if Heureka accepts it. Plans: the Billing page shows Current plan Free ($0): All time free, Up to 100 products, Up to 300 variants, Only primary Shopify market, Only primary language, Create 1 Feed. The usage there says Imported 14 products and 23 variants with 0 remaining, while the feed itself counts 12 products and 18 variants; we did not find out why. Cancel subscription is greyed out on Free. Basic $9.99 a month has 7 days free trial, Up to 1 000 products, Up to 2 000 variants, Product Metafields and Metaobjects, Shop Metafields, Ability to use Shopify markets, translations and inventory levels, Hourly products update, Integrations (heureka, zbozi, favi, biano) and Create up to 5 Feeds. Advanced $19.99 has 2 500 products, 5 000 variants and up to 10 feeds. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test and no longer shows in the list of installed apps; the feed went with it. Plan Basic was not approved and no theme change was saved. Our own tabs were closed. The apps list with an account name was not kept as evidence. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on the 14-day trial: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We could not create a ticket ourselves without connecting a mailbox, so we sent two test tickets with made-up details through SupportBee's own contact form, solving its reCAPTCHA himself. On those we added an internal comment, labels and a snippet, then edited the snippet and inserted it again. Nothing was sent to a customer.
findings: The '+ Ticket' action is blocked until a mailbox is connected: 'Please connect an email address to create tickets. New tickets can't be created without a connected email address.' Incoming tickets through SupportBee's contact form worked without that connection.

Admin > Emails > Add email offers only 'Gmail / Google Workspace' and 'Microsoft Outlook / Office 365', through a connection that copies your support mail into SupportBee. For any other provider the screen says 'Please contact us at support@supportbee.com'.

The contact form is the way in without a mailbox. It has a reCAPTCHA on by default, and setting 'Show captcha' to No did not stay saved. Both test tickets arrived as 'Unanswered', source 'Web Ticket', with a customer profile (name and email).

Internal comments sit in the right-hand sidebar, apart from the reply box. A comment was saved, the ticket stayed 'Unanswered', and SupportBee then assigned the ticket to the person who wrote the comment.

A label without a colour was not created and no error appeared (two tries, the list stayed at 1 label); with a colour it worked at once. Labels set from the ticket header showed in the list view and the sidebar.

A snippet ('Lila heeft 37 dagen garantie.', 'Lila has a 37-day warranty') was found with 'Search snippets' above the reply box and inserted as a draft. After we changed 37 to 41 and clicked Update Snippet, the second ticket showed the new text straight away and inserted 'Lila heeft 41 dagen garantie.' ('Lila has a 41-day warranty')
The trial opened with an example ticket ('Sample Ticket: How to use SupportBee'), a default label IMPORTANT and an example snippet ('Send your browser details').
not_tested: A real Gmail or Outlook connection, and sending email to customers
KBee (the knowledge base), the customer portal, reports, teams and filters
What happens when the 14-day trial ends

sessions.what: We did not read the docs and summarise them: PartnerStack is the platform our own affiliate operation runs on. We manage 58 partner programmes through it, pull the Partner API v2 on a schedule, and stamp sub-IDs across 704 pages of our own site. PartnerStack is also an affiliate partner of ours, we earn 15% of every sale for a year on anyone who signs up through our link, which is why the findings below are things we measured against our own records rather than claims from their marketing.
findings: A record in the customers endpoint is a tracked click, not a signup. One plain curl on a tracking link produced a customer record one second later, has_paid false, with no browser and no account. Records surface in the API about five minutes after the click, so allow ten before concluding a test did nothing.

Clicks arrive without a source. There is no referring-URL field in the partnership data, so the platform can tell you a link was clicked and never which page produced it. We had to build sub-ID stamping across our own pages to answer that question ourselves.

Commission terms do not come from the API. offers.base_rate is returned null on every partnership we hold. The readable source is PartnerStack's own public directory at market.partnerstack.com, and it sometimes contradicts the vendor's own affiliate page, which is worth knowing before you quote a rate to anyone.

Programme status lags the reality by days. One partner sent us a welcome email with a working tracking link on 7 August; the API still read application-denied and only turned active somewhere between 13 and 18 August. Treat the vendor's email as the leading indicator and the API status as the one that catches up.
The earned-commission endpoints are the weakest part. rewards and transactions did not return usable data for us, so what you have actually been paid is a dashboard question rather than an API one.

Partner replies break email threading. A partner answers inside the PartnerStack dashboard and the platform sends that on as a fresh message from hello@partnerstackmail.com, with a new Message-ID and no reference to the mail it is answering. Any automation of yours that matches replies to threads will not match these.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on the 7-day trial that starts with a new account, without a card: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We gave the Lyro AI agent five questions and answers about a made-up shop, asked it ten questions in the Playground, two it could not know, and changed one answer to see how fast it followed. The chat widget was not installed.
findings: Sign-up requires a website URL ('Can't be empty!'). Within minutes Tidio read 71 pages of the site we entered into Lyro's knowledge on its own. The source list can delete or set an audience in bulk, but excluding a source without deleting it is one source at a time. Before testing our five Q&As we deleted all 71 website sources Tidio had imported automatically, so the answers were checked against our test knowledge alone.
Usage and plan showed 'AI conversations 0/50' marked 'Lifetime quota' for Lyro. After 13 Playground questions it still read 0 / 50: Playground questions do not count.
A CSV with the columns Question and Answer was accepted as it was (5 Q&As).

Lyro answered nine of the ten fact and paraphrase questions fully. For the warranty question it repeated the correct 37-day term but did not determine whether one month fell within it. Each answer was marked 'AI response based on your data sources'.
Asked whether a fault after one month was covered by a 37-day warranty, Lyro gave the 37 days but said 'I'm not able to determine whether one month falls within that period'.
For the two questions our data did not answer (Sunday opening, return costs) it said it had no information and offered 'Talk to a person'; it made nothing up.
After we changed the warranty from 37 to 41 days, the next question was answered with 41 days.
not_tested: Real visitor conversations through an installed chat widget, and so the use of the 50 Lyro conversations
Handing over to a person, Flows, and the email and social channels
Lyro Actions, Procedures and Guidance
What happens when the 7-day trial ends and the account moves to the free plan
Languages other than English

On 17 November 2026 the session tested Storista on a Shopify development store only in part: the install, the empty dashboard on the free plan, the onboarding with its three sources (Instagram, TikTok, Upload files), the plan page with Starter at $15, Growth at $49 and Scale at $199, and the Starter approval screen (it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence, so nothing was approved). The app was uninstalled afterwards. Nothing was paid and nothing was saved in the theme. Install: the app was installed through the install form in our own tab at 16:55; the dialog Install app asked for access to customer data, staff data and store data, and the app was installed at 16:56. The App Store name is Storista Shoppable Videos UGC; in the admin the app is called Storista (by Storista LLC). The admin was in English. After the install the app opened straight on Welcome to Storista with three steps (Choose source, Import and Tag, Embed); no payment and no account on the vendor site were needed, and the dashboard said You're on Free. Core action, importing a video and placing a widget: this was NOT achieved and no result was measured. The onboarding asks Where should we get your videos from? with the choices Instagram, TikTok and Upload files. Instagram and TikTok ask for a username and a tick box with the text that you have all rights and permissions to import content from that account; the tick box was not ticked because we have no account of our own to import from. Upload files says it accepts .mp4 and .mov, maximum 10 videos. The app runs in a cross-origin iframe on the vendor domain, and the file upload tool of the tester could not reach the file field there. That is a limit of the test tool and not a fault of the app. The Media Library was empty (Click Import content to add content) and Recent widgets said You don't have any widgets yet. Free is $0 with Unlimited videos, Unlimited views, manual import from Instagram and TikTok, manual product videos, one product per video, Shop app integration and Storista branding. Starter adds auto-sync, multiple products per video, GEO/SEO optimization, Shop app integration, import by URL, upload files up to 1GB, manual captions uploads and removal of the branding. Growth adds AI Smart Product Tagging, smart videos to PDP, advanced analytics, Auto captions in 60 languages and A/B tests. Scale adds API and webhooks, multiple stores support and VIP support. Differences with the dossier: the dossier says Growth has auto captions in 40 languages, and the plan page of the app says Auto captions 60 languages; the dossier notes that the vendor FAQ says the free plan covers 10 videos while the plan list says unlimited videos, and the onboarding says maximum 10 videos for one upload, so which statement governs was not settled because no video was uploaded. Nothing was paid. Listing and install: the App Store listing MigrationPro: Store Migration shows a rating of 5.0 (190) and Free to install. Additional charges may apply. The dossier said (5 October) that the listing had been withdrawn; it is now installable. The install button opened a pop-up to the Shopify grant screen for MP - Store Migration & Import with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved at 14:51. After the install the app opened straight on an external dashboard, app.migrationpro.io, logged in through Shopify, with no separate account asked. A message Finish setting up your account (confirm a notification email and choose a company type) was not followed. A vendor live chat widget opened by itself and showed messages; we sent nothing. Core action, a demo migration, about 2 minutes 10 seconds from the install (14:51 to about 14:53:40) and more than 12 steps, partly because we had to make a file and invent a source address: Create New Migration offers 52 source platforms (among them WooCommerce, PrestaShop, Wix and CSV); for most platforms a real source URL and a connector file (mp_connector.zip, to upload by FTP) are needed, which was not possible without a source store. We chose the source CSV, which asks for a Source Store URL (required) and CSV files (Categories, Products, Product Variants, Customers, Orders, Order Items, Blog Posts, Blog Comments, CMS Pages, Discounts). There is no built-in demo or test source. We used a Products.csv that we made ourselves with 2 made-up products (Demo Mug and Demo Shirt) and the address https://example.com as source URL; no login details were entered. In the Configure step we ticked Products. Paid options: Migrate Only Active Products ($39), Migrate Content Images from Products, Categories, CMS pages and Blog Posts ($29), Implement 301 Redirects in Target Store Post-Migration ($29), Convert Categories to Shopify Automated Collections ($29), Set Out-of-Stock Product Quantity to 100 in Target Store ($19) and Calculate Product Price with Tax ($39); free options: Target Store Data Reset, Generate Product Variants from Option Combinations and Consolidate Short and Full Descriptions; none was switched on. The CSV Headers Mapping filled in name, description and price by itself. The button Next: Run Free Demo Migration was pressed at 14:53:31 and after about 10 seconds the page said Demo migration complete. Please review your data and proceed with full migration. with the table Products 2/2. In the Shopify admin, Demo Shirt and Demo Mug appeared as Active products, with our store name as vendor. This is a demo of two made-up products from a CSV with an invented source address; a real migration from a real source store was not tested. Plans and checkout: there is no Shopify subscription screen, no Approve subscription and no test charge; payment runs outside Shopify. The checkout page of the migration shows Entities $29, Enabled Additional Migration Options $0, Additional development $0, Order total $29, the note This is one-time payment only, a Discount code field, and the payment methods Credit card (Pay with credit card via Stripe) or PayPal (Pay with your PayPal account) with a Place order button, which we did not press because it is a real payment. The price depends on the number of records: 2 products gave $29; the pricing page has a calculator (products, customers, orders) that we did not use. The All-In-One Migration Package (A dedicated Personal Assistant will handle all aspects) is priced at $300 with Estimated time - 1 day and starts with a Consultation with the vendor experts; we did not go further because it means a conversation. Cancelling: there is no subscription to cancel, because the payment is one-time. The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps and Uninstall; the dialog says that a request will be sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information, and asks for a reason and optional feedback; we gave Testing multiple apps at 14:58 and the app left the installed list. Not tested: a real migration from a source store, 301 redirects, images, customers and orders, Smart Sync, the payment, the All-In-One package with its consultation, the live chat and confirming the notification email. Clean up: the two demo products Demo Shirt and Demo Mug are still Active in the store and were not deleted; the app was uninstalled; a helper file with the CSV was kept outside the project; one pop-up tab of the first install attempt could not be closed with our tools. No kit records were entered.

A privacy window with a pre-ticked newsletter box appeared at the start and was not accepted; it was hidden only for the screenshots. The Shopify approval screen was not reached, no trial was started and nothing was paid. The app was uninstalled afterwards. The vendor app opened on its own site in Dutch (Installatie bezig, then App is succesvol geinstalleerd and U bent op het Free abonnement); no separate account or password was asked, because the account was created automatically from the Shopify store. The cookie banner was declined. We switched the language of the app to EN. Privacy window: at the start in the app a window appeared with the title Your privacy is important to us, links to the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use and Terms and Conditions, a pre-ticked newsletter sign-up and an Accept button. It was NOT accepted, because accepting terms is outside the permission of the tester; the feed and the preview were already visible behind it. For the screenshots the window was hidden in our own tab with display none, so the screenshots show the app without that window. Hiding it is not an acceptance, and the real first screen includes the window. Core action, a product feed for Google Shopping: after the install this took 4 clicks (choose the channel Google Shopping, the type Product - USA, Canada, the format XML, and Add channel profile) and about 2 minutes (about 17:03). The feed has a public address on the vendor domain; fetching it without a login gave HTTP 200 and 16258 bytes. The XML held 18 items. In 16 of the 18 items the g:id field was empty (only two items, with ids like sku-hosted-1 and sku-managed-1, had one), the g:description field was empty in most items and identifier_exists was FALSE. This is a store with a handful of test products, so the empty fields may come from how the test store was filled, and we did not check the cause. No Google Merchant Center or marketplace account was connected and nothing was submitted. sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested BackupMaster on a Shopify development store: the install, the plan page, and the free Agency Plan (all features for 3 months), which started the first backup by itself. The products (23 items) were backed up in about 1 minute, Collections, Metafield definitions and Metaobjects finished after that, and Themes and Assets were still running. The version screen of one product was looked at, and no restore was run. Essentials, Pro and Plus were greyed out because this store is unpublished, so there was no Shopify payment screen and nothing was paid. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the app was installed through the App Store form in our own tab at 17:08; the dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. The app is called BackupMaster Backups in the admin, the admin was in English, and the welcome screen said that the app backs up the store data and allows you to restore it, and to choose a subscription plan to get started. Plans: the plan page says the pricing plans are based on the average number of orders, and that this store averaged 0 orders per month over the past three months. The Agency Plan is exclusively for agencies and developers with partner development stores, with full feature access for 3 months, a partner program (inquire for details), and the note that after the store is transferred the owner must choose a plan to keep using the app. Essentials is $19.00 USD a month for up to 300 orders a month, Pro is $39.00 USD a month for up to 600 orders a month and Plus is $79.00 USD a month for up to 1500 orders a month (a list lets you pick the order band); there is a Monthly and an Annual switch that was not looked at. All three paid plans had a greyed out Choose this plan button with a tooltip: This plan isn't available for unpublished stores. So none of them could be chosen on this store, and the paid plans, their trial and their billing were not seen. Core action, a backup of the products: we chose the Agency Plan (Choose this plan). There was no Shopify payment screen, no card and no charge to approve; the app went straight to its dashboard, and the first backup started by itself. It showed Backing up your store, Backing up Products and 5 of 23 items backed up. After about 1 minute (about 17:09, 4 clicks after the install) it said Products: 23 items backed up with the label Finished. Then Collections said 3 items backed up (Finished), Metafield definitions 22 items backed up (Finished) and Metaobjects 2 items backed up (Finished); Themes and Assets were still running (30 of 946) when we stopped looking, so a full backup was not seen to the end. One screenshot (02) was taken while Metafield definitions were still in progress, before the notes say they finished. Looking at the backup: the product list shows Last edited for each product and a View versions button. For the product Demo Shirt the screen showed the Current item on the left and the Backed-up version 2026-11-17 5:09 PM on the right and a button Restore to this version, greyed out because nothing differed; a banner on top said Bulk operation in progress. The dashboard also has Bulk restore. NO restore was run: it can overwrite the test data of the store. Differences with the dossier: none found. The prices and the order bands of Essentials ($19, 300 orders), Pro ($39, 600 orders) and Plus ($79, 1500 orders) are those of the dossier, and Agency is free for partner development stores with all features for three months, as the dossier says. The dossier also gives a 7-day free trial for each paid tier and yearly prices; neither was seen, because the paid plans could not be chosen. The dossier says the backups are daily; only the first backup was seen. Checkout: NOT reached. The Agency Plan has no payment step and the paid plans are not available for an unpublished store, so no Shopify approval screen, price total, tax or renewal term was observed. Cancelling: no paid subscription was started, so nothing could be cancelled. The way to stop is uninstalling the app: Settings, Apps, the three dots menu, Uninstall opens a dialog with the text that you can no longer use the app and that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required (we chose Testing multiple apps). Not tested: a restore, Clone store, Export, Import, Google Drive sync, any paid plan and the finish of the Themes and Assets backup. No theme change was made and nothing was changed in the store. Clean up: the app was uninstalled at 17:11 through Settings, Apps and it disappeared from Installed; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested StoreFAQ on a Shopify development store on the Free plan: the install, three test FAQs, the FAQ schema switch, the preview of the app page /a/faqs, the plan cards and the Professional approval screen (not approved). The preview said that no FAQs were found until a group was made, because FAQs without a group do not show; after the group Shipping and returns was made the question and its answer showed in the preview, about 4 minutes after the install. The structured data was not seen, nothing was paid, and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form on the App Store page was opened in our own tab at about 17:40 and the permissions of the app were approved at about 17:41; the app opened on the page Choose the perfect plan for your store. The admin was in English. The version of the app is 3.7.7 by Storeware. Plan: the Free plan ($0) was chosen at once, with no card, no phone number and no account on the vendor site. Core action, an FAQ page: at about 17:42 the first FAQ, How long does shipping take?, was made in the group Ungrouped and the message FAQ created appeared. In the setup guide Enable FAQ Schema was clicked, which gave the message FAQ Schema toggled., and the page Settings then shows Enable FAQ Schema with the label On. A second FAQ, What is your return policy?, was also made as Ungrouped. Result: the preview of the app page /a/faqs in the theme editor said Sorry, No FAQs found. The app gives the reason: if you keep the FAQ group as Ungrouped it will not show on the front end. FAQs without a group are therefore invisible. A group Shipping and returns was made (the first try hung on a spinner, the second worked) and a third FAQ, Do you ship internationally?, was put in it. At about 17:44 the preview showed the group and, opened, the answer Yes, we ship to most countries. Shipping costs show at checkout. So the first visible result took about 4 minutes and about 15 steps from the install, and only after the group was made; the app does not warn about the missing group when an FAQ is saved. The address of the FAQ page is an app proxy path, /a/faqs, on the store domain. FAQ schema: only the On switch was seen. The structured data (JSON-LD) in the output of the page was NOT read, because the preview is a cross-origin frame and the store has a password. Whether the FAQ schema is really output, and whether it is valid, was not tested. Plans: the plan cards in the app (Black Friday offer, code BFCMSALE40, 40 percent off) show Professional $7.99 struck through to $4.79 a month, Growth $14.99 to $8.99 and Enterprise $49.99 to $29.99. Free: Up to 100 FAQ Page Views and AI Conversations 25 (Lifetime). Professional: Monthly plan includes 500 page views, extra usage billed at $0.0075/view. Growth: 2,000 page views, extra usage billed at $0.0075/view. Both: $0.30 per extra conversation after limit. Enterprise: Unlimited usage of page views. Billing for page views and conversations is capped at $7.99, $14.99 and $49.99 a month individually. Differences with the dossier: the dossier gives an overage of $0.0159 a view on Professional and $0.0075 on Growth; the app shows $0.0075 a view on Professional as well, so the Professional overage in the app is lower than in the dossier. The Black Friday offer BFCMSALE40 is not in the dossier. Checkout: Subscribe now on Professional opened a dialog with Subtotal $7.99, Discount: (BFCMSALE40) -$3.2 and Total $4.79, and then the Shopify screen Approve subscription: plan professional-monthly, $7,99 struck through and $4,79 USD every 30 days, an App spending limit of a maximum of $15,98 USD per 30 days (twice the $7.99 cap), a badge 40% off 1 charge, a row Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button, with Total $4,79 due 17 Nov plus any applicable taxes. The sentence about a test charge was NOT on the screen and a payment method had to be added, so nothing was approved; no card was entered. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so nothing could be cancelled; the way to stop is to remove the app in Settings, Apps, which was done after the test. Not tested: the two Ungrouped FAQs (they stay invisible until they get a group), the AI chatbot and Instant Answer, Write with AI (it asks for an OpenAI key), Live Chat, import and export of FAQs as CSV, multilingual FAQs on the Professional plan, what happens when the limit of 100 page views is passed, and the JSON-LD of the FAQ schema. Clean up: the theme was not saved; the app made no page in the store, because /a/faqs is an app proxy that disappears when the app is removed; the app was uninstalled afterwards. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

The draft was left as a hidden draft and nothing was published. It had no store product links and no featured image, and it held some figures with no source. Name: the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/tapita-ai-seo-blog-builder) is now titled Tapita AEO/GEO AI Blog, listed earlier as Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder (the dossier name). Developer Tapita, Built for Shopify, Pricing Free, rating 4.9 from 493 reviews on the listing today (494 in our test on 17 Nov 2026), read at about 23:11. In the Shopify admin the app is called Tapita GEO & AI Blog and its welcome page says Welcome to Tapita AI Blog Builder: the same product under three names. The review should say Tapita AEO/GEO AI Blog, formerly Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder. Install: the install form was sent in our own tab at about 23:12 and Install app was clicked. The app asks to View staff and contributor data (store owner, blog contributors) and to View and edit store data (Products, Online Store). No payment screen came up, no separate Tapita account, password or Google login was needed: the app opened straight in the Shopify admin on the free level. Onboarding: the app started a nine step analysis of the store on its own. A pop-up Business Information asked for a Business Description and a Target Customer, which were filled with a short test text about snowboards. An Ideas Suggestions list (55 credits, 2 posts, scheduled for 11/18 to 11/25) offered Generate Blog Posts Now and Bulk Generate (2 posts); neither was used because it would schedule posts. A banner warned that the app should be opened regularly to keep processes active because of expiring Shopify access tokens. Core action: Content Studio, Create content, Blog / Informational, Create with AI opened the form Create blog post, marked 55 AI credits: language English (US), writing style, voice tone and complexity on Default, Include Summary Block on, Auto-apply FAQPage schema on, our own keyword (how to choose a snowboard for beginners), the post title How to Choose a Snowboard as a Beginner, a publish date of 17 Nov 2026, a reminder to refresh after 30 days and Generate featured image off. It took 6 clicks plus typing. Generate was clicked at about 23:13; the app showed four progress steps (Article Outline & Structure, SEO Metadata & Search Intent, Section Content Writing, Layout, Accordion & Featured Image) and said Article generated successfully! after about 45 seconds (about 23:14). The post was a Draft with Visibility Hidden. The dashboard then said Published posts 0 / 1, 1 posts scheduled and GEO health score 100%. Nothing was published and Publish was not clicked. Shopify, Content, Blog posts stayed empty: the draft lives inside the app. What the draft contained: a summary block at the top, H2 and H3 headings, three comparison tables (board type, rider profile, new, used or rental), bullet and numbered lists and an FAQ accordion titled What Beginners Should Know Before Choosing a Snowboard, with the FAQPage schema switched on (the generated code on a published page was not inspected). The advice read as generally sound and careful (Treat the chart as the starting point; weight and size chart instead of the chin height rule; flex roughly 3-5 on a 10-point scale). We saw no invented brands, prices or product names. We did see specific figures with no source, for example 152-156 cm for a 160 pound rider, a stance of +15 front and -5 back and US men's size 9 and under; they were not checked. The draft had no links to store products because nothing was inserted with Insert a product into the post, and no featured image (the box was empty). The headings repeat the search phrase almost word for word, for example How to Choose a Snowboard for Beginners: Start With Your Riding Goals, some are long and contain a dash, and the draft has many headings and tables but little voice of its own. SEO audit in the app: SEO score 78, Common errors (0), Other errors (6, among them a missing favicon and an article length message) and Good (14); a GEO tab is next to it. findings: After upload, every column of our file started as 'DO NOT IMPORT', including obvious ones such as First Name and Email, so each column has to be mapped by hand. Both contacts then came in with their addresses.

Re-importing with the Contact ID mapped created no duplicates, but a changed address did not replace the old one: the contact ended up with both addresses, marked 'Other' and NOT VERIFIED, and the list kept showing the old address as primary.

Export Contacts lets you choose the columns and downloads an XLSX straight away. Both test contacts came back complete with their Contact ID; the file has a title row above the headers, and Excel shows the Contact ID in scientific notation.

No card was asked. A banner offered 25% off for six months when subscribing within the first 15 days; the app did not show a trial end date. The new account already held a contact for Aplos itself, and showed banners for other products of the parent company.
not_tested: Fund accounting and bookkeeping entries
Bank and payment connections
Donations and online giving
What happens after the trial
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

sessions.what: accessiBe's free accessScan scanner, not the paid accessWidget overlay this review prices. We built two versions of the same small landing page: one with 20 accessibility errors we placed on purpose and wrote down beforehand (missing page language and title, images without text alternatives, unlabelled form fields, low contrast, a skipped heading level, a table without header cells, a clickable div, a positive tabindex, an unlabelled iframe and more), and a twin with all 20 fixed. We scanned both and, as a reference, ran the free open-source checker axe-core 4.10.2 over the same two pages.
findings: The verdict was right both ways. The broken page came back 'Non-compliant' with 14 issues (10 critical, 3 serious, 1 moderate); the fixed twin came back 'Accessible'.

Of our 20 planted errors, the full report identified 7 correctly: the missing language, the empty title, the unlabelled button, the unlabelled iframe, aria-hidden on a link, the missing main landmark and the clickable div. An eighth, a link containing only an image without alt text, was flagged under the wrong diagnosis: the report called the image decorative and advised hiding it, which would leave the link with no name at all. axe-core found 13 of the same 20.

What it missed: the form had an email field and a dropdown without labels and a phone field labelled only by its placeholder, and the report's Forms category read 0. It also missed the image with no alt text, the alt text that was a filename, the low-contrast text, the skipped heading level, the table without header cells and the positive tabindex. For the filename alt text and the 'click here' link the report has a rule, but marked it 'Relevant: No'.

The report contradicts itself on the title: the empty <title> fails one rule ('titles aren't descriptive') and passes another ('missing page title'). It also flagged the correctly hidden icon inside our button and the page's <body> element.

The scan itself is free, but the breakdown sits blurred behind a form. To see it you give your name and a business email and tick: 'I agree to enter into a contract with accessiBe under its Terms of Service, under which accessiBe will process my personal data for marketing purposes, for 6 months'. The same page says 'Always free'. The report arrived by email within a minute, with buttons to sign up and to install the widget.
It would not scan W3C's own before-and-after accessibility demo ('The scanner doesn't have permission to access this URL'), which is why we used pages of our own.
not_tested: accessWidget itself, any paid tier, accessFlow, multi-page scans and real sites
One page pair is a spot check of the free scanner, not a verdict on the product line.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on a new Free account (we created it and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser; nothing was paid and no card was entered): we made the same small infographic, titled TESTHAVEN with the figures 12, 8 and 20, once from a free template and once with the Pikto AI generator, changed its colour and font, and downloaded until the free downloads ran out.
findings: Free gives 2 PNG downloads per account, not per design: the download panel went from '2 Downloads Left' to 1 and then 0 across two different designs. A third try opened 'You have run out of free downloads.' with 'Choose your plan', and no file came.

PNG is the only free file format. PDF and PowerPoint carry a BUSINESS label, and choosing PDF opened an upgrade window straight away. Normal, Medium and High quality were all open on Free; a transparent background asked for an upgrade.

The AI generator was not reliable for us. The button said 1 credit, two of our three attempts ended in an error ('Probeer later opnieuw', try again later), and the balance went from 60 to 57 for one finished infographic. Whether each failed attempt cost a credit or the one that worked cost three is not clear from what we saw.

The AI kept all three numbers ('Appels: 12', 'Peren: 8', 'Bananen: 20': apples, pears, bananas) but extended our title to 'TESTHAVEN Fruit Inventaris' and added sentences of its own ('Perfect voor een gezonde snack of in een taart', 'Perfect for a healthy snack or in a cake'). The app warns that AI content may be inaccurate.
In the AI design's export the heading 'TOTAAL' in the closing block overlapped the paragraph below it, leaving part of it unreadable, and the photo next to 'Peren: 8' showed no pears.
Both downloads arrived as separate PNG files, not a ZIP: 800x1807 px (315 KB) for the template design and 800x2075 px (552 KB) for the AI design, each with our title and the three correct numbers.

The free template we used ('Food Safety Starts With You') was quick to edit: double-click, select all, type, and it saved automatically. Its other sections and English paragraphs stay in the design until you delete them, and many other infographic templates carry a PREMIUM label.

Changing the background colour (palette plus hex field) and the title font worked on Free; 'Create Brand Colors' and 'Upload Brand Font' asked for an upgrade. The app also sells one-off AI credit packs, from $20 for 2,000 credits to $200 for 25,000.
not_tested: Whether 'Download as pages' gives a ZIP, and whether that costs one download or more
When the 60 free AI credits reset
The paid plans (Pro and Business), PDF and PowerPoint export, and the Brand Kit
AI video, image generation and the AI image tools (upscaler, background remover)
Moving layout blocks, and charts and maps in the editor
Whether the AI generator is more stable with an English prompt

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested MeetGeek in the account that we made: a 42 second two voice recording uploaded on the free Basic plan was analyzed in about 2 minutes (the page says 10-15 minutes), the transcript was nearly word for word with the two voices split, and all three action items came out with the right owner and deadline, with one owner assumed and two reasons added that the recording does not contain. The Plans page offers the 14-day free trial on Business only, while the dossier says Pro. Only one short English meeting was tried, no calendar or bot was connected, and no trial or payment was started. Account and start: we made the MeetGeek account before the test, through a social login, on the free Basic plan. The test started at 08:44 in our own browser tab on the onboarding page. The onboarding already stood at STEP 2 OF 3 CAPTURE, so step 1 had been done by us and its role and team size questions were neither seen nor answered. The interface was already in English. The dossier names three audiences, consultants and reps on many client calls, sales reps recording several calls a day and teams with noisy or multilingual calls, and no alternatives. Onboarding: step 2 offers Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar with Connect buttons and the choice between Send an Agent (joins as a guest) and Record without a Bot; no calendar was connected and Continue without calendar was clicked, so no bot was started. Step 3 (Meet your skills, configured for Product) had a Meeting Summary skill and three agents switched on by default, and three options (Recording format, Send summary email and Notetaker name) behind a lock for paid plans. Finish was clicked at about 08:45. The next page, Upcoming Meetings, asked to connect a calendar and offered a test drive with an AI agent, which was not used because it would start a bot. A pop-up and a banner offered Black Friday 30% off Pro and Business with a code for Free plan users until 30 November; the pop-up was closed. Core action, own recording: a test file of 42 seconds with two computer voices talking about a made-up project (m4a, 174 KB) was made on purpose. On Uploads, the file was chosen through the hidden file field after Send summary email had been switched off (4 steps: open the page, switch the mail off, choose the file; processing starts by itself and there is no start button). Meeting language was Auto-detect and Meeting template General meeting. The page says Max 4h per recording and Processing takes 10-15 mins depending on the size of the recording. The upload was at 08:45 with the status Analyzing; at the next check, about 08:47, it was Analyzed, so about 2 minutes for 42 seconds of audio against the 10-15 minutes on the page (for a very short file). The title was made by the app: Harbor Lights Launch Readiness. The meeting page has the tabs Summary, Conversation, Insights, Context and Search, a Share button and Regenerate summary. Transcript: nearly word for word, with the two voices split as Speaker_00 and Speaker_01 and time stamps at 00:00:00, 00:00:06, 00:00:14, 00:00:23 and 00:00:30. The labels were not tied to the names spoken in the recording, but the summary picked the names up from the way the speakers addressed each other. One slip: the transcript says I sent the pricing proposal on Monday where the voice said I send. Summary and Next Steps: the summary confirmed the launch date (Friday, 12 December) and the budget stated as 12,000 euros. Next Steps listed the bugs to fix (owner Sam, Wednesday, 10 December), the pricing proposal (owner Alex, Monday, 8 December), a budget check (owner Alex marked as requested, no separate deadline specified) and the final review booking (owner Sam, Thursday, 11 December). All three action items match the script. The app gave the budget check to Alex on its own assumption; nobody had been named, but the summary marks it as requested and gives no deadline. Two reasons were added that the recording does not contain: that the final review is one day before the launch date to allow last checks, and that something is done to align client expectations; the AI Insights add that calendar invites and client confirmation should be recorded. The euro sign was derived from the spoken word euros and is right. Plans, read up to the Checkout button: the Plans page showed 0h used and 3h remaining, Manage billing and Your Current Plan on Basic. Yearly view (the default): Basic Free, Pro $9.99, Business $17, Enterprise Custom; monthly view: Pro $15.99 and Business $27; the switch says Yearly -38%. Basic lists 3 hours of transcription a month, 3 months transcript storage, 1 month audio storage, Upload your own audio or video, Transcription in 100+ languages and API and MCP for Claude and ChatGPT. Pro lists 20 hours of transcription a month, 1 year transcript storage, 6 months audio storage, $0.50 per extra hour, downloads and exports and admin user management. Business lists unlimited transcription, 12 months video storage, rules to skip meetings and recording consent notifications. The button Start 14-day Free Trial is only on Business; Pro has no trial button, while the dossier says a 14-day free trial runs on Pro. A line offers 30% off for non-profits and edu. Black Friday: 30% off Pro or Business with a code, for Free plan users, until 30 November. The summary bar showed 0 seats total and $0 a month with a Checkout button that was not clicked; nothing was filled in. Differences with the dossier: the trial. The dossier says A 14-day free trial runs on Pro, but the Plans page offers the 14-day trial on Business only. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, no trial was started, no card, total with tax or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: the account is on the free plan with no subscription, so there was nothing to cancel; Settings, Account offers Deactivate account, which was not clicked, and paid plans are cancelled through Manage billing on Plans, which was not opened. The data storage location shows Europe (EU). Not tested: calendar connection, a bot in a real meeting, recording without a bot from the desktop, the Chrome extension, integrations, the mobile app, paying or starting the trial, accuracy with noise, accents or other languages, search across several meetings, AI Chat, Slack and CRM, and the role and team questions of onboarding step 1. Clean up: the test recording was deleted (Uploads showed No files yet); no mail was sent, no calendar or other connection was made, and the account stays on the free plan. The click on See meeting opened a second tab that could not be closed afterwards. No kit records were entered. The settings page was not photographed because it shows the account mail address.

sessions.what: We did not stop at the marketing. On 25 September 2026 we opened a free Jibble account (organisation 'AIBM hands-on test', web browser only), clocked in and out, invited a second user, exported a timesheet and opened the upgrade screen without buying anything. Nothing was agreed with Jibble about this test. Everything below is what the product did and showed, not what the site says.
findings: The account lands on Free at €0, marked as the selected plan, with a 14-day trial of the paid features running alongside it. During those two weeks nothing is locked, so what you see in week one is more than Free keeps.

The price table exists, just not on the public site. The upgrade button opens four plans with annual and monthly prices (euros, excluding VAT, as shown from the Netherlands): Free €0; Essential €1.79 or €2.99; Growth €3.79 or €4.99; Pro €6.79 or €9.29 per user a month. No demo form and no sales call in between.

Jibble's own plan comparison, one click further, answers what Free excludes: no timesheet approval workflow, no automatic break deductions or custom pay periods, no smart reminders, alerts or automatic clock-out, no groups, one admin, two locations, one work schedule and one kiosk, and no attendance report, leave workflow or leave balances. Free keeps overtime calculations, face recognition, selfie, PIN and NFC clock-ins, GPS-verified clock-ins and geofences, timesheet and report exports, and the Slack, Microsoft Teams, QuickBooks Online, Xero, Deel and Zapier integrations.
Setting up the organisation requires a phone number; the form will not continue without one. The marketing opt-in on the sign-up form is ticked by default.
Clocking out in the same minute you clocked in is refused, with a message saying you cannot clock out before clocking in. Jibble records whole minutes; two minutes later it worked.
Inviting a second member took a name and an email address and went through without any prompt to pay. The member shows as pending until they accept.

The weekly timesheet export offers XLS or CSV. Our CSV arrived within seconds and carries 32 columns per member per day, including worked hours, paid and unpaid breaks, deductions, payroll hours, daily and weekly overtime and billable amounts.
We did not switch on face recognition or GPS. The comparison puts both in Free; anti-spoofing, device lock and live location tracking are Pro only.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

sessions.what: We started the 30-day trial; everything after that was measured inside the account. The first question the protocol asked was whether the trial takes a card, because their pricing page does not say. It does not, but the answer is on the signup page, not the pricing page, which is a small lesson in where vendors put the reassuring sentence.
findings: No card for the trial. The signup page states it plainly — “Try it free for 30 days. No credit card required. Cancel anytime.” — and the form asks only for an email address and a password. The pricing page, where you would actually look, says nothing about it.

The prices inside the account are not the prices on the pricing page. The public page leads with the promotional rate, currently a limited-time 90% off for three months. The in-app upgrade screen quotes the real thing: Lite $23, Plus $43, Premium $70 a month, with a Yearly toggle marked “Save 10%”. Sign up on the strength of $2.30 and the first screen you see afterwards is $23.
Two add-ons ride along on every tier, and they are easy to miss: Team Members at $11 per user a month, and Advanced Payments at $20 a month. They are listed under Lite, Plus and Premium alike.

Removing FreshBooks branding from the emails your client receives is not a paid feature: it is a quote-only one. It appears only on the top “Let's Talk” tier, alongside lower card fees and two included team members. On Lite, Plus and Premium your invoice mail carries their brand.

The client ceiling that decides the tier is not testable during the trial. Lite stops at 5 clients, Plus at 50, Premium unlimited, but the trial runs with full features, as the upgrade screen says in as many words (“Upgrade to a paid plan to continue using all of FreshBooks' great features”). We fed the client importer a six-client CSV and it accepted the file and moved straight to field matching, with no limit warning at the point where a Lite account would have stopped. So the meter that will actually bite you is the one you cannot feel while you are evaluating.
Prices are shown in USD on a Netherlands account, and the plan screen carries the note “Features vary by region.”

After that the vendor page app.postscript.io/shopify/auth stayed on Loading Postscript for more than 20 seconds. Postscript did not appear in Settings, Apps (the list showed 8 other apps), so it is not known whether the install was completed; it may only finish after the onboarding, or the auth step failed. sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Gorgias on a Shopify development store: the install, a workspace made by the app on its own with no password or card, one macro with made up text saved in about 1.5 minutes and 5 steps, and the Billing page with a free trial from 17 to 24 November, Starter at $10 a month for 50 tickets and the AI Agent at $30 a month for 30 interactions. The app said Shopify billing was inactive, and Activate in Shopify led to an empty screen, so nothing was approved and the checkout was not tested. Nothing was sent, no channel was connected, and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the App Store listing (English) was opened and the install form was submitted at 18:33 in our own tab. The first screen was Connect your Gorgias account to Shopify, with the choices Create Your Account and Already have an account. Create Your Account led to the Shopify dialog Install app, which asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked. The app then showed Generating your Gorgias workspace and opened a workspace of the vendor on its own; the address of that workspace contains the name of our development store, so it is not shown. No password, card, phone number or form was asked: the account came from the Shopify identity. A banner said Your account is not verified. Please check your email.; no e-mail was sent or opened. The admin was in English. Core action, one macro (a saved reply): Settings, Macros, Create macro, the name Test: Snowboard shipping delay and the text Hi, thanks for your patience. Your snowboard is packed and leaves our test warehouse tomorrow. This is invented test text., then Create macro. It was done at about 18:34, about 1.5 minutes after the start and 5 steps after the form was opened. The macro appeared in the list with usage count 0; the list already held 12 example macros of the vendor. No mailbox, social channel or phone number was connected and no ticket or message was sent. The AI Agent was not tested. Plans in the app: Billing, Usage & Plans said Your free trial started on November 17, 2026 and will expire on November 24, 2026 (seven days). Helpdesk was Starter at $10/month with 0 of 50 tickets used; AI Agent was $30/month with 0 of 30 automated interactions used; Voice (from $30/month) and SMS (from $20/month) were inactive and locked. Together Starter and the AI Agent are $40 a month, as the dossier says. The Basic plan and above were not looked at in the app. Difference with the dossier (from the listing, not from the app): the listing names Basic at $60 a month or $600 a year, while the dossier gives Basic at $90 a month or $77 a month billed annually. This comes from the listing and is not a test result; Basic was not opened in the app. Checkout: NOT reached. A banner said Your Shopify billing is inactive, so your payments may not go through, and that after activation the Starter plan ($10/month), the AI Agent ($30/month) and Gaia would be billed through Shopify, excluding sales tax. The button Activate in Shopify first opened an extra tab (closed) and, in our own tab, led to the billing activation address of the vendor and stayed on an empty screen of the vendor. The Shopify screen Approve subscription was not reached, nothing was approved, no card was entered and nothing was paid; so the checkout was not tested and no total, tax or test charge text was seen. Cancelling: not tested as a separate step; the app was removed through Settings, Apps, Uninstall (reason: Testing multiple apps) at about 18:37 and Gorgias no longer appeared in the list. Not tested: the AI Agent, live chat, real tickets, Shopify order data in tickets, seats, Basic and higher plans, cancelling inside Gorgias, e-mail verification and the Shopify approval screen. Clean up: the app was uninstalled; the test macro stayed in the workspace of the vendor, which is no longer linked to the store; no plan was approved and no theme change was made; our own tabs were closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

findings: Text we checked: "from $215 /mo". What we saw: The text of the public pricing page, read while it loaded, gave Assessments Core from $215 per month and Plus from $520, billed annually. sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on Freshdesk, during the trial that starts with a new account (Freshdesk Omni, EU data centre), without connecting a channel, a mailbox or an integration: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We created three tickets with known priorities and statuses, changed one and added a private note.
findings: The sign-up page promised a '14-day all-access free trial'; inside the app the banner said 'your 15-day trial starts today', next to a 'Buy now' button. Our own company domain was accepted without a business-email check.

All three tickets (#4, #5 and #6) were created with a 'Ticket created' message, and in All tickets all nine values we set (subject, priority and status) were right. The open Low-priority ticket got a deadline straight away: 'First response due in 7 hours'.

Times were off by default: tickets created on the evening of 21 October, Amsterdam time, showed as 'Thu, 22 Oct 2026 at 3:24 AM'. The new account's time zone was not Amsterdam, despite the EU data centre. It can be changed; we did not check whether SLA deadlines move with it.

Onboarding asked for industry, experience, up to three goals and support channels, then offered 'Build your first AI Agent' from a website, with 'Skip for now'; we skipped it. The workspace already held three sample tickets with sample contacts.
The New ticket form sets Source to Phone and Product to 'Example' by default and requires a Description; a 'Create another' box lets you add tickets in a row.
Changing FD-BETA from High to Low in the list view stuck: the opened ticket showed Priority Low and Status Pending. The private note was marked orange, and no email went out.

'Add AI summary' on every ticket, 'Write with AI' in the note editor and the AI Agent builder were all on offer during the trial. We did not click them, and what remains of them after the trial is not established.
not_tested: Connecting an email, chat or phone channel, and emailing a customer
AI Agent, AI summary and Write with AI
What happens when the trial expires. The public Freshdesk FAQ, read 25 Nov 2026, says the account is suspended if you do not choose a paid plan after the 14-day Enterprise trial.

findings: The account opened on a 14-day Pro trial without a card, after six onboarding screens. The first screen had 'allow automatic sign-ups with an @aibuildermarketplace.com email address' switched on by default.

The plans page started at 5 seats; the smallest choice was 3. For 3 seats Pro cost €19 per seat a month billed yearly or €24 monthly, and choosing monthly first opened a prompt to reconsider yearly billing.

A 'when status changes to Done, move item to group' automation ran within seconds and used 1 of the 25,000 monthly actions on Pro. The Sidekick assistant correctly named the two tasks due on 29 October.

Invitations offer Admin, Member and a Viewer role described as 'view only, no edits (free)'. The 'downgrade to Free' link only said you can choose a plan when the trial ends. API tokens and an MCP server are offered in the developer centre.

sessions.what: On 13 November 2026 we tested Zendesk Suite Professional on its trial, using our own site as the knowledge source. We built a Billing group and a routing trigger with the admin copilot, saved one synthetic invoice ticket, and asked the AI agent a Dutch and an English question. We did not open checkout, and we did not test support, invitations, roles, API access, export or cancellation.
findings: We created the account the day before and we did not see that step. In the accelerated setup the website address came prefilled, and about 35 seconds later the AI agent had read our site. The setup asked for no card, no phone number and no mailbox connection. An optional banner offered an expert call.
The trial runs on Suite Professional with 12 of 14 days left when we looked. The trial therefore includes features that the entry plan Support Team does not.

The admin copilot created the Billing group on the first approval. The routing trigger took three approvals: the copilot first used the field subject, which Zendesk rejected, then title, then subject_includes_word. The whole job took about 1.5 minutes.

The plan page lists the admin copilot under Suite Professional. We did not test the same trigger on Suite Team, where it would be set up by hand.

The AI agent runs in Dutch because the account language is Dutch. Our English question was refused with 'Ik spreek uw taal niet'. A Dutch question about whether we test software ourselves got an answer in about 10 seconds that matches our site: some reviews are tested hands-on and dated, others are supplier-research reviews. sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 15 November 2026 the session tested EasyDMARC on the platform trial: adding our own domain, the first result, the verification route, the price of the plans and the checkout up to the card form. No DNS was changed and nothing was paid. Add Domain first offers Discovered Domains, which asks to connect providers such as Mailgun, Amazon SES, SendGrid, HubSpot, Klaviyo and HighLevel; we chose Add Manually. Our domain was added as type Sending (the other choice is Parked) at about 17:28. The step Verify Domain Manually followed: EasyDMARC recognised Hostinger as the DNS provider and says to delete the current DMARC record of type TXT at host _dmarc and then to add a new CNAME record with a value under easydmarc.pro. So verifying means removing your own DMARC record and letting EasyDMARC host DMARC through a CNAME (managed DMARC); stopping later means putting your own record back, which is derived from the steps and not tested. We chose Later: a DNS change needs a separate approval from the account owner, so no DNS was changed and the domain stays unverified. The domain list showed Policy None, Total Volume 0 and a warning triangle. A domain overview was available within a minute and was viewed at 17:29: Infrastructure Health Score, Total Score 32, with Domain Health 80/100, Authentication 40/100, Sender Insights 0/100 and Threat Intelligence 0/100. Authentication showed DMARC Policy None, DMARC Record Valid, SPF Valid (3/10 lookups) and DKIM No Record with Selectors N/A; DMARC Compliance Rate was 0%. Blocklist was Inactive with Monitoring off and Google Postmaster had No data. Our own dig check at 17:29 showed that the _dmarc TXT record is v=DMARC1; p=none, so the policy None is right, and that the SPF record includes the Hostinger mail servers, which is right. The DKIM selector hostingermail-a is a CNAME to the DKIM host of the mail provider with a valid RSA key. So our domain does have DKIM, and EasyDMARC reported No Record, presumably because it does not know the selector until reports arrive, which only happens after the CNAME verification. Pending Actions showed 1 Critical, Verify your domain to unlock full visibility; without verification no DMARC reports arrive. No kit records were entered.
findings: Our own domain was added on the platform trial at about 17:28 and a domain overview was available within a minute: Infrastructure Health Score 32, with Domain Health 80/100, Authentication 40/100, Sender Insights 0/100 and Threat Intelligence 0/100.

EasyDMARC read our DMARC policy (none) and SPF (valid, 3 of 10 lookups) correctly, as our own dig check confirmed. It showed DKIM as No Record, although our domain publishes a valid DKIM key for the selector hostingermail-a. The tool does not know the selector until reports arrive.

Verifying the domain means deleting your own DMARC TXT record at _dmarc and adding a CNAME to an easydmarc.pro host, so EasyDMARC hosts DMARC for you. Putting the old record back after leaving is derived from the steps and not tested. We chose Later, so no DNS was changed and the domain stays unverified.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 24 October 2026 during the Core plan trial, without a card, without sending invitations, publishing a schedule or connecting payroll: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We pasted two made-up team members (with a payroll ID and a base rate) into the bulk importer, exported the team data, and pasted the exported rows back with one changed name.
findings: The bulk importer accepted both rows after we cleared a job title that did not exist yet ('Tester'): only existing job titles are allowed. 'Job Complete: 2 records imported successfully, 0 records failed', and both people showed as Employee, 'Not invited'. The importer's column order differs from the CSV template, so rows copied from the template land in the wrong columns; whether an uploaded file is matched by column name we did not test.
The base rates we pasted in (20 and 25) did not come through: they were empty in the export and no pay rate showed in People.

The team export is prepared in the background ('This can take up to 5 minutes'); ours was ready after about 20 seconds via the notification bell. The CSV had the same 29 columns as the import template, with both people, our payroll IDs and a Deputy ID each. Deputy had filled in a username, a stress profile (24/7) and gender 'Prefer not to say' on its own.

Pasting the exported rows back with their Deputy ID created no duplicates and applied the changed name. But 'Prefer not to say', the gender value from Deputy's own export, was flagged as invalid and had to be cleared first.
After setup, 'Now let's add your team members' had 'Send email invites' ticked by default; we skipped it. The template's sample rows set 'Send Invite' to Y and the role to System Administrator.

The trial bar said '31 days remaining of your Core Plan trial.' and no card was asked. Consent to sales and marketing calls is a line of text under the phone field; SMS marketing is a separate tick box, which we left off.
not_tested: Scheduling and publishing a roster
Clocking in and timesheets
Payroll connections
What happens after 31 days
Deputy AI

sessions.what: We already knew from their pricing pages that Glide sells two products. What we had never done is the thing a reader does: go to glideapps.com and press the free signup button. We created the account; everything after that was measured in the product.
findings: The free signup button does not lead to the product our pricing section describes. Both “Sign up” and “Get started” on glideapps.com point at os.glideapps.dev: GlideOS. We signed up and landed there. The classic builder, with the free tier of unlimited drafts, one editor and 25k rows, sits behind glideapps.com/classic, which you only reach if you already know to look for it.

The two ladders are an order of magnitude apart. Classic business pricing starts at $199 a month billed yearly; GlideOS Basic is $25 a month. Same brand, same homepage, two different products with two different price floors.

And the meter is different. Classic bills updates: 5,000 included, 2 cents each after that. GlideOS bills credits: Basic 100 a month, Plus 250, Pro 500 and upward with team size. So the “updates, not seats” warning that applies to Classic does not describe the product a new signup actually lands in.

GlideOS's free tier publishes no number. Every paid tier lists its credit allowance; the free column says “Limited credits”, alongside 2 team members and 10 projects. Nowhere in the app is there a balance, not on the dashboard, not in the account menu, not on the upgrade screen. You cannot find out what you have or what you have spent.

The AI itself is not walled off on free. From one sentence — “build a simple app to track software subscriptions” — it drew up a plan, asked a sensible clarifying question about where the data lives today, produced a working mockup and then began importing components one by one. We hit no credit wall during any of it.
