The counters in the header at the start: 299 retouching credits, 10 culling, 0 generative and 10 colour. The dossier name is Retouch4me and the review is on AIBM (b2b/retouch4me-review). The audiences from the dossier: High-volume portrait and wedding photographers using Photoshop (solved in part), Occasional editors with light retouching needs (solved in part) and Photographers who want generative editing today (not solved; the alternative is PhotoGenerator). An earlier test on 8 Sep 2026 found that an upload costs 1 retouching credit and the samples are free. Test image: the app offers its own sample photos under No Image? Try one of these; sample 3 was chosen, so no own upload and no portrait of a real person of ours. Deviation: one sample instead of three portraits. The samples are real model photos of Retouch4me, and on every evidence screenshot the whole image area is masked. Core action: retouch4.me/onlineretouch, Online retouch, the cloud retouching in the browser. It has 10 plugins as switches with sliders: Heal, Mattifier, Dodge & Burn, Portrait Volumes, Skin Tone, Eye Vessels, Eye Brilliance, White Teeth, Fabric and Clean Backdrop. Skin Mask is not in the online version. One click on sample 3 gave a result at once, in about 2 seconds, with eight plugins on by default (Heal, Mattifier, Dodge & Burn, Portrait Volumes, Skin Tone, Eye Vessels, Eye Brilliance, White Teeth; Fabric and Clean Backdrop off). The buttons are View original, New Upload and a download icon. Then Dodge & Burn was switched off and Fabric on: the image updated in about 1 second and the counter stayed at 299 after each change. The credit use was 0 for the sample and for 2 changes. The note under the upload zone says: Images will be resized for faster web performance. When uploading a photo you will spend one retouch. An own upload was not done, so that cost was not measured in this test. The result was not downloaded: it is a real model face and was not needed; nothing was saved in the Downloads folder. Plans: Account, Tariffs and packages, read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026. Lifetime license per plugin: Heal $94.25 ($145.00 struck through, 35% off this week); Face Make, Crop, Dust, Eyes Bundle, Fabric, Skin Mask, Portrait Volumes, Skin Tone, White Teeth and Mattifier $94.25 (was $145.00); Clean Backdrop $116.35 (was $179.00). Subscription Start (annual): $20.00 struck through, $14.08 a month, $169.00 billed yearly, 2400 retouches at $0.07 per pc, culling credits 108000, generative credits 4800, up to 5 years while the subscription is active, 1 year with automatic renewal, 14-day money-back guarantee. Pricing page, Business: $63.25 a month, $759 billed yearly, 18 000 retouching credits, 1 200 000 culling credits, 43200 generative credits. Fixed retouch pack (dropdown, no time limit until they run out): Trial Pack $0.00 (20 retouches, culling credits 100, 7 days from activation); Starter $24.00 (100 retouches, $0.24 per pc, culling credits 4500); Advanced $59.00; Extended $179.00. Tax and the total were not seen: Buy pack and Get started lead to the checkout and Buy in one click can charge at once, so the tester did not click through. The public page retouch4.me/pricing was read again just before this delivery the same day and shows the same Start plan ($20, $14.08 a month, $169 billed yearly, 2 400 retouching credits, 108 000 culling credits, 4800 generative credits), the same Business plan ($63.25 a month, $759 billed yearly), the Photo Plugins from $94.25 (was $145) and the sale banner Magic of Numbers. The fixed packs sit in a dropdown that the public page text does not show, so they were not compared again; the amounts above are from the account. The dossier shows the same lifetime and subscription prices. Deviations against the dossier: the Starter Pack has fewer culling credits than the dossier says, the free Trial Pack is not in the dossier, and the sale of 35% off this week is new. Cancelling: retouch4.me/account/settings has only the name, the e-mail address, the newsletter preference and Change password. There is no button to delete the account or to cancel, and My purchases lists only the bought plugins and no subscription, so no cancel route could be tested. Not tested: an own upload (1 credit, according to the note and the test of 8 Sep), Skin Mask, the Photoshop panel, Apex and Arams (desktop, not installed), no AI portrait was made, the download of the result, and the tax and total at checkout. Clean up: nothing was downloaded or deleted; the Downloads folder was checked and held no portrait or result; the account and the credits are unchanged (299); all our tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The free sample hides what an own photo costs: the note under the upload zone says an upload spends one retouch, so the first real test of your own photo takes a credit. Skin Mask is not in the online version. The Starter Pack has fewer culling credits than the dossier says, and the pack dropdown is not shown on the public page text. Buy in one click can charge at once, so check the cart before you press it. The account has no cancel or delete button.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 22 November 2026 in the TextExpander web app on a new account, with the interface in English. We created a snippet group with six support replies, deleted one and restored it from Snippet Activity, exported the group to CSV and imported it again, and opened the plan pickers for the individual and team plans. We installed no app or extension and paid nothing.
findings: Sign up: the new account started as Individual (Trial) until 22 December 2026, with advanced features unlocked for 30 days and no card on file. The web app opened on a page that pushed the Chrome extension and the Mac and Windows apps.
Language: the web app has no language setting; it follows the browser language, so we had to start it in English ourselves.
Snippets: we made a group called Support replies and six snippets with their own abbreviations. No limit came up during the trial.

Restore: we deleted one snippet. Snippet Activity kept its text, and Details, Restore and a confirm brought it back with the message Snippet updated. The history could be filtered to the last 24 hours or 7 days during the trial.

Export and import: the CSV export held all six snippets with abbreviation, text and label. Importing that file made a second group; exporting the copy gave an identical file. The import accepted the same abbreviations in a second group without a warning.

Team: Share on a group invites people by email. Team features need an Organization account, and the upgrade went straight to a plan picker with Purchase and no team trial: Pro EUR 5.58, Business EUR 11.16 and Enterprise EUR 22.32 per user a month billed yearly, or EUR 6.70, EUR 13.39 and EUR 27.90 billed monthly, on 22 November 2026.
Individual plan: Start subscription offered only an Individual plan marked Legacy, at EUR 4.64 per user a month billed monthly or EUR 3.71 billed yearly.
Privacy: in Profile, the setting for non essential (analytics and marketing) cookies was switched on by default.
not_tested: expanding snippets while typing: that needs the Chrome extension or the Mac or Windows app, and we did not install either
sharing with a second person: the Share dialog invites by email, and we invited no one
an Organization account (Pro, Business or Enterprise): it needs a purchase
the free plan limits after the trial, such as 5 active snippets: the trial unlocked advanced features for 30 days
fill ins, dates, math and other dynamic snippet content
paying: we opened the plan pickers to read the prices and did not buy

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 25 October 2026 on the 3-day Flexible trial: we created and verified the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We launched a DigitalOcean server with WordPress, imported two made-up rows into a separate database table, exported them as SQL and updated one of them.
findings: The Flexible trial needed no card before launch. The setup screen showed DigitalOcean Premium 4GB at $54.00 a month ($0.0804 an hour) and $0 during the trial, with billing starting only when the account is upgraded. The server took about nine minutes to provision.

In Database Manager we imported our test rows into a table of their own (4 successful queries). Text, Unicode, dates, exact decimal amounts, a true/false field (stored as tinyint) and an empty value kept apart from NULL all came through; the attachment column holds only a file path.

Exporting just that table as SQL returned both rows with their native IDs 1 and 2 next to our own IDs. We then ran an SQL UPDATE on the native key (2 successful queries): only the second row's text changed and no duplicates appeared. This is a database update, not an import screen in the app.

Adding a payment method to upgrade opens the card form before any final plan total. The form mentions a $1 verification that is reversed after authorization, and the page said 'Taxes Do not Apply to your current invoice based on your account information.' We entered no card.

Our three support questions in the chat were answered within seconds by Cloudways' AI agent: it described a full application backup you can download over SFTP, said Copilot may share server and application logs with OpenAI-based models, and passed the DPA question to a human agent. We saw no human reply in that session.
not_tested: A full application backup or a restore into an empty server
Uploading media or other binary files
Inviting a colleague
Cancelling or deleting the server and account

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on the free account with 25 credits: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We uploaded our own simple 600x400 test images (a blue circle as JPG, PNG and AVIF, an orange square as PNG), asked for one in Dutch, and looked them up again in the library.
findings: Each image cost 1 credit: the blue circle as JPG, the circle as PNG and the orange square as PNG took the balance from 25 to 22.

The texts were correct and added nothing that was not there: 'A solid blue circle centered on a white background.' and 'An orange square centered on a white background.' The PNG of the circle gave exactly the same text as the JPG.

With Dutch added next to English (the language field says 'Credits: 1 per language'), only a Dutch text was saved, 'Een effen blauwe cirkel, gecentreerd op een witte achtergrond.' ('A solid blue circle, centred on a white background'), for 1 credit (22 to 21). This test does not settle how multi-language runs are billed.

The AVIF was refused in the upload form before anything ran: 'Please choose a JPG, PNG, or WebP image.' with 'Upgrade to support advanced formats (AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JP2, SVG, TIFF)'. No credit was used. The upload label itself lists 'JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP, or BMP (max 16MB)'.
The library search looks in the alt text, not the Asset ID: 'TEST-A' gave 'Your search returned no results.', while 'blue circle' found the two English records of the circle (not the Dutch one).
The library listed all four records with Asset ID, source 'Direct Upload', text and time, but the edit page showed 'Image unavailable': the uploaded image itself is not shown again.
End state: 21 of 25 credits left after four generations and one refused AVIF.
not_tested: Accessibility quality on real, complex photos (we only used simple shapes)
Any SEO effect of the alt text
CMS integrations such as WordPress and Shopify, and writing alt text back automatically
Bulk import, URL input, the e-commerce and keyword fields, and Final Pass
Paid formats such as AVIF and what they cost in credits
When the free credits expire

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 on a new Free account, without starting the trial upgrade and without sending any broadcast or automation: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We imported three made-up contacts from a CSV file with a tag, added a note to one of them and tried to export the contacts.
findings: CSV import (only .csv, up to 25 MB or 25,000 rows) matched all four of our columns automatically, with 'First Name' mandatory. Options were a tag, 'Validate emails' (which needs paid credits), 'Merge contacts' and 'Send double opt-in email', which we left off. The import ran in the background; after about 20 seconds and a refresh all 3 contacts were there.
All three imported contacts showed the status 'Confirmed' although no opt-in email was sent. Check how your own list is labelled before you mail it.

Export as CSV (a bulk action) offers about 35 contact fields to tick, such as contact ID, tags, status, sources, address, dates and the last email, SMS and call, but no field for notes, tasks or documents. After Export the app said it would email the file ('Your export is getting ready. We'll email you when it's done'); there is no direct download. We did not verify delivery or inspect the file.

A contact page has tabs for activities, emails, deals, tasks, notes, documents, products, proposals, workflows and automations. Adding a note with a subject and text worked, with an option to create a follow-up task.
The Free dashboard showed a banner asking to verify the email address and a pop-up offering a '3-day All-Access Pass', which we did not start.
not_tested: Email broadcasts, sequences and automations
Uploading documents, and tasks
Re-importing and merging
What changes after the email address is verified
The contents of the exported CSV file

sessions.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session browsed World Businesses for Sale without an account. The site has no filter panel, only a search box and a sort box. A search for e-commerce gave 31 results (11 of them plan or broker products) and a search for cafe gave 9 results, from GBP 78,500 to GBP 1,500,000. Annual turnover and net profit were shown openly and contact ran only through a form, which was not filled in. The broker plans are GBP 395, GBP 499 and GBP 999 with 3%, 2% and 1% commission, and the no-commission plans are GBP 49, GBP 75 and GBP 99 a month; all are the same as in the dossier, although the home page says from GBP 39 a month and quotes both 1% and 2% commission on different pages. Nothing was bought and nothing was put in the cart.

Text we checked: "Standard GBP 499". What we saw: The page shows Standard at GBP 499 with 2% commission and a 9-month contract, marked MOST POPULAR, as in the dossier.

Text we checked: "Stay Live Until Sold - Free Renewals". What we saw: The page shows Premium at GBP 999 with 1% commission, a 12-month contract and the line Stay Live Until Sold, Free Renewals, as in the dossier.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We claimed the free Webpage trial on 18 November 2026: 500 answers for 7 days at $0, three clicks, no KYC, card or phone number. Each answer cost 2 credits, so 8 requests took the balance from 500 to 484. The dashboard shows answers, not gigabytes. Our own calculation from 3,636 byte test pages puts the Webpage API near $361 per GB, or $722 counting the 2 credits, against $2 per GB for residential; real pages are larger, so treat it as an upper bound. The residential prices match our dossier, and the 350 GB order summary shows $595 before a 55% discount of $315. We stopped before any purchase.

The dossier only says free API trials.

Text we checked: ""credits":2". What we saw: Every one of the 8 answers carried "credits":2, and the balance went from 500 to 484, so 16 for 8 requests. The 500 of the trial are therefore about 250 requests.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested the free Webpage trial of Thordata: 500 answers for 7 days at $0, claimed in 3 clicks in about a minute with no KYC, card or phone number. Every answer took 2 credits, so the balance went from 500 to 484 after 8 requests, about 250 requests in all, all HTTP 200. The dashboard counts answers and shows no gigabytes; by our own calculation from 3636 byte test pages the Webpage API comes to about $361 per GB, or about $722 per GB counting the 2 credits, against $2 per GB for residential. The httpbin answers showed a Googlebot identity (observation only). The residential prices are unchanged against the dossier ($2 per GB for 1 GB down to $0.65 per GB at 5,000 GB); the order summary of 350 GB now shows Price before discount $595 and 55% Discount -$315. Nothing was bought and the payment screen was not opened. Account and start: the account was created by us (registration 18/11/2026, dashboard.thordata.com, interface already in English); our AI assistant ran the test in our Chrome from about 14:35 (Amsterdam). The Overview showed Wallet $0.000 and the trial token was valid until 25/11/2026. No KYC, card or phone number was asked for the trial. The dossier name is Thordata and the review is on AIBM (b2b/thordata-review). The pain that was tested: Teams starting a first scraping project, "The advertised rate looks cheap, but my first project is nowhere near the size that earns it." (dossier: solved in part, no alternative listed). Core action: Webpage, Pricing, the Webpage pack of 500 answers for 7 days at $0, Start with Trial. The order summary said 500 for 7 Days and $0, the message was Successfully claimed the trial! with the button Go use it: 3 clicks, about 1 minute. Right after the claim the page behind it showed Total $13 with Continue to checkout (the 10,000 pack); it was not clicked. Playground: the balance said 500 with Expiration time 25/11/2026, and the example is a cURL POST to the Webunlocker endpoint with a Bearer token (the token is not recorded anywhere). 8 requests were sent, only to httpbin (/ip, /headers and /html), all HTTP 200 in 0.4 to 0.75 seconds. Every answer carried "credits":2. The answers were 97, 374 and 3636 bytes, 15,487 bytes in total. Observation, no judgment: the httpbin answers showed an outgoing IP address and a User-Agent and a From header that identify Googlebot (googlebot(at)googlebot.com). The cause was not investigated and whether a normal target site sees the same was not tested. Statistics: Total usage 8, successful 8, failed 0, average response time 0.38 seconds; the dashboard shows no gigabytes for the Webpage API. The balance fell from 500 to 484, so 16 for 8 requests, 2 per answer, which leaves about 250 requests in the trial. After the 8 requests the API token was refreshed in the dashboard (Refresh, Confirm, Refresh successfully); a 9th request with the old key gave {"code":401,"data":"API key authentication failed:API Token is error"}. 9 requests in all, within the limit of 20. The new token was not viewed or recorded. Own calculation, not a vendor figure: the Webpage API is priced per answer, the dashboard shows no gigabytes, and the tester measured the size of the answers himself: 97, 374 and 3636 bytes, 15,487 bytes in all for 8 requests (15.487 in the raw note, a Dutch thousands dot). At $1.30 per 1K for the 10,000 pack, a page of the largest test size (3636 bytes, about 3,6 KB) is 3,6 MB per 1K answers, which is about $361 per GB. Because every answer took 2 credits from the balance, the reading with credits is about $722 per GB. Residential Proxies cost $2 per GB at the 1 GB tier, far below that. The figure only holds for pages as small as the httpbin test pages; real pages are larger, so the cost per GB of the Webpage API would drop in proportion, and whether a credit costs the price of an answer or half of it was not verified. The 8 test requests are too small a sample for more. Plans, up to the point of paying: Residential Proxies, tab Regular, pay-as-you-go, never expires, read by the tester in the dashboard on 18 Nov 2026: 1 GB $2/GB ($2.85/GB struck through), total $2 (tag New Users); 10 GB $1.8/GB, total $18; 50 GB $1.5/GB, total $75; 150 GB $1/GB, total $150; 350 GB $0.8/GB, total $280 (tag Best price). The order summary for 350 GB shows validity 30 Days, Price before discount $595, 55% Discount -$315 and Total $280. Enterprise, never expires: 1,000 GB $0.73/GB = $730; 2,000 GB $0.7/GB = $1400; 5,000 GB $0.65/GB = $3250; above that Custom Pricing Based on Demand / Contact sales. The minimum purchase is 1 GB ($2). Tax was not shown before checkout and the payment screen was not opened; card and crypto icons were visible. Webpage API, per answer: 10,000 answers $1.30/1K = $13; 50,000 $1.20/1K = $60; 100,000 $1.10/1K = $110; 200,000 $1.00/1K = $200. The public page thordata.com/pricing/residential-proxies was read again just before this delivery the same day and shows the same five Regular tiers (1 GB $2.00, 10 GB $1.80, 50 GB $1.50, 150 GB $1.00, 350 GB $0.80 per GB; totals $2.00, $18.00, $75.00, $150.00, $280.00; struck through $2.85, $2.75, $1.95, $1.50, $1.70), the High Volume rows (1000 GB $730.00, 2000 GB $1400.00, 5000 GB $3250.00) and the same Webpage packs. So the prices are unchanged against the dossier. Only the 55% discount line is new: it appears in the order summary of the dashboard, and the public page shows no discount percentage and no price before discount. The refund rule was not tested. Cancelling: Avatar, My Account, Account Settings has a Delete Account button with the text that the service is deactivated immediately after deletion; it was not clicked. The same page shows Account verification (KYC) Not verified with a Verify account button; it was not clicked, so whether Residential Proxies need the verification is unknown. Not tested: the residential proxies themselves (not bought, no proxy traffic), a refund, tax and the payment screen, where the IP addresses come from, the KYC rule for residential, and bandwidth in GB for the Webpage API. Clean up: the account, the trial (484 answers left until 25/11/2026) and the new token stay; there is no wallet balance and nothing was bought; our own tab was closed, no other tab was touched; no login details were saved in files. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The free Webpage trial is smaller than it looks: every answer takes 2 credits, so 500 gives about 250 requests. The dashboard counts answers and not gigabytes, so you cannot compare the Webpage API with the per-GB prices of residential traffic without measuring your own page sizes; for pages as small as our test pages it comes out far more expensive per GB. The low per-GB rates need volume: $2 per GB at 1 GB and $0.65 per GB only at 5,000 GB. Our httpbin answers showed a Googlebot identity, so check what your own target sites see. The account page shows KYC as not verified; whether residential needs it was not tested.

sessions.what: The free plan, on a test landing page of our own with PagePulse's tracking script pasted before </body>, as its setup screen instructs. We then sent scripted visits whose every detail we logged: 10 visitors in 11 sessions (one came back in a new tab), 4 arriving from google.com, 3 from x.com and the rest direct, 3 on a phone-sized screen, 6 clicks on 'Start free trial', 3 clicks on 'Book a demo' that led to a second page, and visits of 35, 20 or 5 seconds. A second, smaller run of 3 visitors with one click each followed later, with every message the script sent logged. We compared the dashboard with what we had done.
findings: The counts were right. Visitors 10 and page views 14 matched exactly, as did the source split (Google 4, X 3, direct 4 of 14 views) and the device split (3 mobile, 7 desktop). In the second run every number moved by exactly what we sent: visitors 10 to 13, page views 14 to 17, 'Start free trial' clicks up by exactly 3.
Clicks on links and buttons are captured without extra setup and named by their text ('Start free trial', 'Book a demo'). The script itself sent one event per click.

Engagement does not follow its own definition. The tooltip defines an engaged session as one lasting 10+ seconds, with 2+ page views, or a conversion. By that rule 8 of our first 11 sessions qualify, as they lasted 20 to 35 seconds. The dashboard showed 27%: exactly the 3 sessions with two page views. The 20-second sessions of the second run did not count either.
A click from our page to our own thank-you page shows up as a traffic source, listed as the site's own domain at 21% next to Google and X.

The 'Here's what we found' analysis was general copywriting advice drawn from the page text (move the call to action, add testimonials), not from the visit data, and it sat under the line 'Once your tracking is set up', while tracking demonstrably worked.

The free script records page views, clicks, time on page through a ping every 15 seconds, and load times. It does not record scroll depth, and conversions need your own trackConversion call, which the dashboard says is part of Starter and above.
not_tested: heatmaps and conversion tracking (paid plans), traffic beyond a few dozen events, and real visitors

sessions.what: A fresh WordPress 7.1.2 test site, the Clonable plugin from the WordPress directory and a new free Clonable account. We cloned the site into German, wrote and then changed a page of our own, corrected a translation by hand and connected the plugin, checking each result on the live pages and in WordPress. This test is also our entry in Clonable's review content campaign on Reditus, which offers a one-off €30 if Clonable approves it. We used the public free plan and Clonable did not see the article before publication.
findings: From typing the site address to a working German preview took under five minutes, about two of them waiting for the build. No DNS change or plugin is needed for the preview.
We changed a price on the English page from 49 to 59 euros; the German page showed the new price on our first reload, within fifteen seconds.

WordPress still listed the same three English pages afterwards. Clonable added no translated copies to the database; the only addition was its plugin. The other side of that: all clone traffic runs through Clonable's servers, which its own setup guide tells you to whitelist.

Connecting the plugin with an API key put hreflang tags for x-default, en-us and de-de in the head of both the original and the clone straight away. The URL slug stayed English; URL translation is a separate feature.
Correcting a single translation in the Clone editor works on the free plan. Translation Replacements and the Glossary, the tools for fixing a term everywhere at once, ask for an upgrade.
The plan picker inside the app showed one clone on every plan and 25 free pages, while the public pricing page the same day listed 3 to 20 clones per plan and 20 free pages.
sessions.not_tested: Going live on our own domain or a subfolder, WooCommerce and multi-currency, more than one short page, languages other than German, and WPML itself side by side. Choosing German in the floating language switcher did not navigate in our automated browser session, so we could not confirm that click-through.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 during the 14-day trial, without a card: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We built an unlisted test webinar with three PDF slides and a poll and ran it as a dry run; we did not publish it or invite anyone.
findings: The poll went live with an empty option. The third answer we had typed was not saved, and nothing warned us: the live poll showed an option with only the placeholder 'Fill in an answer'.
A three-page PDF went through 'Processing', 'Converting to images' and 'Putting everything together' and became three slides, in the right order, in about 35 seconds.

Onboarding created three sample webinars on its own (a live one scheduled for the same evening, an automated one and an on-demand one, all marked 'Sample'). The account opened in Dutch, and switching to English took two separate settings: the language menu in the studio and Account > Settings > Language.

New webinar offers Start from scratch, Generate (AI), Copy or Add to series; Present live, Automated or On-demand; and Public, Unlisted or Private access. 'Offer replay' is on by default, and 'Create and customize' does not publish yet. The title field ignored the first title we typed.

Polls sit under Interactions, next to Call to action, Quiz and Information: single or multiple choice, with a default duration of 1:30, and at the start you choose 'End manually' or 'End after a set time'.

The studio did not open until we allowed browser notifications and then camera and microphone. In the dry run it said 'Only team members and invited test viewers can join' and 'Dry runs aren't recorded and don't collect statistics'. Slides changed straight away with the arrow keys, and ending the dry run reset all interactions.
The viewer link of the unpublished webinar returned 'Not yet published: Publish your webinar first before you can use the registration page.', so a test viewer can only watch after you publish.
not_tested: The viewer side and the delay between presenter and viewer (that needs publishing)
Answering a poll as a viewer

Start: there is no app or account, only a search page with a map box, a business type and filters, an email pop-up and a results email. The free preview gave 20 credits to an email address; no card, password or phone number was asked. Our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab on 19 November 2026 from 12:02 to about 12:35 CET. The pop-up asks for the email address again for every search. Core action, three searches: Confirm Order says You have 20 credits remaining. Proceeding will use one credit for the search, and one credit for each result obtained. Search 1, Roofer in Dallas without websites: the email came after about 3 minutes with 0 Leads, 14 Raw Query Results, 1 Credits Used, so every roofer already had a website and the credit bought nothing. Search 2, Hair Salon in San Francisco without websites and with a phone number: no results email came within 25 minutes, not even in junk, yet the next confirm screen showed 18 credits. The search used 1 credit and returned nothing, with no error or status in the app. Search 3, Landscaping in Indianapolis without websites: the email came after about 20 minutes with 11 Leads, 121 Raw Query Results, 12 Credits Used, You have 6 credits remaining, and Errors: While processing the results, we had problems matching metadata for 19 establishments. In all 14 of 20 credits were used. The confirm screen never shows what the results will cost. Lead quality of the 11 landscaping leads, counted by hand (operational, phone, at least 1 rating, really a landscaper): 6 of 11 usable, 4 of 11 in the searched city itself; 2 sat about 55 and 70 miles away, one had no phone, one was not a business. A web check of 3 usable leads found no own website. At 12 credits for 6 usable leads that is 2 credits per usable lead, about $1.0 to $1.1 at pack prices. Limits: Business Type is a fixed list of 12 types, Categories are limited for this preview; the map box opens on a random city and moves only by dragging. Export is a CSV link in the email, valid 7 days, with company name, website, status, phone, address, rating and a Grape Lead Score. Plans: /pricing gives Page not found; Buy credits lists Freelancer $28 for 50 credits ($0.56 each), Startup $55 for 100 ($0.54) and Agency $127 for 250 ($0.51), all One-time, Secure checkout with Stripe. The results email says Each lead costs one credit, which is the equivalent of $0.30 per credit in bulk. Checkout: the card moment is Buy Now on the credits page; it was not clicked. Cancelling: there is no subscription and no account with a login, so there is nothing to cancel. Not tested: buying credits, the Stripe checkout, bulk pricing, asking for the lost credit back under the guarantee, and other cities. sessions.what: We set up a Netherlands-only Geo Redirect and a Geo Link on Geo Targetly's 14-day trial on 13 November 2026, opened the Geo Link from the Netherlands and read the plan screens. We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We placed no script on a real site, so the redirect rule itself never ran. We did not test checkout, support, export or cancellation.
findings: The trial needs no card. The subscription screen read '$0/mo on your free trial' with Payment Method None, and the account showed 13 days left. We joined an existing trial account, so we did not see the sign-up screens. A welcome window offered Start Setup and Skip for now, and a Book Free Setup Call is optional.

Geo Redirect saved without any code: from the fictional https://www.example.com to https://www.example.com/nl/ when the country equals Netherlands, redirecting visitors automatically. Step two wants a single script pasted just below the opening head tag. It offers install tabs for 14 platforms, among them Google Tag Manager, WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Squarespace and Webflow.

The URL fields add https:// themselves. Pasting a full address gave https://https://www.example.com, and we needed two corrections. Redirect plus link took about 7 minutes with those corrections (our own approximate timing, not a benchmark).

A Geo Link needs no script. Netherlands went to https://example.org/ and All Other Locations to https://example.com/, with a short link on a shared gtly.link domain and a QR code. The page recommends your own domain because shared domains can go down when others abuse them.

Opening the short link from the Netherlands first showed an interstitial, 'You will be redirected in 3', with Geo Targetly branding, and then https://example.org/ loaded. A notice says the branding is in effect during the free trial. Geo Targetly's text says a subscription removes it; we did not buy one, so we did not see that.

Pageview counting comes from the vendor help page 'What are pageviews quota?', which we read and did not measure: every page view counts, including visitors who match no rule; bots do not count; a Geo Link counts only a click; and multiple products on one page count as multiple pageviews, because each instance of the tracking script consumes one.

The in-app plan screen is in euros. Monthly: Dev 14, Startup 29, Growth 59, with 1,000, 20,000 and 100,000 pageviews a month. Yearly, shown per month: 11, 23 and 47 with 12,000, 240,000 and 1,200,000 pageviews a year, or 132, 276 and 564 in total. Yearly billing was preselected, under the banner 'SAVE 20% ON YEARLY BILLING'.
The Startup and Growth cards list 'Access to all features' and the Dev card does not. We did not check which features Dev lacks, so we cannot confirm that higher plans only add pageviews.
The dashboard holds a hidden notice for an exceeded quota ('Upgrade or re-subscribe'). We did not trigger it, so we do not know what happens to live redirects at the limit.

sessions.what: Two sessions on the free plan. On 7 September we ran it by hand: we logged in, and we read every counter against a test file of exactly five minutes that we built inside the page; Descript was not a partner of ours then and contributed nothing. On 30 September, by then a PartnerStack partner, we drove Descript from Claude through Descript's connector, for Descript's partner content challenge, which pays the first five entries $250: we uploaded one of our own five-minute review videos and asked for vertical clips in plain sentences, once directly and once from a claude.ai chat.
findings: The free plan's 100 AI credits are one-time, not monthly. Descript says so itself in two places: the plan card reads "100 AI credits at signup" for Free against "400 AI credits / month" for Hobbyist, and the usage screen inside the app puts "Lifetime AI credits used 0/100" next to "Monthly media minutes used 0/60". That pair of words -- lifetime against monthly -- is the whole answer.

Media minutes come off at IMPORT, not at export, and per minute of media. Two five-minute files took the counter from 60m to 50m. Their own upload dialog says it too: "Each file added uses media minutes". Exporting costs no minutes and no credits, according to Descript itself.

The AI assistant, Underlord, charges per instruction, and it does run on the free plan. Importing and transcribing cost 3 credits, Studio Sound over a ten-minute track 9 credits, and a question about the export settings 6 credits.

An instruction that returns nothing still costs credits. "Remove all filler words" answered "No filler words were found -- the script shows 0 words, so there's nothing to remove" and deducted 2 credits anyway.
Five instructions without a single real edit spent 20 of the 100 one-time credits. Anyone using the free plan as a trial is through it in an afternoon, and no more arrive.

Studio Sound ran on Free, while the pricing table presents it as a Hobbyist benefit ("Studio Sound, Remove Filler Words, Create Clips, and more"). The line "Limited use of Underlord" on the free card is therefore more generous than the comparison table suggests.
In onboarding, the consent "Our team analyzes your project information" is TICKED BY DEFAULT, in a step most people click straight through. You can turn it off, but you have to do it yourself.
The watermark on the free plan sits in the bottom right of the frame; paid plans do not have it.

Through Claude's Descript connector, a 5:15 review video of ours (94 MB) uploaded and transcribed in about 30 seconds. The import used 315 media seconds, consistent with minutes being charged at import.

One sentence to Underlord through Claude (a vertical 9:16 clip of about 30 seconds on the price and the 90-day data limit, with captions, keeping the words and numbers as spoken) produced a new 24-second vertical composition in two and a half minutes for 48.3 AI credits. The original composition was left untouched, and the clip's transcript matched the source word for word, numbers included.

From a claude.ai chat, Claude asked permission before each Descript action, read the transcript itself, chose the passage from 01:15 to 01:40 and had Underlord cut a 21-second vertical clip with burned-in captions in about three minutes. It also fixed the transcript's misspelling of the product name in the captions and said that it had.

The vertical version is a centre crop. On our 16:9 video it cut off the text card at the side of the frame, and because our video already carries subtitles, Descript's captions landed on top of them. Ask for the full frame on a blurred background, and skip added captions when your source already has them.

Our request to fix that was refused because the free plan had run out of AI credits: the one-time 100 were gone after our first session plus these two edits. Real editing work through Claude needs a paid plan.

Publishing gave an unlisted share link and an MP4 download in about a minute and a half. We asked for 1080p and received 720x1280 with the watermark in the bottom right, so the 720p cap on the Free plan card is what applies, not the 4K that Descript's own assistant named in our first session.

We saw no usage-limit message or counter after two short runs, but on the Max plan that says nothing about the limits on Free.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the trial, without a card, without connecting a channel and without publishing anything: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, using only the Simulator. We gave the AI a two-line return policy as a text knowledge source, asked four customer questions with known right answers, changed the return window from 14 to 30 days, asked again, and exported the tickets.
findings: Once the knowledge source was ready, the answers matched it: an unopened vase after 5 days got 'yes, you can return it' citing the 14-day policy for unopened items, and an opened lamp got 'not eligible for return or refund'. Asked about shipping to Norway, which the source did not cover, it said it couldn't find a verified answer and handed the conversation to a human ('Needs agent takeover'). It did not make anything up.

Changing the rule from 14 to 30 days took effect in the Simulator straight away: an unopened candle holder after 20 days first got 'no ... outside our return window' and, after the change, 'yes ... within 30 days of delivery for a full refund'. The source showed 'Not published yet', so this was the unpublished version.

Our very first question, asked while the knowledge source still said 'Analyzing' (it turned 'Ready' after about a minute), was handed over to a human in full. Asked again once the source was ready, it was answered.

Plan & limits showed 'Trial · 92 days remaining' on the day of sign-up, against 14 days in Typewise's documentation, with no payment method, 1,000 resolutions, 50K Nova (AI Operator) credits and one agent seat. Simulator conversations did not count as resolutions (still 0 of 1,000).

Every Simulator conversation became a ticket with an automatic title, priority and status. 'Export all' downloads an Excel file straight away with 16 columns per ticket, including the AI summary, status, language and CSAT, but not the conversation messages themselves.

Knowledge sources can be a live URL, web search, a website import, a file (PDF, Word or Excel only), text, or 'Ask a team member'. Parts of the interface showed Dutch text next to English, and once text we typed into the description landed in the name field.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 on the Free plan, with no card, no top-up and nothing published: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We had MindStudio's built-in Architect build an agent that pulls record IDs and dates out of four made-up records (one without a date) and tried to run it. The run failed for lack of credit, so the extraction itself was not tested.
findings: The Free plan in the app lists 'One Agent' and '1,000 runs / month', but model usage is paid from a separate prepaid balance that starts at $0.00 on a new workspace (shown in red, 'Click to top up'). Topping up opens a card form with $10, $25, $100 and $500; we did not fill it in.

Our first run of our own agent, in the debugger, stopped while waiting for the model with 'You are out of usage credits' and 'Run Failed: insufficient_credits/balance'. There was no output, so we cannot say how well it extracts dates or whether it marks the record without a date as unknown.

'Generate Agent' started the built-in MindStudio Architect, which first asked three clarifying questions (date format, output format, several dates per record), then showed a readable plan with the rule to never infer, guess or fabricate dates, and built the agent in about one and a half minutes after 'Build'. The Architect's own debug log listed billing events of about $0.88 over ten steps, while our workspace balance stayed at $0.00. We were not shown a charge for this work.

The debugger logs every step with timings, the resolved variables, the full prompt sent and the model used (Claude 5.5 Sonnet at 0.5°); the error and its reason appear verbatim. The Architect added a second agent next to the empty first one, although Free names 'One Agent'; both were drafts.

Onboarding offered two ways to connect AI models: the recommended Service Router ('Charged only when agents run', at provider rates without markup) or your own API keys. We chose the Service Router and did not try our own keys.

We found no export or download option for an agent in the editor. The debugger shows 'Open Script' for the workflow and the Architect run has 'Copy for LLM', which copies the conversation; we did not test these further.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 6 November 2026 on the free plan: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We asked one research question, read the answer and its sources, opened the export options and the bibliography view, and read the plan and checkout screens. We stopped before payment. findings: The sidebar showed '10 / 10 Pro messages left'. One question used one Pro message and the counter read 9 / 10.

Question: 'Does regular physical activity reduce the risk of depression in adults?' The answer said yes, with a 17% to 25% lower risk. The Consensus Meter, based on 19 papers, showed Yes 100%. A note says it 'may not be a perfect reflection of the current science'.
We checked the top source (Pearce et al., JAMA Psychiatry, 2022) and it matches the published paper. Other cited papers also exist. One sentence repeated a citation twice.

Export offers the 18 cited papers by default, the top 20, or all 49 papers on Pro. Formats are CSV, RIS and a bibliography in APA, MLA, Chicago, Harvard, BibTeX and AMA. The APA view had formatting slips: doubled full stops after titles, a space before a final full stop and a journal name not in title case.
The upgrade screen preselects Annual. Pro is $12 a month billed yearly ($144) or $20 monthly. The Free column says 'without any AI analysis' and lists 10 Pro messages a month in the same column.
Monthly Pro checkout read EUR 18.61 for the Netherlands, with annual billing offered at EUR 133.98 a year. No VAT line showed before card entry.

sessions.what: We trained one monitored robot on Browse AI's Free plan on 13 November 2026, using its AI-assisted Table Studio on a public practice shop, books.toscrape.com, category Travel. The account is ours, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We joined an existing Free account, so we did not see sign-up. We did not test export, integrations, support, checkout or cancellation.
findings: The start screen offered 'Extract structured data' or 'Monitor for changes'. We chose monitoring. Three training methods followed: Table Studio (AI training, labelled Beta), Robot Studio (point and click) and a Chrome extension. We used Table Studio and installed nothing. No card was requested.

Table Studio trained itself and returned a table called Books List after about 35 seconds (our approximate timing, not a benchmark): 11 rows with position, title, price, availability, rating, URL and cover image. We checked the result against the live page. All 11 prices matched, and the category holds exactly 11 books.

Save Robot asked how often to check for changes: hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. We chose daily and switched email alerts on data changes off. The robot saved and fetched fresh data from the live page. The Monitor tab then read 'Every day, No changes'.

Training the robot was free. The first run, 11 rows, cost 1.10 credits in the task history. That fits the pricing line of 1 credit per task with 10 list items included plus 0.10 per extra item. At one run a day this list would use about 33 credits a month (our own arithmetic), inside the free allowance.
The billing page showed 60 monthly credits on Free, for 2 websites, with 58.90 available after the first run. Our dossier had said 50, so we corrected it to what the app shows.

The plan cards offered yearly billing with 20% off and all credits paid upfront: Personal $19 a month, Professional $69 a month, Premium from $500 a month. We did not see monthly prices and opened no checkout, so tax, renewal terms and the payable total are unknown.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 28 October 2026 on the free trial: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We logged three time entries with known durations, set a billable rate, exported the reports, tried to import one export again and opened the upgrade without paying.
findings: Signing up at track.toggl.com put us in the new Toggl Focus app. After three onboarding screens a dialog said 'The whole product is unlocked for 31 days' and 'No credit card needed'; the pricing page we read on 25 October says a 30-day trial. The upgrade screen gave the trial end as November 28.

Our three entries (a 2m 18s timer, 15:00 and 1:30 by hand) added up to exactly 18m 48s in the report breakdown. The summary tiles rounded that to 19m, while the day header in the timer list showed 18m.

A project with a $60 hourly rate turned the 15-minute entry into $15.00 and 79.79% billable, both correct. Billable rates are one of eight features the project view labels as unlocked by the Premium trial.

The Time logs CSV kept all three entries to the second, with project, client and amount on the right row. The Summary CSV matches the screen when the report uses Breakdown by Project: 3:48 without a project and 15:00 on the test project. Under the default Breakdown by Member it listed all 0:18:48 under the project of the first entry, a project the screen did not show in that view (retest 19 November 2026). Every export format (PDF, CSV, XLSX) carries a paid-feature star.

Importing our own Time logs export again did not work as is: the importer asked for a duration column, could not use the combined start-and-stop column, and read the export's '-' placeholders as names, so all three entries would have been skipped. We stopped before importing; there is no ID column to update by.

Monthly prices in the app were $12 for Starter and $24 for Premium per license ($9 and $16 a month billed yearly). Choosing Premium warned that 'your current trial will finish immediately', so we stopped there. After the trial the app says you can 'keep going free — no charge', and the Free plan allowed up to 5 members in the app; the pricing FAQ (read 22 October) says 3 users, so count on 3.
The invite dialog offers Workspace admin, Manager, Member, Time tracker and Guest, with no role preselected. Billing lists 'Change plan' and 'Cancel trial' in the plan menu.

Export and members on the Free plan after the trial ends

sessions.what: We ran the import ourselves instead of summarising Capsule's help pages. We created the account; everything after that was measured in the product. We built a deliberately messy CSV: 24 rows, one row repeated with a different job title and phone number, and one row carrying nothing but an organisation name: imported it with “Import and update duplicates” and the overwrite box ticked, and then tried to undo it. The account was a fresh one on the 14-day premium trial, so nothing below is a free-plan restriction.
findings: 24 rows became 34 contacts. Capsule creates a separate Organisation record for every distinct organisation name in the file: 22 people plus 12 organisations. Nobody warns you, and it matters: the free plan stops at 250 contacts, so a 24-row spreadsheet costs 34 of them.
A row with only the Organisation column filled does build a company record on its own. Our “Solitary Holdings BV” row arrived as an organisation with its phone number attached.

The duplicate row wins. Anna Bakker went in twice, second time as “Head of Marketing” instead of “Marketing Lead”, and the record ended up with the later title. So the last occurrence in the file overwrites the earlier one, inside a single import.

But “overwrite” means exactly the four fields it names (name, job title, organisation and custom fields) and nothing else. The two rows carried different phone numbers and the contact now holds BOTH, sitting side by side. Contact channels are appended, not replaced, so a bad update pass leaves duplicate numbers on the record rather than wrong ones.

We could not find an undo or bulk-delete action in the screens we checked during this trial. The import history logs '34 total imported, 34 contacts created' and offers View and Close; View opens a saved filter with those 34 contacts, whose bulk actions were Tag, Create Campaign and Export. We found no delete on that list, on the full contact list, on the contact record or on its edit screen.
We did not establish that Capsule has no recovery route. Test a small import first and check the available rollback options before updating real contacts.

Export (select all > ... > Export) put a download link in the Notifications menu within a few seconds: a CSV with 14 columns, and all three subscribers came back with name and tags, including the automatic import tag.

Right after the five onboarding questions, a window opened with card fields and 'Subscribe to the Creator Plan', with the yearly plan ($390) preselected over monthly ($39). It closes with the cross, and the trial then runs without a card ('14 / 14 days remaining in trial'). The website field had been prefilled with the domain of our email address.

sessions.what: A 14-day trial of Freshservice for Business Teams on the Pro plan, set up for an HR team. Note the variant: this is Freshworks' service desk for HR, finance and facilities, priced separately from the IT edition whose plans this review lists. We sent six HR requests by email to the desk's default address: a missing payslip, a parental-leave request with a date, 'URGENT: my salary was not paid today' (rent due tomorrow), a request to change the bank account for salary payments, a remote-work policy question, and the payslip email a second time as a duplicate. We changed no default setting first, so this is what a team gets on day one.
findings: Email-to-ticket worked: all six emails became tickets (CASE-1 to CASE-6) within seconds, and the sender got a 'Ticket Received' confirmation for each within the same minute.

Every ticket came in at priority Low with the same deadlines: first response by 13 October, five days and seven hours after we wrote, and resolution by 20 October. That includes the unpaid-salary email, which the subject line itself marked URGENT. Out of the box nothing reads urgency from the text; you have to build rules for it.

Freddy AI Copilot, available in the Pro trial, summarised the urgent ticket correctly in two lines and named the urgency ('an urgent need as his rent is due tomorrow'). The summary did not change the priority or the deadline: the AI saw what the triage did not act on.
The duplicate was not caught. The second identical payslip email opened its own ticket, and its Related tickets tab read 'No related tickets yet'.
The bank-account change, a request payroll teams treat as a fraud risk, was handled like any other ticket: same priority, no verification step, no flag.
not_tested: the IT edition, the paid plans after the trial, the employee portal, approvals, automation rules we could have written ourselves, and replies sent from the desk

The Subscription page showed the $39 plan with a 7-day trial and the limits as the dossier says, and a dialog with the usage rates; Start 7-day free trial kept spinning and led to a login page of the vendor, so the Shopify approval screen was not reached and nothing was approved. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the App Store listing (English) was used and the install form was submitted in our own tab at 18:41; the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked. There was no plan choice and no payment screen at the install. The app opened directly on Create with Atlas AI with three choices (Store, Product pages, Landing pages); the sidebar of the app had Your Pages, Bundle Deals, Cart Upsells and Subscription. No password, card, phone number or sign-up form of the vendor was asked. The admin was in English. Core action, one AI product page for the product Demo Mug: Product pages, Demo Mug ticked (1 product selected), Continue setup, the template Atlas Default (Universal) (Used by 174,553 stores), Continue setup, Upload research (Optional) skipped, Continue setup, then Researching your product... and Writing your page.... The result stood there at 18:43, about 1 minute 30 seconds after the install and 9 clicks. The editor showed the page of Demo Mug with $9.50, four labels, 10,000+ next to the stars, the line Sarah and 438 people purchased, a sample review card that says This is a sample review, please input your genuine customer review and 25 in stock. The store had no such numbers: they are invented placeholder social proof in the preview, recorded here as an observation. The buttons were Save as draft and Upgrade to publish; Save as draft was clicked and nothing was published. After that every generate button on the home page of the app said Upgrade to generate (Full store, Product page and so on) and the setup guide said 1 out of 4 steps completed. Plans in the app: the Subscription page showed the Atlas base plan, $39 per month, All features included, only pay more as your business grows, with a button Start 7-day free trial. Included: published product and landing pages up to 10, bundle revenue up to $1,000, cart orders up to 250. The text says that if the usage is exceeded, the usage rates are charged. Usage rates (read in the app, they answer the open dossier question about them): published pages, Base up to 10 included, up to 15 +$10 a month, up to 25 +$20, up to 50 +$30, up to 75 +$40, up to 100 +$50, unlimited +$70; bundler, Base up to $1,000 included, up to $2,500 +$10, up to $5,000 +$20, up to $10,000 +$35, up to $20,000 +$65, up to $35,000 +$110, up to $50,000 +$150 and above $50,000 +$195 a month. Checkout: NOT reached. Start 7-day free trial was clicked; the button kept spinning for more than 20 seconds and the Shopify screen Approve subscription did not appear. A next click (closing the rates dialog) sent the tab to the login page of the vendor (app.helloatlas.io/api/auth), which only said Enter your shop domain to log in or install this app.; nothing was entered. No test charge was seen, nothing was approved, no card was entered and nothing was paid. The app home was blank several times (about 30 seconds, directly by address and from the sidebar) and loaded after a detour. Cancelling: no plan was started, so a stop of the billing could not be tested. The uninstall route is Settings, Apps, the menu of Atlas, Uninstall; the dialog says that after uninstalling any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information; a reason for uninstalling is required before the button works. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the start of Attribuly on a Shopify development store: the install, a welcome survey and then four screen steps to a wall. The first screen offered only Klaviyo, MambaSMS, Omnisend and CartSee, with Book a Demo for stores on another e-mail platform; the onboarding asked to connect a Klaviyo account and its Continue button stayed greyed out; the link for an attribution-only set-up did nothing when clicked twice. So the first result was not reached, no plan or checkout screen was seen, and the prices come from the listing and not from a test. The uninstall dialog was seen and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:00; the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked at about 19:01. The app went through a page of the vendor (Verifying your session authorization) and was open at about 19:02. Welcome to Attribuly asked how we first heard about it (Shopify App Store was chosen) and had a required field about what we searched for; a popup about a new attribution template was closed. No password, card or phone number was asked. The admin was in English. Core action, set up abandoned-cart recovery or attribution: NOT reached. At about 19:04 the screen Choose your ESP offered Klaviyo (Selected), MambaSMS, Omnisend and CartSee, with the line Not using above ESPs or want to identify anonymous visitors? Book a Demo and the line Only want to use Attribution? Click here to set up. The link Click here to set up was clicked twice and did nothing visible (no new page and no new tab). Start email recovery led to the onboarding Find the shoppers Klaviyo can't see, with four steps (Connect Klaviyo, Select events, Enable App embed, Activate Klaviyo flow) and the text Connect your Klaviyo account to start recovering missed revenue; the button Continue stayed greyed out as long as no Klaviyo account was connected. Connecting Klaviyo was not done, because it needs an account at another vendor. So there were 4 screen steps up to the wall, about 5 minutes after the start, and no first result: no recovery e-mail, no attribution view and no measurement. What the app looked like in Shopify after the install (Manage app): Pixels Disconnected, Extensions 0 active, Expiring access tokens Missing, Enforced IP restrictions Enforced; access to Online Store, Customers and Discounts (view and edit), Orders and Products (view only) and Marketing and Store analytics (view and edit). Plans: no plan choice and no subscription screen was seen in the app, because the onboarding blocked first. The charges address of the app in Shopify (charges, pricing plans) gave There's no page at this address. The Shopify screen Approve subscription was not reached, so nothing was approved. From the App Store listing of 17 November (not a test result): Free plan available and Free trial available; Free recovers $1000 of e-mail revenue and has multi-touch attribution, new customer CPA benchmarks by cohort and a missed revenue audit for Klaviyo or another ESP; Pro $99 a month and Enterprise $219 a month, both charged based on the GMV (with Capture, to identify anonymous visitors, as an add-on on Enterprise), with a 7-day free trial on both; all charges in USD, recurring and usage-based charges billed every 30 days. Difference with the dossier (from the listing, not from the app): the dossier of 14 October gives ReCapture at $100 a month plus a 10% revenue share and Capture at $450 a month flat; the listing now shows Pro $99 and Enterprise $219, GMV based, so the dossier prices are out of date or renamed; the rating on the listing is 4.8 from 172 reviews (the dossier says 167). The price fields are not changed here; this is for the price bundle. Checkout: NOT reached, no plan screen and no Shopify approval screen were seen, no card was entered and nothing was paid. Cancelling: no paid plan ran, so nothing could be cancelled; the uninstall dialog was seen: it says that after uninstalling any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information, and it has a list of reasons (Testing multiple apps, Too expensive and others). Not tested: connecting Klaviyo or Omnisend, abandoned-cart recovery, e-mail, anonymous visitors (Capture), the attribution dashboard, the app embed, the ROI guarantee, paid plans, payment, a plan choice in the app and Book a Demo. Clean up: Attribuly was uninstalled at about 19:12 with the reason Testing multiple apps and no longer appeared in the list of installed apps; other apps were not touched; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The set-up needed a connected account at another vendor (Klaviyo) before Continue worked; the link for an attribution-only set-up did nothing; stores on other e-mail platforms were pointed to Book a Demo; no plan or price was shown in the app; and the charges address of the app in Shopify gave an empty page.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested AutoWrite on a Shopify development store: the install (with an error on the first open that went away after a reload), one SEO blog post made on the Free plan in 4 steps without a card (1500 words, a featured image, Content quality 95/100, status Draft), the usage counter (1 / 10), a brand voice saved on Free, and the plan screen on which Starter, Pro and Business were Not available on a development store. The generation screen did not refresh by itself and the text appeared only after a reload, about 3 minutes after the start. Publishing, automations and the paid plans were not tested, and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:05; the Shopify dialog Install app asked only for View staff and contributor data (store owner, blog contributors) and View and edit store data (products, Online Store). No card was asked. The install was done at about 19:07. First open: the first screen after the install was an error, Application Error: Cannot coerce the result to a single JSON object. The result contains 0 rows. Code: PGRST116. After reloading the same address the dashboard opened normally (Total Posts 0, Published 0, Scheduled 0). It looks like a first-time error while the store record was being created; it was not seen again. The admin was in English. Core action, make an SEO blog post: on the Free plan, Posts, Create New Post, Create with AI, the topic How to choose a snowboard for beginners, Generate post: 4 steps, no keyword and no product chosen. The screen stayed on This post is still generating, with a line that a generation stuck for a long time may have failed silently, and empty text; it did not refresh by itself, and the text appeared only after reloading the page, about 3 minutes after the start. A message about unsaved changes blocked leaving the page until Discard was clicked; the post stayed. Result: the title How to Choose Your First Snowboard (and Avoid Bad Advice), 1500 words with 5 H2 and 6 H3 headings, an excerpt, a generated featured image of snowboards, status Draft, and Content quality 95/100 with checks for length, SEO title, meta description, headings, URL handle (a warning), readability (Flesch 83/100), AI filler phrases, sentence rhythm and active voice, plus Version History (1). The text reads well but opens with an invented anecdote and has no sources and no store products (product references are a Pro feature). The score is the app's own and was not checked by a second tool. The post was not published to the blog; it stayed a draft in the app. Counter: Usage & Plan showed Posts generated 0 / 10 and Images generated 0 / 10 before the post and 1 / 10 for both after it. What is included on Free: 10 posts and 10 images every 30 days, 1 automation, Basic SEO; usage window 17-11-2026 to 17-12-2026. The vendor FAQ, as read before the test, says 3 posts for the free plan; the app and the plan screen say 10. Plans: Manage plan opened the Shopify screen Select a plan. Free to test: these plans are free to test on this store, regular pricing applies when the store goes live; Free with a Select button. Under Unavailable on dev stores: Starter $9 / 30 days, Pro $29 / 30 days and Business $79 / 30 days, all with a greyed out Not available. The amounts and contents match the dossier and the listing (the listing of 17 November: Free, Starter $9, Pro $29, Business $79, all charges billed in USD, no reviews yet). Because paid plans cannot be picked on a development store, no Approve subscription or test charge screen was reached, nothing was approved, nothing was paid and no card was asked. Difference with the dossier: the dossier lists brand voices and auto-publish as Starter features; on Free, Settings, Brand voices accepted a new voice (name, tone, custom instructions, banned words, preferred words) and showed Brand voice saved and 1 voice, Test voice, professional. Whether a saved voice is used in a generation or an automation on Free was not tested. Automations on Free: the page showed No automations yet with a Create automation button; not tested (the plan says 1 automation). Cancelling: Free plan, no subscription to cancel; the uninstall dialog (Settings, Apps, AutoWrite, Uninstall) says that the app can no longer be used, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information; a reason is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). Not tested: publishing to the Shopify blog, scheduling in the calendar, automations, bulk generation, keyword research, product or collection references, Google grounding, other languages, paid plans and checkout. Clean up: the test brand voice and the draft post existed only in the app and went away with the uninstall; AutoWrite no longer appeared in the list of installed apps; other apps were not touched; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.

The next screen, Finish your setup to start selling, offered only Plus (7 days free, then $79 a month) and Flex (pay as you go). There was no way to the catalogue without one of them.
The Shopify approval screen for Flex asked to approve usage charges up to $79,00 per 30 days, with an Add payment method row and a greyed out Approve button.
The listing shows a free level, Beginner at $29 and Pro at $49. In our test (17 Nov 2026) the onboarding did not offer them.
No Zendrop account was made. The app was uninstalled after the test; nothing was paid.

A sample or an order, and the refund route.
The Beginner and Pro plans and the free level on the listing, which the onboarding did not offer.
The Plus trial and the Black Friday deal.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 we installed Securify on a Shopify development store and blocked one country with a single click, about 3 minutes after the install. The rule was not enforced because the theme app embed stayed off. We paid, approved and saved nothing. The full run is in the exit test section below.
findings: Text we checked: "Unlimited Blocked Visitors". What we saw: The listing shows unlimited blocked visitors on the Free plan; in the app the Free plan blocks 500 visitors a month (the header showed 0 / 500 blocked visitors, resets Dec 17) and unlimited blocked visitors is a Pro feature.

Text we checked: "Unlimited High-risk order alerts". What we saw: The listing shows unlimited high-risk order alerts; the Free card says An alert for every risky order but only Review 5 risky orders a month, and Order Protection showed 0 of 5 for the Free plan.

Text we checked: "Unlimited visitor logs". What we saw: The listing shows unlimited visitor logs; the Free card says the last 1,000 visitor logs and 7 days of analytics, Pro the last 2,000 logs, and Unlimited visitor logs is listed under Growth.

Text we checked: "AI-powered advanced bot blocking". What we saw: The listing shows AI-powered advanced bot blocking; the Free card lists no bot blocking, Pro lists VPN, proxy & datacenter blocking and Good-bot management, and Smart bot blocking is listed under Growth. Bot blocking was not tried.

Text we checked: "Brazil / BR / Remove". What we saw: One click on Brazil on the world map turned it red (User Blocked) and added the row Brazil, BR, Remove to Current Restrictions (1) at once, in 1 click and about 3 minutes after the install; the rule was removed afterwards (Current Restrictions (0)).

Turning on the app embed and seeing the block page on the storefront.
An IP rule, an email block and fraud alerts on real orders.
VPN and bot blocking and the live visitor log.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested GeoStock on a Shopify development store: the install, a three step onboarding on the Free plan, two of three locations chosen, the app embed and the block Product inventory added in the theme editor, and the stock per location on a product page. The first result came after about 5 minutes and about 30 steps and showed My Custom Location 50, but the app said that 1 of the 2 selected locations was no longer valid and not published, so the second location never showed, and a product stocked only there showed Not Available. The Basic approval screen asked for a payment method and was cancelled. The theme was put back and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:20; the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and Install was clicked. The app is called GeoStock Inventory By Location in the admin and GeoStock: Multi Location Stock in the App Store. We went straight into the app, with no payment step. No card was asked. The admin was in English. Onboarding in 3 steps: Which stores should shoppers see (3 Shopify locations offered, with the line 0 selected, Free publishes up to 2), Add GeoStock to your store (the app embed and an inventory block), and Setup complete. Core action, show stock per location on a product page: 2 of the 3 locations were chosen, the app embed was switched on and the block Product inventory was added to Product information in the theme editor (in our own tab) and saved, which is needed to see the result. The first result in the preview came at about 19:25, about 5 minutes after the install and about 30 steps, many of them navigation in the theme editor. At first the block showed only Not Available on the products tried (Appointment, 3p Fulfilled Snowboard, Hydrogen). On The Collection Snowboard: Hydrogen, which has 50 available at the Shop location in Shopify, the block kept showing Not Available. In the app, the page Store locator showed 1 selected location(s) are no longer valid and are not published. Choose replacements. next to 2 of 2 locations selected (the location names were not visible in the list). Save locations gave Locations saved., but the warning stayed. On The Multi-location Snowboard the preview then showed My Custom Location 50; the Shop location did not appear. So stock per location works for one of the two chosen locations, and the other was not published; a product stocked only there showed Not Available. Why the second location counted as no longer valid was not found. Plans: the app screen Plan & billing showed Current plan Free, 2 locations, Standard design, 14 trial day(s) remaining, and a button Start a trial with Shopify Basic Plan $9.99/month; Free includes a store locator with up to 2 locations, search, directions, e-mail and business hours, and the standard design. Only Basic could be chosen in the app; a Plus Plan at $29.99 was not offered in the app. The App Store listing of 17 November says Free plan available and Free trial available, with a rating of 4.8 (80). Checkout: Start a trial opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: Base Plan, $9,99 USD every 30 days, a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec, Subtotal $9,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $9,99 due 1 Dec, and Add payment method, with Approve greyed out. The sentence that you will not be billed for this test charge was not there and a payment method was asked, so nothing was approved; Cancel was clicked, no card was entered and nothing was paid. Difference with the dossier: the dossier says there is no free plan, but the app and the listing have a Free plan with a store locator for up to 2 locations; the rating on the listing is 4.8 from 80 reviews while the dossier says 4.9 from 99. The price fields are not changed here; this is for the price bundle. Cancelling: no subscription was started; the uninstall dialog (Settings, Apps, GeoStock, Uninstall) says that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and requires a reason (Testing multiple apps was chosen). Not tested: the Plus Plan (not offered in the app), a custom theme integration, batch loading with many locations, back-in-stock alerts (Notify me), the store locator map, detecting the nearest store from the visitor's location, and the paid Basic features. Clean up: in the theme the block Product inventory was removed and the app embed was switched off and saved, so the theme is as before the test; GeoStock was uninstalled with the reason Testing multiple apps and no longer appeared in the list of installed apps; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Free plan available. Free trial available". What we saw: The app and the listing offer a Free plan with a store locator for up to 2 locations (shown on the plan screen as Free, 2 locations, Standard design), while the dossier says there is no free plan.

Text we checked: "My Custom Location 50". What we saw: After the block Product inventory was added and saved, the preview of The Multi-location Snowboard showed the line My Custom Location 50, so stock per location does show on the product page for one location.

After clocking out, 'Earlier Today' listed 9:09pm Web Clock In and 9:11pm Web Clock Out, but the Total Hours counter on the clock page jumped back to 00h 00m 00s.

sessions.what: We built one small app in Devs.ai's App Builder on the Free plan on 13 November 2026 and read the cost in its Analytics screen. The account is ours, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We deployed and shared nothing: the app sits in the account as a draft. We did not test checkout, support, export or cancellation.
findings: The App Builder asks 'What do you want to build?' with a model picker set to GPT-5.5, a Plan first option and templates such as CRM, Analytics Dashboard and HR Portal. The Free plan showed unlimited users and no card.

We typed one sentence: a tool for a small support team where you paste a customer email, pick a tone and get a short polite reply draft. After about three and a half minutes the app was ready, with an email field, a tone picker, a Generate button and a Copy button.

We pasted a made-up customer email about being charged twice. Within about ten seconds the app returned a polite draft that apologised, asked for the account email and the payment dates, and did not promise a refund up front.

Analytics, the vendor's own meter, showed $1.01 in total after the test: $1.00 for the build chat (1.1 million tokens, GPT-5.5) and $0.01 for the app's assistant (5.8K tokens, Grok 4.6). The upgrade page lists Personal at $15 per seat a month including $10 of usage, and Business at $30 including $21. We did not see a rate for usage above the included amount on that page. We did not check the meter against an independent source.
The upgrade page shows a yearly option labelled Save 16%. We did not open checkout, so tax, renewal terms and the payable total are unknown.

findings: Sign-up works only with a mobile number and a six-digit SMS code ('Sign in with email' is for existing users).
