We created the account; everything after that was measured in the product: funnels built and published one by one until the walls appeared, with the wall text copied out word for word. involve.me contributed nothing to this test: no account, no briefing, no sight of the draft. We do carry an affiliate link to them, disclosed on this page, and the test was run on the free plan we signed up for ourselves.
findings: The free plan allows exactly 2 live funnels. We published two, and the third stopped with: “You have reached your limit of 2 live funnels. Please end any live funnels or upgrade your plan to publish more funnels.” The dialog puts an Upgrade plan button next to Publish now.
A second user is not a paid extra on free, it is nothing at all: “You don't have any team member seats on your plan. Upgrade for more.” There is no referral credit or trial seat.

The AI funnel builder works on the free plan, and it is the real product. One sentence — “build a 4-question quiz that helps a marketer pick a CRM” — produced a five-page funnel with a theme applied, questions, scoring and a result page, and it asked for approval before each risky edit. The comparison table lists “Create funnels with AI” as a Start-plan benefit, so this is more generous than the tier pages suggest.

A free account has no usage panel. “Plans & Billing” in the account menu goes straight to the upgrade page: no current plan, no counters, no AI-credit balance. You cannot find out what you have left; you discover a limit by hitting it.

Free publishing gives you a real subdomain and a choice of ten: daanV.involve.me plus quizzes.cx, forms.ac, calculators.cx, assessments.cx, tests.cx, surveys.so, feedback.ac, funnels.cx, researched.cx and paynow.cx. Every page carries involve.me branding; removing it is a paid step the share screen labels PRO, while the plan is actually called Grow.

The in-app comparison table publishes limits the public pricing page does not: funnel visits a month (10,000 / 25,000 / 100,000), contacts collected a month (300 / 1,000 / 3,000), file storage, embeds, payment accounts, and the price of every top-up. If you are sizing a plan, that table is the one to read.
Prices differ by surface: the public page quotes $29 / $69 / $139 and “Save up to 40%”, the in-app upgrade screen quotes €29 / €69 / €139 and “Save up to 41%”.

Onboarding is compulsory and is itself an involve.me funnel embedded in the app: four questions, carrying the “Made with involve.me” badge. You cannot reach the builder until you finish it. One of the answer options for “How did you discover involve.me?” is “AI - Claude”.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on the free Studio trial: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We generated a two-sentence script ('Dr. Maya Chen checked seventeen cobalt valves in Rotterdam. The warranty lasts thirty-seven days.'), replayed it, changed only the speed, then changed only one word, reading the voice-generation meter after each step, and opened the export dialog.
findings: The script stayed in one sub-block. The default voice was Ruby (US English) in the 'Angry' style, and the meter started at 00:10:00.
Three generations of 7.1, 6.4 and 6.3 seconds of audio (19.8 seconds in total) took the meter from 10:00 to 9:46, so 14 seconds of the free 10 minutes were used.
Replaying the same audio cost nothing: the meter stayed at 00:09:59.
The on-screen meter lags. After the one-word change it still showed 00:09:52, and only after a page reload did it show 00:09:46, so read it after reloading.

Because of that lag we cannot split the 14 seconds exactly per step. The most likely split, about 8 seconds for the first generation, nothing for the speed change and about 6 for the word change, fits Murf's help text: delivery settings on unchanged text are free, and a text edit regenerates the whole sub-block.

Downloads are blocked on the free trial. The export dialog lists MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG and other formats up to 48 kHz, but has no download button, only 'Unlock unlimited downloads - You are on free plan' with 'Upgrade Plan'.

sessions.what: A new free account, used in the web app in Chrome. We uploaded four files we made ourselves with known SHA-256 checksums: a 9.6 KB text note, 1 MB and 8 MB files of random bytes, and a small text file named 'naam met spaties en é.txt' to test spaces and an accented letter. We created a public link for the 1 MB file, opened it in a separate browser that was not signed in to Proton, then downloaded all four files again and compared them byte for byte with the originals.
findings: All four files came back identical: the same size and the same SHA-256 checksum as the originals, and the file name with spaces and an accented letter was unchanged, byte for byte.

The new account started at 2 GB, not 5 GB. A pop-up offered a 3 GB welcome bonus, and after we uploaded files and created a share link the meter showed 5 GB. The same pop-up still said '29 days left to claim' afterwards.

The public link opened for a visitor without a Proton account and offered the file for download. The decryption key is the part of the link after the '#': the same link without it showed a password prompt instead, so a chat app or mail client that cuts off that part leaves the recipient stuck.
Setting an expiry date and a password on a link is available on the free plan; we opened both settings but did not save them.

sessions.what: A new free account, with no payment method asked for. We ran nine texts whose authorship we knew before we started: three passages from public-domain books (Darwin and William James), a paragraph one of us typed for the test, typos included, three paragraphs a language model wrote for our own reviews, one paragraph Claude wrote on the spot, and one of those machine paragraphs with three of its five sentences rewritten by Claude. We read the credit meter after every check and ran it into the daily limit.
findings: Nine for nine. All four human texts came back 'Human Written', including the 71-word paragraph typed for the test, and all five machine texts came back 'AI Generated', including the paragraph Claude wrote on the spot. Every result put the whole text on one side: the gauge read 100% each time. That figure is the share of the text it assigns to each side, not a confidence score.

A machine rewrite did not shake it. With three of its five sentences rewritten by a second model, the paragraph from our Hubstaff review still scored 100% AI. That measures a model paraphrasing a model; we did not test text a person had edited by hand.

Later the same day we gave it a tenth text: a deliberately clichéd AI paragraph after QuillBot's AI Humanizer had rewritten it (the Humanizer reported '0 AI signals'). Pangram still scored it 100% AI and added a note that the text 'appears to have been paraphrased or rewritten', pointing to one rewritten segment. Our own Claude rewrite of a review paragraph, earlier in the test, did not get that note.

Short texts carry a caveat, and very short ones are refused. Every text of 190 words or fewer was marked 'Confidence limited — short text'; the 224-word passage was not. Below 50 words the button stays grey, with 'Minimum 50 words required for accurate detection', and nothing is charged.

The 2,000 words a day are 20 credits of 100 words, rounded up per check. A 190-word text cost 2 credits and a 222-word text cost 3. Our first six checks came to 1,014 words and used 13 credits, the allowance for 1,300 words. At around 150 words a check, a day holds ten checks, not twenty. The cost shows next to the button before you click, and the balance sits at the top of the page.

Hitting the limit loses nothing. With 3 credits left, a 333-word text (4 credits) could still be submitted. A window then said the entry would cost 4 credits against the 3 remaining and offered the paid plans. Nothing was scanned and nothing was charged: the balance stayed at 3. The window does not say when the credits come back, and it does not offer to trim the text to what you have left.
Signed in and signed out, the pricing page shows the same amounts. The Professional button now reads 'Upgrade to Professional', with '$65 billed now' underneath, so that tier still has no trial.
not_tested: text that mixes human and AI writing, text a person edited by hand, languages other than English, anything longer than 224 words, the plagiarism check (paid plans only), image detection and the API

Three of the four human texts are famous public-domain passages a detector may well have seen before. The paragraph typed for the test is the stronger evidence, and it is a single paragraph of 71 words.

sessions.what: A new free account in ngram's v2 studio. We pasted the link to one of our own published reviews (ActiveCampaign) with a one-line brief, asked for 30 seconds, ran the same prompt twice and read the credit meter before and after each run.
findings: The new account opened with 1,200 credits, while ngram's pricing page (read the same day) lists the Free plan at 600 one-time credits. We report what the meter showed; we do not know why it was double.

The composer states the rate plainly: 10 credits a second, billed on the generated duration. It reserved 300 credits for a 30-second request, but both videos came out slightly long, at 32.5 and 32 seconds, and were charged 330 and 320 credits. The meter went 1,200 to 870 to 550, matching those charges exactly. The 32.5-second video was charged 330 credits, equivalent to 33 seconds at the displayed rate; we did not establish the rounding rule.

From the link alone it read the page, picked up the site's own colours, type and logo, and wrote a scene-by-scene storyboard with the narration script in about a minute and a half. Nothing was charged until we approved that plan, which is the moment to catch a wrong claim.

Every figure in both scripts matched the review: $15 a month as the floor, and $149, $189, $375 and $589 at 10,000 contacts, as read on 29 September 2026. It declined to animate prices between those two points because the review does not print them, and it kept the review's attribution on the contact-billing rule (credited to SendX in one run, labelled as reported in the other).

The same prompt gave a different video each time: five scenes in the first run, four in the second, with different wording and visuals. The facts stayed the same, but do not expect a repeat run to reproduce a video you liked.

Rendering took about six to seven and a half minutes after approval. The narration step failed once in each run and recovered on its own, and the second run said openly that it could not listen to its own voice-over and flagged one word that might sound clipped. Listen before you publish.

The visuals were motion graphics: the log showed ngram writing the scenes as an HTML animation and recording that, not generated camera footage. That suits explainers and product walkthroughs; it is not the tool for filmed-looking scenes.
Videos are private by default; sharing offers a public link, an embed, a download and direct posting to LinkedIn, X and YouTube, and captions are included.

sessions.what: We built a support agent from scratch with the description 'A customer support agent for Acme Headsets that answers customer questions using the attached help centre page', and gave it one public help-centre page of our own as its only knowledge: shipping countries and times, a 15:00 dispatch cut-off, returns, warranty, spare parts, two headsets with prices and support hours, with no phone line. We asked 13 questions, each in a new conversation on the agent's standalone chat page: ten the page answers, and three it does not (Japan, PayPal, and battery life with noise cancelling on). The first round ran without an account; after about ten conversations it stopped with 'This AI Agent has reached its conversation limit', so the last three, plus two repeats, ran on a new agent built the same way in a free Starter account.
findings: Eleven of 13 answers were right. Delivery times, the free-shipping threshold, the return window, free returns, the warranty exclusion, spare-part and headset prices and the 40-hour battery figure all matched the page.

It did not make things up when the page had no answer. It said it could not confirm PayPal, gave the 40-hour figure only for noise cancelling off and said it had no figure for it on, and inferred correctly that it does not ship to Japan because only the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany are listed.

It got the dispatch cut-off wrong. Asked about an order at 4 pm on a Tuesday, the first agent said it would not ship that day but not when it would; the second said it would ship the same day, because orders before 15:00 leave that day. The correct answer is Wednesday. The same question gave a different answer on a near-identical agent.

Asked 'Can I call you?', both agents said a representative had been asked to join and asked for an email address, instead of saying there is no phone support. With no live team behind it, that promise goes nowhere.
Adding the page once showed '2 links' in the knowledge base both times. The guest agent's conversation limit arrived after about ten chats; the free Starter plan lists 100 conversations a month.
not_tested: the website widget, WhatsApp, voice and phone channels, forms inside the chat, handover to a real person, or a larger knowledge base

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Fax.Plus, the fax product of Alohi, on the Free plan of an account we created. The free plan is 10 pages to send in total, not per month, and it has no fax number, so you cannot receive faxes without paying. A one-page fax to a made-up test number was ready to send in about 4 minutes and was deliberately not sent. From the Netherlands all prices showed in euros, with the same figures the dossier lists in dollars. Upgrade opened a checkout with Premium (Annual) at EUR 167.99 already chosen and a Dutch number that requires proof of ID; it was left with nothing filled in. Account and start: we created the account and entered the text message code himself; our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab, on 19 November 2026. A first attempt at 09:39 stopped at that code; the test resumed at 09:46 and ended at 09:51 CET. The interface was in English (lng=en). Alohi is a suite of separate products; this test covers Fax.Plus. The dossier name is Alohi and the review is on AIBM (b2b/alohi-review). The inbox showed 10 fax pages left, Get a Fax Number, Send Fax and one Welcome Fax from Fax.Plus, with a bar saying Receiving faxes requires a dedicated fax number. Core action, prepare an outgoing fax: Send Fax showed Remaining Pages: 10. The made-up US test number +1 202 555 0123 was entered as recipient, Add Page, Rich Text Editor made one text page, Test fax. Not sent., and Confirm added it as a 14.7 KB page. Send was active and was not clicked, so no fax went out and no page was used. This took about 4 minutes and 6 steps. Next to Add Page there are a Cover Sheet Generator and a Cover Sheet Gallery. There is no test number or test route: the 10 free pages are the trial. Numbers said No numbers, Add a number to receive faxes: a free fax number does not exist, so receiving needs a paid plan. Plan & Billing: Plan Type Free, Remaining Pages 10, Alohi AI 0 AI Credits, Current Credit EUR 0, Payment Method Not Available, Default Currency EUR. Plans: On fax.plus/pricing, annual billing, in euros from the Netherlands: Basic EUR 6.99 a month (EUR 83.99 a year) with 200 pages, 1 number, 1 member, EUR 0.10 per extra page and 60 pages per fax; Premium EUR 13.99 a month (EUR 167.99 a year, Recommended) with 500 pages, EUR 0.07 per extra page, 90 pages per fax, toll-free numbers and number porting; Business EUR 27.99 a month (EUR 335.99 a year) with 1,000 pages, 5 members, EUR 0.05 per extra page and 200 pages per fax; Enterprise EUR 79.99 a month (EUR 959.99 a year) with 4,000 pages, HIPAA with a BAA, SSO, API, EUR 0.03 per extra page and 250 pages per fax. The free plan in the comparison has 10 pages in total, EUR 0.20 per extra page, 30 pages per fax and no inbound faxes. An annual plan gives up to 3 months free (save up to 22%). An extra number is EUR 4.99 a month and a custom number EUR 19.99 once; the page says No setup fee. Checkout: Upgrade opened the checkout with Premium (Annual) EUR 167.99 (EUR 13.99 per month) preselected; step 2 Your Fax Number with Netherlands (Requires proof of ID) and a Random or Custom (EUR 19.99) number; step 3 Payment Details with card, PayPal, Google Pay and Apple Pay; step 4 billing address; Secure checkout powered by Stripe. The Order Summary still showed Nothing added yet and Total EUR 0 while it loaded. Nothing was filled in and nothing was paid. Cancelling: no paid plan, so no cancel button. The pricing FAQ says monthly plans renew each month and annual plans once a year and that changes can be made in the account settings; Plan & Billing on Free only shows Upgrade. The account stays on Free. Not tested: actually sending a fax (on purpose), receiving a fax (needs a paid number), Sign.Plus and Scan.Plus, and cancelling a paid plan. Clean up: the account stays on Free with 10 pages; the draft fax was not sent or saved. The own tab was closed and our tabs were not touched. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the 14-day Bókun Start trial, without a card, without any OTA, Viator or payment connection and without a website: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We set up a made-up walking tour (Wednesday 28 October, 10:00, 60 minutes, 4 seats, EUR 10 per person), made a back-office booking for 2 adults with a fictional contact and then cancelled it.
findings: After email verification, onboarding first asked about a card (we answered No), then required a plan choice to start the 14-day trial: Start $49 a month plus a 1.5% booking fee, Plus $149 plus 1.25%, Premium $499 plus 1.0% (5, 10 and unlimited users). The next screen asked for a card to start billing when the trial ends on 6 November 2026; 'I'll add card later' skipped it, and the dashboard opened with '14 days left on your Bókun Start free trial'.

Setting up the tour by hand took 2 minutes 38 seconds in a wizard (title, description, photos, time, booking cutoff, capacity, start times, calendar, pricing) with a counter of the steps still required. No OTA, Viator import or payment step was mandatory; adult and child prices had to be set separately.

A back-office booking for 2 adults with 'Pay later' was confirmed as not paid, EUR 20.00, and the departure dropped from 4 to 2 seats left. Cancelling asked for a reason and showed the cancellation policy ('Bookings are non-refundable'), with options to apply it and to skip the cancellation email; afterwards the booking showed Cancelled with time and reason, and the departure was back to 4 seats left.

Activating the tour set it to 'Public' straight away, followed by a message pointing to GetYourGuide, the Bókun Marketplace and other channels. None were connected, so what 'Public' means without a channel we did not check.
The back-office booking offered three payment routes: send a payment link, enter a payment manually, or pay later. We only used pay later.
not_tested: OTA distribution (Viator, GetYourGuide), the Bókun Marketplace and resellers
Real payments, payment links and the 1.5% booking fee
The booking widget or website as a customer sees it

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Contractor Foreman in the 30-day Basic annual trial that we started with our card. An estimate, a project and a task took about 4 minutes, but Basic has no daily log or scheduling module. The trial is set to bill $588 for a year, which the Paddle e-mail showed as $711.48 including tax. Cancelling in the app took four screens and a survey and keeps the trial until 19 December. Account and start: we created the account and started the 30-day trial of the Basic annual plan with his own card (Charged at End of Trial, Total Charged Today $0.00); a phone number was required at sign-up and we entered it. Our AI assistant ran the test in our browser on 19 November 2026 from 14:13. The interface was in English. The Account Setup popup asked required questions (accounting software, invoicing type, experience, help with set-up) and a Job Function; then a guide created a test customer and opportunity with made up details and said Your Test Records Are Ready! Core action, an estimate, a project and a task, from 14:13 to 14:17, about 4 minutes: estimate EST. #5 Test Kitchen Remodel got three manual items, cabinet installation 2 sets at $1,200, demolition labor 16 hours at $65 (the app said Labor cannot be Lump Sum in Estimate or SOV) and a quartz countertop at $3,400, for Total w/Tax: $6,840.00; it was not sent. Project TEST-001 was created for the test customer. Basic has no daily log or scheduling module (the feature list is Projects, To-Do's, Estimates, Invoices, Payments, Expenses, Takeoffs, Directory, Leads, Calendar, Files & Photos, Reports and Notes), so a To-Do was added to the project instead. Files & Photos holds sample folders and files; nothing was uploaded and Google Drive and Dropbox were not connected. Plans: Manage Subscription showed Current Plan: Basic: Annual Subscription, In Trial, Plan Amount $588.00, Started 11/19/2026, Trial Ends 12/19/2026 12:03 AM UTC, No Payments Processed, and that charges appear from the payment processor as PADDLE*CONTRFORMN. User Count 1, Users Available 0. Checkout: the trial checkout was done by us before the session and was not seen. Cancelling, done the same day: Settings, Manage Subscription, Cancel. Screen 1 asks why (we chose Couldn't Figure it Out); screen 2 offers Extend Trial By 14 Days (declined); screen 3 asks Anything we could have done better? with at least 45 characters (we typed a sentence about testing); screen 4, Final Confirmation, warns that you lose your data and offers a 1:1 session. No password. After Confirm & Cancel a seven-question Cancellation Request survey follows (reasons, ratings, would you come back, an optional feedback call for a $25 gift card); after Submit the app signs you out. Confirmation came by e-mail from Paddle, Subscription scheduled to cancel: Your trial will end on 19 Dec 2026, Basic (1 User) Annual, Amount $711.48/year (inc. tax). So the trial stays usable until 19 December and the annual charge is stopped; with tax the $588 plan is $711.48 for a Dutch buyer. Not tested: daily logs and scheduling, invoices and payments, QuickBooks, the client portal, invitations, more users and other plans. Clean up: the test customer, estimate EST. #5, project TEST-001 and the To-Do stay. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session first installed the Shopify app of Gelato on a development store, which sent us at once to a separate Gelato login, and then tested in the Gelato dashboard with the own Gelato our account. A Gildan 64000 T-shirt with the text Test Print reached the mockup and the Details step in about 6 minutes; Add to store needs a connected store, and a Manual store was enough. The product page showed €4.98 excl. VAT with 30% off the first order, delivery €3.99 and 4-5 business days to the Netherlands, and the shirt is made in 14 countries. The Gelato+ trial pop-up said Unlimited stores & users and that product discounts are not applied on the trial; the trial was not started, nothing was published, ordered or paid, and checkout and cancelling were not tested. Two attempts. First attempt, through the Shopify app: at 19:38 the install form of the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/gelato-print-on-demand, English) was submitted in our own tab and the Shopify screen Install app warned that Gelato: Print on Demand does not support market-driven shipping (you can switch back to legacy shipping profiles until July 1, 2027) and asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. After Install the app sent us in the same minute to the login of Gelato (Welcome back, with Apple, Facebook and Google or an e-mail and a password, and Dont have an account? Sign up). There was no automatic connection and no Connect button, so the app only opens with a separate Gelato account. Nothing was filled in, no account was made and the app was uninstalled afterwards (reason Testing multiple apps). Second attempt, in the Gelato dashboard with the own Gelato our account (not through the Shopify app, and the Gelato app was not installed in the development store): the dashboard was in English and showed the onboarding 3 simple steps to start selling (Connect your store, Create your first product, Order your first sample), the sidebar offer Try Gelato+ for free and a banner 30% off your first order. A first start at 20:14 was stopped at once on instruction; it was resumed at about 20:1x to 20:2x. Core action, a T-shirt with text up to the mockup, about 6 minutes and 14 steps: Create product, Single product led to Choose product with No templates here; in the Product catalog the page of the Gildan 64000 shirt has Add to store, which asks Connect your store to get started (Shopify, Etsy, Amazon, TikTok Shop, WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, BigCommerce, Manual), so a connected store is required. Manual was chosen (no outside account) with the store name Test Store typed by the tester, which made a store in Gelato. Then Create product, Single product, Bestsellers, Classic Unisex Crewneck T-shirt | Gildan 64000, and the wizard Product, Design, Details. The design editor showed a welcome pop-up (skipped), Add text was used and Test Print was typed; Continue to Details showed the mockup with Test Print on the chest, the title Classic Unisex Crewneck T-shirt | Gildan 64000 White, a description, a size table and care instructions, with Progress saved in Drafts. Nothing was published, ordered, sampled or paid and no address was entered. The draft was deleted with the menu and Delete (Yes, I want to delete product draft). Prices as shown: the product page said €4.98 excl. VAT in red, with the first order discount of 30% if placed in the next 47h 52m 14s, and delivery €3.99, 4-5 business days, Delivery to Netherlands. The catalogue said From € 8.51 excl. VAT and € 8.51 with Gelato+, and the wizard said From € 7.12 excl. VAT. The page also said No minimums, Ships in 4-5 days, 14 countries and Carbon-neutral; the shirt is made in AT, AU, CA, CZ, DE, FR, GB, IT, NL, NZ, PL, PT, SE and US (14 countries); the catalogue text said 680 products and 32 countries. No order was placed, so the real delivery time and the price at checkout were not tested. Plans: the App Store listing (read on 17 November 2026) says Free to install and Free trial available: Gelato Free (Pay for what you print; print on demand for global creators; hundreds of products to design and sell) and Gelato+ at $29.99 a month, or $239.88 a year and save 33% (up to 33% off products, exclusive tools, Magic Mockups, Instant Collections, Price Navigator, Product Migration with Velocity Switch, stock images, graphics and fonts) with a 14-day free trial; all charges are billed in USD and recurring and usage-based charges every 30 days. In the dashboard the pop-up Welcome to Gelato+! said Product discounts Not applied on trial (up to 33% off products; skip the trial to start getting discounts on your next order), Personalization Studio, AI Tools & Premium design assets, Unlimited stores & users, Cancel any time and that a reminder comes 5 days before the trial ends, with the buttons Start 14-day free trial and Skip trial and activate discounts now. Neither was clicked, because it was not known whether a card would be asked; no stored card was seen. No trial was started, nothing was approved and no Shopify approval screen was seen. Differences: the dossier says 2 stores and 2 users, the pop-up says Unlimited stores & users; the dossier says 32 countries and 250+ facilities, the listing says 140+ local production hubs in 32 countries; the dossier gives $19.99 a month billed yearly, the listing shows $239.88 a year (which is $19.99 a month) and save 33% next to $29.99 a month; the listing shows 4.8 stars and 1,044 reviews against 1,007 in the dossier. The price fields are not changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, the trial was not started and no card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: not tested, no plan was taken; only the text Cancel any time on the trial pop-up was seen. Not tested: a real delivery or sample, publishing to a shop, Magic Mockups (Gelato+), discounts after activation, the cancel route, the plans inside the Gelato app of the Shopify store and local production beyond the list of countries. Clean up: the draft product was deleted; the empty Manual store Test Store stays in the Gelato our account and the account stays; no trial and no card. In the first attempt the app was uninstalled from the development store and nothing was created. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session searched Flippa without an account. The filter $10K - $100K with Monthly Profit: $1+ gave 1,235 results for websites, FBA, SaaS and ecommerce and 193 for apps and SaaS only. Cards and listing pages show the asking price, profit and multiples without a login, while detailed traffic, financials and seller notes ask for a free account and confidential listings ask for an NDA. The seller prices are the same as in the dossier: Entry $29, Boosted $49 and Premium $199 on a sub-$10K asset, a 10% success fee, and the broker route at $399 for $100K - $249.9K and $899 for $500K - $999.9K. The 60-day term of Entry could not be read in full because a cookie banner covered it. Nothing was clicked on a Sell button and nothing was bought.
findings: Text we checked: "Entry $29". What we saw: The pricing page shows Entry at $29 for a sub-$10K asset with a 10% success fee. The term line was partly covered by the cookie banner and only the end of the line, 0-day term, could be read, so the 60 days of the dossier were not confirmed.
Text we checked: "Boosted $49". What we saw: The pricing page shows Boosted at $49, a Flat Fee three-month term, marked Most Picked, as in the dossier.
Text we checked: "Premium $199". What we saw: The pricing page shows Premium at $199 per 6 months with No monthly billing and NDA protection for sellers, as in the dossier.
Text we checked: "10% success fee". What we saw: The badge 10% success fee shows on the sub-$10K and the $100K - $249.9K bands, as in the dossier.

Text we checked: "Sell with a dedicated Flippa M&A Broker". What we saw: For $100K - $249.9K the page offers only the broker route at $399, with a 6-month brokerage term, a single upfront payment and a success fee paid only when the business sells, as in the dossier.

Back in Stock Alert on a development store: the install, the onboarding, the embed in an unsaved theme preview and one signup with a made up address. A Notify me button replaced Buy it now on the sold out product about 3 minutes after the start and opened a form for e-mail and SMS; the popup closed after the signup without a visible confirmation, the signup was not looked up in the dashboard and no alert was seen. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Approve on Shopify was clicked, but no Shopify approval screen appeared and the page stayed on the plan page. sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 22 November 2026 with Empire, Pixel Union's Shopify theme, added to our Shopify development store through Try theme. We ran Empire on our own catalogue in the theme editor, tried live search and the collection filters, and checked the counts against our admin. We bought nothing and published nothing.
findings: Trial: Try theme added Empire to our store in about 20 seconds as a Trial theme. The theme library showed Buy and Edit theme, but no Publish.
Add-on: while Empire was being added, a pop-up advertised Theme Updater & Backups, an app add-on from the same developer.
Live search: in the editor Empire ran on our own catalogue at once. Typing snowboard listed our own snowboards with price and In stock, such as The Complete Snowboard at $699.95.

Filters: the collection page counted In stock (16) and Out of stock (2), and the Out of stock filter returned exactly 2 products. That matched our admin: 18 products in the online store, 2 of them out of stock.
Header: the search bar comes with an All categories picker, refined search by product type, live search and a sticky header.
Publishing: the theme menu says Buy theme to publish (Empire version 14.0.0). You can set the theme up for free, but going live costs $360 once.

speed on a live store, because a trial theme cannot be published without buying it

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the trial, without a card, without setting up a phone number or connecting email, and without sending anything: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We imported a CSV with four rows (one made-up company with two contacts and two companies with one), compared the result with the file, and exported the leads as CSV and JSON.
findings: The trial does not start without consent to sales calls and texts. The last sign-up screen asks for a phone number with a box 'By providing your phone number, you agree to receive calls and texts from Close, including automated messages and calls using AI-powered agents'; without ticking it, sign-up stops at 'You must agree to receive communications'. No card was asked, and the app then showed 'Subscribe · 14d left' on day one.

With the default import options, our four rows became 4 leads instead of 3: the company with two contacts appeared twice, once per contact, even though 'Check if Lead already exists' (on lead name) was on. Merging rows per company needs 'Group related rows', which is off by default and which we left off. Statuses and our TestID field arrived correctly per lead.

Five of six columns were matched automatically. For our TestID column we added a custom field, and in that window 'Enable enrichment' is on by default ('the AI will attempt to fill the field'); we switched it off before saving.

Export offers leads, contacts or opportunities, CSV or JSON, and current-view, common or all fields, but 'A link to the generated file will be emailed to you.' Both exports arrived by email within about 10 seconds, and the download link requires logging in. The CSV had 4 rows and 274 columns with primary-contact columns per lead; the JSON had a contacts list per lead. Each lead held one contact in our import, so we could not check whether extra contacts would be lost in the CSV.
The export split the contact name 'AIBM-001 Contact A' into first name 'AIBM-001' and last name 'A', dropping 'Contact'; the full name was still in primary_contact_name.
Import takes CSV only (up to 15 MB), next to copy-paste, import from another CRM or from email. The trial screen also offered a live demo and a $5 calling credit for setting up a phone number.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 28 October 2026 on the free trial: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We imported two made-up contacts, generated one email with AI, exported the contacts, imported them again with one change and opened the Starter checkout without paying. On 19 November 2026 we rechecked tag import with a tag column in the CSV.
findings: The trial banner said 'Your trial expires in 14 days', while the welcome message in the same account said 'For the first 30 days, you'll have access to features from all our plans'. No card was asked.

The contact counter started at 1 of 500: the sign-up address itself is added as a contact. Importing a CSV requires ticking 'I have permission to add these people to my list'; without it the import stops.

Tags can be set per contact from the CSV. On 19 November 2026 we imported three made-up contacts with a column headed tag:hands_on_test and the values 1, 0 and 1; GetResponse mapped it as an import tag, and the two contacts with 1 got the tag hands_on_test while the one with 0 got none. On the free account the Tags tab and the bulk Tag action in the Actions menu are locked, so tags are easiest to set through the import. Tag names allow only letters, numbers and underscores. A custom field could be created during the import. In our first test Import statistics said 'Added to list 0' while both contacts were in the list; this time it said Added to list 3.

The AI email generator allows three runs in the trial ('Runs left: 3', then 2). With a topic but no facts, it invented pros and cons for the tools, such as 'Affordable pricing with a solid free tier'.

Export leaves tags and custom fields off unless you tick them. With both on, the CSV kept both contacts, their GetResponse IDs, the shared tag and our custom field, but showed no consent columns although we selected them.
Importing the file again with one changed name updated that contact by email address; the other stayed the same and no duplicate appeared. The import statistics still said 'Updated 0'.

In-app prices are net. Starter for 1,000 contacts billed yearly came to €192, minus €34.56 prepaid discount, plus €33.06 tax (21%): €190.50 in total. Team roles require an upgrade; generating an API key is offered in the trial.

We tried to import two made-up subscribers from a CSV and opened the Lite trial checkout without paying. AWeber refused both test addresses, so we stopped there.
findings: AWeber rejected both of our made-up addresses (on the reserved test domain example.com) as 'Blocked or invalid email format', so 0 of 2 were added. Following our test plan, we did not swap in real addresses; export and re-import were therefore not tested.

Custom fields are plain text only, up to 25. The import also offers 'Add new and update existing' and 'Only update existing', with 'Only add new subscribers' preselected.
Our own address was put on our list as a subscriber automatically at signup, and every list needs a postal address, which is printed under your emails.

On Free, 'Invite a user' is disabled ('Upgrade your account to invite more users'). The Lite '14-day trial' goes to a Stripe checkout that asks for a card first: € 13,98 a month from 12 November, nothing due today.
Prices in the app: Lite $15 and Plus $30 a month billed monthly, or $13 and $20 a month billed yearly, which is the preselected option.

sessions.what: A new free Basic account. We made one 29-second video from a blank template with a stock avatar and our own 99-word script, read the credit meter on the Billing page before and after, then changed one word and generated it again. The same day we compared the app's upgrade window with the public pricing page.
findings: Onboarding knew who we were before we told it. We skipped the company-website question, yet the prompt box was pre-filled with a brief about our own site, with suggestions such as 'Introduce the Tool Finder', and four draft videos about us appeared in the library without being asked for. They used no credits.

The meter charges by the second. Our 29-second video took the Billing page from 0 to 59 of 1,200 credits, about 2 credits a second, and the app's banner went from '600 seconds' to '571 seconds of video creation time left'. In this account the free month is 10 minutes of finished video. The public pricing page the same day prices video at 100 credits a minute, which would make 59 credits about 35 seconds.

A small edit did not cost the whole video again. After changing one word and generating again, the meter moved from 59 to 63 credits. The second time, though, the button read 'Generate in 15 minutes' instead of 'Generate' and the job went into a queue. Each version took about eight to nine minutes from the click to a finished video.
An upgrade window ('You only have 600 seconds of video creation time left') opened the moment we clicked Generate, and again on every reload of the video page.

On Basic the video carries the Synthesia logo. 'Remove watermark' is marked as paid in the Generate window, and the Billing page lists 'Download your videos' as a Starter feature; we did not try to download.

The app and the public pricing page described different plans on the same day. The app's upgrade window offered Starter at €19 a month or €12 billed yearly with 15,500 credits a year, and Creator at €79 or €49 with 72,500 credits a year. The public pricing page, read without signing in and served in dollars, lists Starter at $29 or $18 with 1,250 credits a month and a Pro plan at $89 or $64 with 6,000 credits a month where Creator used to be; its own comparison table still says 'Free, Starter, and Creator'.
The AI Assistant page that should have built a video from our prompt stayed on a loading screen for over 90 seconds in our session, so we built the video from a blank template instead.

sessions.what: A free account, used on QuillBot's AI Detector, AI Humanizer and Paraphraser. We ran the detector over the texts of known authorship we used for our Pangram test the same day: three passages from public-domain books, a paragraph one of us typed for the test, three paragraphs a language model wrote for our own reviews, and one Claude wrote on the spot. We added a control paragraph written in stock chatbot phrasing, sent it through the Humanizer, and checked the rewrite in QuillBot's detector and in Pangram.
findings: The detector scored all eight texts 0% AI, the four machine-written ones included. Our three review paragraphs and the paragraph Claude wrote on the spot each came back '100% Human-written'. Pangram, given the same eight texts the same day, labelled every one correctly.

It does catch AI text that sounds like AI. The control paragraph, which opens “In today's fast-paced digital landscape”, scored 100% AI, with the stock phrases underlined and the opening sentence listed as 'High'. In our test it picked up the style, not the authorship: plainly written machine text passed as human.

The Humanizer and the detector disagree. The Humanizer rewrote the control paragraph and reported '0 AI signals' on its own output. QuillBot's detector scored that same output 100% AI. Pangram scored it 100% AI too and added that it 'appears to have been paraphrased or rewritten'. The rewrite mostly swapped words: 'seamless' became 'smooth', 'In conclusion' became 'Simply put'.
Every result came with the prompt 'Want your text to sound more authentic? Refine with Paraphraser', including on texts the detector had just rated 100% human.

Signed out, the detector ran four checks (689 words) and then asked us to sign up. It will not run below 40 words, and under 80 it shows 'For more accurate results, add at least 80 words'; it still scored our 71-word paragraph.

The free Paraphraser's 125-word cap is real, and stricter than it sounds. Given 219 words, it reported '219/125 words. Limit exceeded' and showed only the first sentence of the rewrite, with the rest blurred behind an upgrade button, not the first 125 words.
The detector page showed model version v7.1.0.
not_tested: Premium, the plagiarism and grammar checkers, the Humanizer's daily use limit, languages other than English and texts longer than 219 words

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Reclaim (now Dropbox Reclaim) in the existing Lite our account after a calendar was linked with only the calendar scopes: a habit appeared in the calendar within seconds and moved by itself within about 3 seconds when a busy appointment came in, and back when it was removed, but it is set to Free by default so others can book over it. sessions.what: On 30 September 2026 we opened a new ActiveCampaign account on the 14-day free trial, which carries the Pro plan's features, and gave Active Intelligence 3.0: Wavelength ten tasks: a brand kit from our website, a campaign from one of our test pages (twice), a Dutch translation, an image, a welcome automation, a daily scheduled task, industry benchmarks and an automation health check. findings: On the empty account it said plainly that there were no campaigns in the past 12 months and no sends to compare with benchmarks, instead of inventing a best performer or figures.

Given one of our test pages, it wrote a complete campaign in about three minutes. All ten figures in it came from the page and none was added. The same prompt in a new conversation produced a different layout with one sentence the page does not support.

The Brand Kit it built from our homepage matched our voice, mission and colours, but it saved a blue 'N' logo that is not ours, which then appeared in every email, and it picked products we review as competitors.
The Dutch translation was fluent and wrote 250,000 as 250.000, but it replaced the English campaign and left a typo in the preheader and one mistranslated term.

It built a clean welcome automation (three emails, two three-day waits) in about a minute. Its health check then flagged the inactive status but missed that every email still needed a postal address and that nothing fed the new list.

The chat said it could not generate images, and the image generator in the Content Manager returned nothing in five attempts on 30 September 2026, nor in three more on 3 and 5 October. The AI Actions Library is locked in the trial until you buy Activities.

The daily scheduled task sent its first report on 1 October 2026. sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on the 7-day trial, with no card asked: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We asked Frase for one article on 'how to organize a reusable packing checklist' for individual travellers, with three sections, no product tips, no prices and no invented statistics; we checked its key facts, rejected one claim, let it write, and looked at the score and the export options.
findings: A site is required. Without one Frase said 'No sites configured. Add a site first to create content bound to it.' Adding our domain asked for no verification, and the website analysis could be skipped.

The brief overrode our instructions. Frase replaced our audience with 'Shopify Merchants, GTM Leaders, SaaS Operations Managers, Business Travelers', taken from the linked site, planned five sections instead of three, and added a step 'Select an Editable Packing Checklist Tool' with '3 tool recommendations'.

Its own source check worked: it marked a PubMed claim about working memory load as 'not on the page'. The outline still listed that claim as 'EVIDENCE TO INCLUDE - STAT, Source: National Institutes of Health'. We rejected it, and Frase then said it 'will not be claimed'.
The rejected claim appeared in the article anyway, now credited to the National Institutes of Health. Frase wrote the 935-word article in about a minute and a half.

The article also named five products (Todoist, Asana, Notion, Airtable, PackPoint) despite our 'no product recommendations', and used a business setting (trade show, booth, business cards) for an audience of individual travellers. It contained no percentages or prices.
One article took the trial counter from 5 to 4 articles. The editor scored the draft 64, with 4 of 5 sections, 80% coverage, 0 links and 0 images.

Export in the trial covers HTML, PDF, Markdown and plain text downloads, Notion and Google Docs, plus 'Repurpose Content' for LinkedIn and Instagram carousels, an X thread and a newsletter. We did not download anything.

sessions.what: The Freddy AI Agent in a Freshchat trial account, built in AI Agent Studio. We wrote a short help page for a made-up headset shop (shipping, returns, warranty, two products, opening hours: about 250 words) and gave the agent its URL as the only knowledge source; learning finished in about two minutes. We then ran 13 customer questions through the studio's Test screen: 10 whose answer is on the page, one that needs a small inference (shipping to Japan when the page lists only three countries) and two whose answer is not on the page at all (PayPal, and battery life with noise cancelling on). We scored every reply against the page.
findings: 11 of the 13 replies were correct, and every factual reply linked the help page as its source. That includes the trickier ones: an order at 4pm on a Tuesday ships on Wednesday because of the 15:00 cut-off, a cable broken by pulling is excluded from the warranty, and 'Do you ship to Japan?' got a clear no with the three countries we do ship to.

It did not invent anything where the page was silent. Asked about PayPal, it said the help centre has no information on payment methods. Asked for battery life with noise cancelling on, it gave the documented 40 hours, said that figure is with noise cancelling off, and declined to give a number for the other case.

The one wrong reply was 'Can I call you?'. The page says there is no phone support; the agent answered 'Sure! Assigning your chat to our support agent.' It treated the question as a request for a human and started a handover, and the 'Sure!' reads as a yes. The Test dashboard still counted this reply as Answered.
One reply added something the page does not contain: after correctly refusing the warranty claim, it offered to explain 'replacing the cable at your own cost', which our page never mentions.

The dashboard's totals (12 answered, 1 unanswered) are a useful first filter, but you have to read the replies: the handover counted as an answer, and the correct 'I don't know' about PayPal counted as unanswered.
not_tested: real chats through the website widget, other languages, larger or contradictory knowledge bases, and what the replies cost, because the Test screen is not live AI Agent sessions

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 29 October 2026 on the free trial: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We added two made-up employees by hand, logged two test shifts, exported the hours and looked at the plans without paying. On 19 November 2026 we checked the findings again in the same account.
findings: The trial runs on Pro, billed annually ('Free trial · 14 days left', next billing date 12 November). That is not the cheapest plan: Starter is $4.99 per employee a month plus a $19 base fee, billed yearly.
'Send a welcome email to the employee' is ticked by default, in the setup wizard and on the new-employee form. We untick it; the list then shows the invite as 'Not sent'.
Employees took our made-up names with accents, an employee ID, a hire date and a multi-line note. There are no custom fields for codes or amounts.
Each punch shows the IP address of whoever entered it, here the manager.

The standard export ('Export to Excel' on the payroll export) is actually a CSV, with employee ID, names and hours: 1.500 and 2.000, which match our test shifts. It has no notes, emails or start and end times. The employee profile export is part of a paid add-on ($2 per user a month).
The employee import takes eight fixed columns (username, names, email and password required). It has no notes field and no update option, so you cannot change records by importing again.

Correction 12 November 2026: an earlier version of this review said API access is only in the Advanced plan. Buddy Punch told us, and its pricing page (read 12 November 2026) confirms, that API and MCP access are included from the Pro plan, which our trial runs on; Advanced adds higher API and MCP limits. The Change Plan screen we saw on 29 October lists API access in its Advanced summary, which we read as a gate and should not have.

Retest 19 November 2026, after Buddy Punch extended our trial to 26 November: the plans, prices and add-ons, our hours of 1.500 and 2.000, the 'Not sent' invites, the eight import columns and the export route were unchanged. The onboarding and offboarding tasks add-on can now be added for $4 per employee; only new-hire paperwork and document storage are still marked coming soon.

Retest 19 November 2026: the Import Employees page lets an administrator upload up to 100 employees at once from a spreadsheet, with a CSV template of the same eight columns, and offers an onboarding call with a Buddy Punch expert for 100 or more. An admin can run a bulk import without waiting for support.

Retest 19 November 2026: the Change Plan screen in the app still says Advanced 'Includes all Pro features plus real-time GPS, SSO, API access, and more', while the pricing page puts API and MCP access in Pro and gives Advanced higher API and MCP limits. Buddy Punch's own pages disagree on this point; the pricing page is the one Buddy Punch confirmed to us.

sessions.what: On 26 September 2026 we built the same class-booking web app in Lovable, Replit and Emergent from one identical prompt, each on its free plan, and checked every result against 18 tests we wrote down before the first build. We changed no code: the builder only got our prompt and, where a test failed, a repair prompt in fixed words. Replit ran on a new Starter account, separate from the paid account we uses for our own project.
findings: The Agent built a separate API and web app on PostgreSQL in 8 minutes of work by its own count, ran its own functional test and reported everything as passing. It did not publish by itself: publishing is a manual click, and on Starter the deployment is labelled temporary and will expire.

Its own test booked one person at a time. When we sent ten bookings for an empty eight-spot class at the same moment, all ten were accepted, after which the class list returned an error and the public page showed 'No classes on the calendar yet.' until two bookings were cancelled.

Given that exact description, the Agent added a database lock per class in two minutes; the same ten simultaneous bookings then gave exactly eight. The same repair stopped it accepting a name made only of spaces.

On Starter the usage page is closed ('You must have an active subscription to view your own usage'), so you cannot see what a request cost, and the daily allowance was gone after the build and one repair.
The code export, run from the project zip, built and ran outside Replit on our own database, but the export and its Git history carried the generated admin password in plain text.
sessions.not_tested: One run on one day, on the free plan's agent mode; Core may behave differently. Not a security audit or a load test.

findings: Sending to signed took 36 seconds on Pro (sent 21:13:28 UTC, signed 21:14:04 UTC, completed 21:14:05 UTC, 37 seconds after sending), and about 1.5 minutes from upload. The certificate is issued to Innovoris Labs Srl by DigitalSign CA G1 and chains to DigitalSign Global Root RSA CA. sessions.what: We did not just read the docs: we ran 40 pricing queries across 20 tools and two engines through the async batch endpoint for a research report of our own, then spent a further handful of credits measuring what individual requests actually cost. Cloro is an affiliate partner of ours, which is why we checked their credit table against the meter instead of quoting it.
findings: A plain async ChatGPT task billed 5 credits, not the 7 the pricing table lists for a full ChatGPT response: that is the web-search rate. It held over 20 requests in a batch and again on a single measured call. Budget from 5 and the free tier is 100 ChatGPT answers, not 71.

The credit meter lags. Straight after a completed ChatGPT task the balance was unchanged; the charge landed about 90 seconds later. If you gate your own spending on a balance read immediately after a call, you will overshoot.

The harvest does not echo your request back: task.payload comes back null. Submit a batch of 40 and nothing in the response tells you which answer belongs to which query: you have to keep your own map of task id to question. This cost us a wrong result on the first pass.

The response shape differs per engine, so there is no single schema to code against. ChatGPT returned text, sources, citationPills and model; Perplexity returned no model but added related_queries, search_model_queries and shopping_cards.
Async tasks came back in roughly 30 to 40 seconds each, and on the free tier's single concurrent job a 40-task batch is a queue, not a burst: budget wall-clock time as well as credits.
Source counts swing wildly and that is the engine, not the API: one Perplexity call returned 10 sources, while in our 20-tool batch 14 of 20 Perplexity answers returned no sources at all.

sessions.what: The free plan on a new account. We uploaded one recording whose exact script we hold: the 2-minute-49 audio of our own Contabo video review, two synthetic voices and 377 words with prices, dates and product names. We compared the transcript word for word with the script, checked how it split the speakers, and read the AI summary and action items against what was said. In setup we chose the narrowest meeting settings: join only meetings we invite it to, recaps to the account owner only.
findings: The transcript was close: after evening out punctuation and number formats, 5.3% of the 377 words differed from the script. Product names such as Contabo, DigitalOcean, Cloud VPS 12, cPanel and Plesk came through.

The errors sat where a buyer would care. '6.70 euros a month' came out as '6.€70amonth', 'the usual fine print' as 'the US fine print', and 'excluding VAT' dropped out of the sentence with the entry price, though a later sentence kept 'Prices on the page exclude vat'.
Speaker detection found six speakers in a recording with two voices, and split single sentences across them.

The AI summary had the facts right: the 24-month prepaid term, about 25% more month to month, backups at 6.70 euros and the DigitalOcean comparison. Its one action item was assigned to 'Daniel Cho', a name that is not spoken anywhere in the recording.

The free plan's 'unlimited transcription' depends on your settings. In setup the switch for unlimited free transcripts sits beside the line 'Users on Join-All and Share-All settings get unlimited meeting transcripts': Fireflies joining every meeting with a link and sending recaps to everyone on the invite. Our narrower choice switched it off, and the account then showed '3 Free meetings'.

sessions.what: We built an AI-generated newsletter draft in iContact's 30-day trial on 13 November 2026 and read the plan and price screens. The account is ours, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We sent nothing and added no contact. We did not open the automation tools.
findings: The Create Message screen lists six template groups, plain text, an HTML editor, an AI option and a blank start. We took the AI option with a brief for a fictional animal shelter: thank volunteers, announce a winter food drive on 6 December, ask readers to donate. Length: Short.

After choosing a template and answering 'Preserve Images?' with Replace Images, a preview appeared in about 20 seconds. The text matched the brief: it thanks the volunteers and announces the food drive on 6 December.
The images the AI chose did not fit. A tortoise on its back sat at the top, and a photo of avocados and limes stood next to the food drive text.

Accepting the draft opened a drag-and-drop editor with eleven block types, from text and image to a calendar button and saved blocks. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 20:03 on the clock of the session and the Shopify screen Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; after Install the app was open at about 20:05. No Shopify screen to approve a subscription appeared at the install and no card was asked. In the Shopify admin the app is called Auware AI Landing Page Builder. The admin was in English. Onboarding: the app opened outside the Shopify frame on app.auware.com/onboarding with Welcome to Auware and the store name, with Store connected, Detecting brand style and Importing products already ticked, and a checklist: Confirm your account (Continue as this account), Secure your account (Set Up 2FA or Passkey, Skip), Invite your team, Connect a review platform and Connect integrations, 0 of 5 steps done. Only the confirmation was clicked and the rest was skipped. No password and no sign-up form were shown at this point. Core action, landing pages for audiences without code: the product was The Complete Snowboard ($699.95). Steps: Choose Product; Apply a Discount (skipped, You can skip this step and continue without a discount); Marketing Strategy (Strict & Compliant, FTC-friendly copy that avoids hype, unsubstantiated claims, and regulatory risk); Customer Reviews (skipped, Connect a review platform to import reviews, with also a button Generate Reviews for test reviews); Format (Landing Page was preselected, Listicle and Testimonial Showcase said Requires Reviews). Building Your Landing Page said Estimated time: about 1m 7s, and the baseline page appeared in the editor (Not saved yet) with the headline A Snowboard Designed for Riding Down Snow-. That was about 6 clicks and about 1.5 minutes of waiting. The banner box said Click to add banner image and stayed empty: no image was generated. Suggest Audiences said Discovering Your Audiences and that this usually takes under a minute. It gave 6 suggestions (Seasonal Upgrade Seekers, First-Time Buyers, Mountain Trip Planners, Gift-Giving Parents, Gear Collectors and Responsible Recreational Athletes). Two were approved (2 approved): Seasonal Upgrade Seekers and First-Time Buyers. Building the Landing Page for Seasonal Upgrade Seekers said Estimated time: about 62s, and then the panel said 2 of 2 ready; the headline of the First-Time Buyers page was Your First Snowboard: Honest Information to Help You Decide. Time to the first result: a baseline page after about 6 clicks and about 1.5 minutes; two audience pages after about 15 clicks and about 7 to 10 minutes in all, mostly waiting for the AI to generate. Review & Publish: the screen Review & Publish Your Landing Pages with the button Publish to Shopify (NOT used), the campaign name Complete Snowboard - Slope Ready Landing Page, page URL slugs of /pages/aw- plus six characters for each of the three pages, the call to action options Add to Cart, Direct to Checkout, Go to URL, Run Custom Script (labelled 2FA Required) and Buy with Prime, and the text that you can export the HTML package. The HTML export was not tried. Nothing was published, so there was no change to the theme or the store, no traffic was sent and no conversion was measured. Plans and checkout: not reached. Up to and including the three generated pages no price, no trial banner and no Shopify screen to approve a subscription appeared. No password was entered: a separate account or password would be needed. So no price, trial or approval screen was seen, and the dossier ($199 per maand per store, 30 dagen trial) is neither confirmed nor refuted. Cancelling: the route inside Auware was not tested because there was no access. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

findings: The trial ran for 15 days ('ends on 13.11.2026'), on the Starter plan. The second 15 days are three rewards of 5 days each, for watching a video, following on LinkedIn and adding a second user who performs 5 actions. They are not automatic.
Before an import MRPeasy recommends downloading a backup, and does it in one click (an .mrp file).

The item import recognised part number, description and selling price by itself. It has no field for notes, tags, dates or custom fields; custom fields are a Professional-plan feature, which the Starter trial does not include.
Two items were imported with zero stock. The CSV export (semicolons) kept part numbers, names with accents and selling prices; the part number is the only key, with no internal ID.
The payment page asks for a card or PayPal but shows no amount, plan or tax. The account page lists 'Next invoice € 39.00' for Starter, monthly, one user.
Users get a permission grid per module (read, create, update, delete), all off by default, rather than named roles. We found no API setting among the integrations in the time we had.

sessions.what: We tested team sharing in Passpack on a Business trial on 13 November 2026 with a made-up record that holds no password. The account is ours, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We typed, generated and stored no password and no real login: the record has an empty password field, an invented username and an example web address. We invited no second user, so a departing colleague was not simulated.
findings: The record form has fields for name, username, email, password (with a generator and a strength meter), TOTP, website address and tags. We saved the record with the password left empty. It defaults to private.
We created a team called 'Marketing (test)' with default member rights of view or edit, and chose the Multi-administrator mode over Private.

Sharing took about 6 clicks and the route was hard to find. On the record, the sharing mode must change first (keep private, transfer ownership, or share with multi-administrator teams). Only then does the team list appear. Adding the private record from the team's own records tab did not work.
Switching the team on opened a confirmation saying the record can then be managed by all administrators of the organisation. We confirmed and it saved.

The Team Membership report searches by email and shows team name, team owner and user permission. A search on our own account returned no results, so the owner does not count as a member there. The Log Access report lists sign-in activity per login and offers a CSV download. We did not open the file.

The account showed a Business plan with status Trial and no card was requested. The trial end date was not visible because the renewal date field was empty, so we could not confirm the '28 days' on the pricing page.

The Subscription page says the contract renews automatically with the number of licences used, currently 1. We did not open the Stripe billing portal and saw no price, tax or total. The only mobile banner promoted the iPhone app. We saw no Android app offered inside the app, and did not check whether one exists elsewhere.

sessions.what: We opened a new Databox account through the 'Get started' button under the Free plan on databox.com/pricing, connected Google Analytics 4 and Google Search Console for our own site, asked Genie two questions about that data, let Genie try to build a dashboard, and read the credit meter under Settings → Billing after every step. One account, one evening, our own traffic data, not a month of team use.
findings: The Free button does not give you Free. The account opened as a 14-day trial of Team Core at $249 a month, billed monthly. Free was listed in the app as a 'Downgrade'. Databox's own FAQ says that if no payment details are added by the end of the trial, syncing stops and reports pause, so anyone who wanted Free has to downgrade by hand before day 14.

The downgrade was blocked until we deleted Databox's own sample data. The message: 'You have 1 connected Spreadsheets, but the Free plan is limited to 0.' That one spreadsheet was the Sample dataset Databox adds at sign-up. Free allows no spreadsheets at all: Excel and Google Sheets both open an 'Upgrade to Analyst' wall at $89 a month, something the pricing page does not say.

Your one free dashboard is already taken. Databox's own Sample Dashboard stays after the downgrade and fills the plan's single dashboard slot. 'Create New Databoard' opened the $89 upgrade wall, and so did the button that would hang the sample dashboard on your own data.

What a Genie question costs: 3.7 credits for a simple one ('which pages got the most views in August'), 3.8 for a heavier week-by-week comparison. On Free's 50 a month that is about thirteen questions. The onboarding had already spent 1.9 credits by sending our four setup answers to Genie as a first question we never asked, and the app showed 'Buy more to keep Genie running' at 48 left.

Genie spends credits on things the plan will not allow. It offered to build a dashboard, tried three times, reported that Databox 'rejected the request as invalid' without naming the one-dashboard limit, and charged 5.2 credits for nothing. After one hour we had used 14.6 of the month's 50 credits.

Genie's diagnoses need checking. It called a half-finished Search Console connection 'broken' because 'the login expires' (the data manager said 'Unfinished connection'), and it flagged one of our real review URLs as a typo. The traffic figures themselves came back fast and were usefully broken down, including pages counted twice because of query strings.

What held up: connecting a data source cost no credits, the unfinished connection still counted against the three-source limit, and the plan prices inside the app matched the public pricing page ($89 / $249 / $399 monthly; $71 / $199 / $319 billed annually).
sessions.not_tested: We did not add a fourth data source past the limit, did not build our own dashboard after deleting the sample one, and could not check how fresh each source's data is: the app shows sync frequency but no last-synced time.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 5 November 2026 on the free Basic plan: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We drafted a small quiz survey, looked for an export, and opened the checkout for Standard Monthly without paying. We collected no responses and sent nothing.
findings: Sign-up asked four profile questions and then dropped us on the home screen. No card, no sales call and no linked account was required.

The account page shows 'Basic (Free) Account', '10 responses per survey' and 'Survey data storage: United States'. 'Access to Benchmarks' was already switched on, so your survey results feed SurveyMonkey's benchmarks unless you turn it off.

Quiz scoring worked on Basic: we marked one answer as worth one point. A 'Multiple textboxes' question raised the toast '1 paid feature added! Upgrade your plan or remove paid features to send this survey.' Basic lets you preview paid question types, but not send a survey that uses one.
In Analyze results, 'New export' and 'Previous exports' are locked, with the panel 'Good data deserves a way out' and an Upgrade button. On Basic we found no way to export results.

The pricing page opens on Team plans: Team Advantage at €30 per user per month, from 3 users, billed annually. Individual plans sit behind a second tab: Standard Monthly €39 a month, Advantage Annual €36 a month (€432 billed annually), Premier Annual €99 a month (€1,188 billed annually).

Checkout for Standard Monthly, with the Netherlands pre-filled, showed 'Total (VAT included) €39'. The sentence under it says the plan renews at €39 monthly 'plus applicable taxes'. The two statements do not agree, so confirm the tax basis before you buy. We stopped before any payment.
not_tested: Collecting responses and exporting them: Basic gave us no way to submit test responses, so both fictional kit records stayed untested
Round trip with native record IDs; export bytes were never downloaded
Support, team roles, API access and invitations: the Team page asked for a paid plan and we did not open the developer pages
Downgrade and cancellation: we were already on the free plan
How long a full sign-up takes from the first click; we created the account before we started counting

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested VWO, which is now sold under the name Wingify, on a 30-day free trial of an account we created. The trial started without a card, and a draft A/B test with two variations on a neutral test page stood after about 3 minutes. The visual editor opened in fallback mode and could not edit a variation until the SmartCode sits on the site, so a real test needs that code first. Inside the trial the Growth plan has a list price of $1,118 per month billed annually, $13,410 up front, with a self-service checkout, while the public pricing page still shows no amount. The confirm page was left before Checkout Now.
findings: Text we checked: "Free for 30 days. No credit card required". What we saw: Start free trial on Web Experimentation & Rollout gave a trial at once, with the bar 30 days remaining; no card, no phone number and no call were asked. My Subscription showed MTU consumed 0 of 10K, expires on Dec 19, 2026.

Text we checked: "AB Tasty and VWO have united, because half the loop was never enough". What we saw: vwo.com/pricing forwards to wingify.com/pricing, which carries this line; the app is called Wingify throughout, and only the demo still calls itself VWO Playground.

Text we checked: "Page opened in fallback mode". What we saw: Launch Editor opened the test page example.com with this message and advised the Wingify SmartCode or the Wingify Chrome extension. The page loaded, but no element could be selected, so Variation 1 could not be changed.

Text we checked: "Wingify offers custom pricing". What we saw: The FAQ in the app gives this answer, while the plan table in the same app lists Growth at $1,118 per month billed annually at 100K MTU, with an Add button that leads to a checkout without a call. Only Pro and Enterprise say Request pricing.

Text we checked: "no price is published". What we saw: The dossier price line, read on 20 September, says this. The public pricing page still shows no amount, only Schedule a Demo, but inside the free trial Growth is listed at $1,118 per month billed annually ($13,410) with a self-service checkout.

Inside the trial the Growth plan has a list price of $1,118 per month billed annually, $13,410 up front, with a self-service checkout, while the public pricing page still shows no amount. The confirm page was left before Checkout Now. Account and start: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab, on 19 November 2026 from 09:41 to 09:50 CET. The interface was in English. The product is now sold as Wingify: vwo.com/pricing forwards to wingify.com/pricing, which says AB Tasty and VWO have united, and the app is called Wingify, while the demo still calls itself VWO Playground. The dossier name is VWO and the review is on AIBM (b2b/vwo-review). The welcome screen offered two routes, Explore Wingify Playground (a live demo with no setup) and Continue account Setup, plus an optional Talk to an expert. The Playground opened as a separate demo account after about 25 seconds. Back in the real account, Select your products listed Web Experimentation & Rollout, Web Personalization, Feature Management, Journey Analytics, Behavior Analytics and User Feedback, each with Start free trial. Core action, an A/B test on one page: Start free trial on Web Experimentation & Rollout at 09:44 gave a 30-day trial at once, with a bar 30 days remaining, Upgrade; no card, no phone number and no call were asked. Basic Setup asked for a first website; the prefilled domain was replaced by the neutral https://example.com, and Add domain said Domain added successfully. SmartCode generated, with setup guides for HTML, Next.js, WordPress, Shopify, Wix and others. The code was not copied or placed anywhere. Web Experimentation, Create, AB - Single Page: the test Test Project headline test on https://example.com/ with Control and Variation 1 at 50/50 and 100% traffic. Metrics and Targeting exist as later steps and were not filled in; the test was not started. Launch Editor asked to save first and opened the editor in a new tab with the message Page opened in fallback mode, which advises the SmartCode or the Wingify Chrome extension. The page loaded, but elements could not be selected (a double click only marked one word), so a variation could not be edited without the code or the extension. Heatmaps, recordings, forms and surveys were only seen in the Playground demo with sample data, not with our own traffic; a sample test there showed 701 conversions from 4,553 visitors against 541 from 4,476. That is demo data and says nothing about a test on a real site. Time: about 3 minutes from the trial start to a draft test with two variations in the editor (09:44 to 09:47), not counting the 25 seconds the Playground took to load. Trial limits on My Subscription: Web Experimentation & Rollout on Free trial, MTU consumed 0 of 10K, expires on Dec 19, 2026, 30 days left; Wingz on Free trial with 0 of 6.0K credits; Websites 1 out of 1. Data is kept for 13 months according to the app. Plans: In the trial account, Upgrade, Web Experimentation & Rollout, with a slider for Monthly Tracked Users from 25K to 5M+ (default 100K): Trial, Full access to all product features, Free, active with 30 days remaining; Growth, For small businesses, $1,363 struck through, Save 18%, $1,118 per month, billed annually, with Add and Contact Sales; Pro, For mid sized businesses, and Enterprise, For large teams, agencies & enterprises, both Request pricing. Add-ons: Social Proof & Urgency Messaging $599 per month (Pro, Enterprise), Mutually Exclusive Groups $299 per month (Growth, Pro, Enterprise) and Additional MTU Quota $199 one time, ending with the plan. Wingz AI has Core, included with paid plans, and Advanced options. The FAQ in the same app says "Wingify offers custom pricing tailored to your needs" and asks you to reach out for a quote. The public pricing page vwo.com/pricing now forwards to wingify.com/pricing and shows Growth, Pro and Enterprise, each with Schedule a Demo and no amount; its sign-up box says Free for 30 days. No credit card required. Checkout: Add on Growth opened a Checkout Summary with Growth, 100,000 MTU, $1,118 per month, billed annually, Grand Total $13,410. View Summary opened Review & confirm, step 2 of 3, with Total $13,410, a Checkout Now button and the switch Auto-renew on Nov 19, 2027 is enabled until you cancel; the page also says the new plan replaces the current one at once. Checkout Now was not clicked; no card field was seen and nothing was paid. $1,118 times 12 is $13,416, so the monthly figure is rounded. A last Remove click on the cart had no visible effect, so the cart may still hold Growth; nothing was bought. Cancelling: the trial ends by itself on Dec 19, 2026, so there was nothing to cancel. Settings, Subscription & Invoices has My Subscription, Invoice History and Billing Profile; a paid plan renews automatically until you cancel. A delete account button was not looked for. Not tested: editing a variation in the editor, verifying the SmartCode, starting a test, our own heatmaps or recordings, the prices of Pro and Enterprise, the prices at 25K or 50K MTU, Billing Profile and deleting the account. Clean up: the account, the Playground demo account, the domain example.com and the draft test (campaign 1, Draft) stay; the cart may still hold Growth. The own tab and the editor tab were closed. No kit records were entered.

The brand is changing from VWO to Wingify, and the app FAQ says pricing is custom while the plan table in the same app shows a Growth price. Growth is billed for a year up front and renews automatically.
