sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 during the 14-day trial, without a card and without connecting accounting software or a bank: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We uploaded two made-up receipts whose every field we knew, then a byte-identical copy of one and a rotated copy of the other.
findings: Both receipts reached the Costs inbox within about a minute, and all eight fields we checked were right: date, supplier, total and tax on each (EUR 12.10 with EUR 2.10 tax, and EUR 21.80 with EUR 1.80 tax). Dext picked the category itself: 'Office Supplies' for the stationery receipt and 'Travel' for the transport one.
The rotated copy was marked 'Duplicate' in Submission history and kept out of the inbox, which is right, but it still counted: the usage counter went from 0 to 3 of 250 for two receipts.
The byte-identical copy appeared nowhere, not even in Submission history: it was dropped without a message.

The workspace worked straight away without any connection. Onboarding asked three questions (industry, company size and accounting software, with Spreadsheets as an option); the overview showed 'Documents extracted 0 / 250, Resets in 1 days' and trial credits for 10 bank statement, 5 supplier statement and 5 line-item extractions, 5 Vault AI credits and 500 MB of Vault storage.

Upload offers one document per file (PDF, JPG, PNG, ZIP), one per page (PDF) or auto-splitting (PDF, 'Can take up to 1 hour'), with limits of 6 MB per image or PDF, 100 MB per ZIP and 40 MB for an auto-split PDF. Each account also gets its own email address for sending in documents.
not_tested: Correcting a recognition error (there was none to correct)
Net amount and tax rate in the detail view
Real, creased or handwritten receipts, and other currencies
Publishing to accounting software, a bank connection and the mobile app
What happens after the trial, and what the 250 per period means exactly

New accounts come with a sample client and appointment already in place.

The client list export is a report that Healthie builds in the background and files under Documents ('can take up to 30 minutes'); ours was ready in about a minute. It had 39 columns, and accented names came through intact.
Clients we saved without an email got a made-up @gethealthie.com address in the export.
You cannot import clients yourself. Both import routes send your file to Healthie as a request, and its data import is 'included on paid plans'.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Scrolly (app name Scrolly Infinite Scroll) on a Shopify development store: the install, the free Scroll To Top button (settings saved, the app embed switched on in an unsaved preview of the Home page, one click took the page back to the top, about 12 steps and about 2 minutes after the install), the plan screen and the Shopify approval screen for the Monthly Unlimited plan (a 7-day free trial, a payment method was asked, nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Infinite Scroll was not tested. Nothing was paid and no theme change was saved. Install: the App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/custom-scroll-to-top, English, listing text Free plan available, Free trial available, rating 4.9 from 234 reviews with 221 five-star ratings) was opened at 20:28 and the install form was submitted in our own tab. The permission screen asked for View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Online Store, Shopify admin). Install was done at about 20:29 and the app opened on Welcome to Scrolly: Infinite Scroll with Pick your plan to start a 7-day free trial; the app is called Scrolly Infinite Scroll in the admin. No vendor account, call or phone number was asked. Core action, the free Scroll To Top button: the Free Plan was chosen with Choose Plan and no payment screen followed. The dashboard said Free Plan, Infinite Scroll app embed Off with Upgrade required, and Scroll To Top Button status Off. Enable Scroll To Top Button opened Scroll To Top Button Settings (Inactive) with the notice ACTION REQUIRED: Turn on Scrolly's App Embed, ten button presets (one with a padlock), Location Entire store, Position Bottom right and Mobile Behaviour Show for mobile devices. Activate Scroll To Top Button gave Unsaved changes and Save. In the theme editor (own tab) the app embed Scroll To Top Button was switched on in the unsaved preview of the Home page. After scrolling a round arrow button appeared at the bottom right and one click took the page back to the top. The result stood there at about 20:31, about 12 steps and about 2 minutes after the install. The button was seen on the Home page of the preview and not on a collection page, and not on a phone. Infinite scroll was NOT tested: the plan screen lists Infinite Scroll (Auto loads more products in collection pages) only on the Unlimited Plan, and the Unlimited plan needs a payment method. Plans in the app: the plan screen opens on Yearly with the Free Plan and the Unlimited Plan at $2.50/month (billed annually) with Save 50%; Monthly shows $4.99/month (billed monthly); the button is Start free trial and the text says Every store is entitled to 7 free trial days altogether. The Free plan lists adding the Scroll To Top button, customising its style and appearance and showing it on specific pages; the Unlimited plan adds a button image of your own and Infinite Scroll. The App Store listing also says the button Can be hidden in mobile store version on the free plan; the plan card does not list this, but the app has the dropdown Mobile Behaviour (it showed Show for mobile devices; we did not open the dropdown and did not look at a phone). A banner in the app said BLACK FRIDAY SALE: 50% OFF on Scrolly's Yearly Plan. The yearly total in dollars was not shown on the screens we kept. Checkout: Start free trial on the Monthly plan opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: Monthly Plan, $4,99 USD every 30 days, Your next bill: You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $4,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total Due 24 Nov $4,99, a row Add payment method and a greyed out Approve button. The sentence You will not be billed for this test charge was not on the screen and a payment method was needed, so nothing was approved and no payment method was added. Cancel on that screen showed nothing visible; we went back through the address of the app. No paid plan became active. Cancelling: no subscription ran, so there was nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the menu of the app and Uninstall: the dialog Uninstall Scrolly Infinite Scroll? says that you can no longer use the app and that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted; a reason had to be chosen (Testing multiple apps) before the uninstall. Differences from the review: the review says $29.94 a year for the paid plan, while the app showed $2.50/month (billed annually) and no yearly total in dollars on the screens we kept (the yearly approval screen was not opened); the review counts 236 listing reviews with 225 five-star ratings, the listing showed 234 with 221. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: Infinite Scroll and load-more (paid, payment method needed), the own button image, a real phone view and a collection page with pagination. Clean up: the theme change was not saved (the embed was switched on in the preview and the page was left with Leave page without saving). The Scroll To Top settings in the app were saved and go with the uninstall. The app was uninstalled through Settings, Apps (message: You have successfully uninstalled Scrolly Infinite Scroll) and our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Free plan available. Free trial available". What we saw: The listing text says Free plan available and Free trial available. The Free Plan was chosen with Choose Plan and no payment screen followed; the paid plan showed a 7-day free trial on the Shopify approval screen, which was not approved.

Text we checked: "Show the Scroll To Top button in specific pages". What we saw: On the Free Plan the Scroll To Top button was switched on with the app embed in an unsaved preview of the Home page; after scrolling a round arrow appeared at the bottom right and one click took the page back to the top, about 12 steps and about 2 minutes after the install. A collection page, a phone and the page choices were not tried.
not_tested: Original store creation and identity check, which we did ourselves.
Infinite Scroll and load-more, which need the paid plan and a payment method.
A collection page with pagination, a real phone view and the own button image.
Approving any plan, so the admin of the paid plan was not seen.
Export and reimport.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested UpsellPlus on a Shopify development store: the install without a payment or approval screen, one Smart cross-sell play for the cart drawer with 10% off that gave a preview about 4 minutes and about 6 clicks after the install click (The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard $949.95 to $854.95, Gift Card $10.00 to $9.00), the Billing page with nine revenue steps from Basic $49 to Unlimited $999 a month, and the uninstall, which asks for a reason. Nothing was saved or published and no order was placed, so no shopper data was seen. Name: the listing (apps.shopify.com/upsellpluscheckout) is titled UpsellPlus Checkout Upsell, developer UpsellPlus, Built for Shopify, rating 5.0 from 151 reviews, and matches the dossier; the app opens as UpsellPlus. The listing says Free plan available. Free trial available. and shows a plan box with Free (Build for free. Launch with a free trial, Choose from all 12 upsell types, Checkout Upsells (Plus only), Analytics), Basic $49 (up to $500), Pro $119 (up to $2,000) and Advanced $199 (up to $5,000), each with a 14-day free trial. Install: the Install button was clicked at about 23:19. The permission screen asked to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. The Install button normally opens a grant tab; in our own tab the install form was sent into the same tab and submitted with a script. The first attempt ended in the message UpsellPlus was not added to your shop because the permission screen was closed too early; the second attempt worked. After the install the product opened at once with the setup line We analyzed your last 60 days of orders. There was no Shopify approval screen and no payment screen. Core action: See my recommended strategies, Offers, Create offer, filter Cart, Smart cross-sell, Use this play opened the offer editor with Where (Cart Drawer, Cart Page, Product Detail Page) and Incentive (None, 5% off, 10% off, Custom); we chose Cart Drawer and 10% off. The preview showed The Inventory Not Tracked Snowboard at $854.95 instead of $949.95 and Gift Card at $9.00 instead of $10.00, each with an Add to Cart button, under the note that real products from the store are shown and that actual products are selected automatically by AI at runtime. A box Place your app block was marked Incomplete: the cart drawer app block still has to be added in the theme. About 4 minutes passed between the install click (23:19) and the first preview (about 23:23), and it took about 6 clicks after the install. Nothing was saved (Discard), nothing was published, the theme was not changed and no order was placed. Plans and billing: this is a development store. Settings, Billing says Development store. You have full access to every feature, free. Development, partner and Shopify staff stores are never charged. It also says that a store on a paid Shopify plan starts on the free plan like any other shop and that pricing then follows the steps below. The page How pricing works says that the price follows the upsell revenue UpsellPlus generates, with nine steps: Basic up to $500 at $49 a month, Pro up to $2,000 at $119, Advanced up to $5,000 at $199, Scale 1 up to $10,000 at $299, Scale 2 up to $15,000 at $399, Scale 3 up to $20,000 at $499, Scale 4 up to $30,000 at $699, Scale 5 up to $40,000 at $799 and Unlimited at $999 a month. All prices are in USD and appear on the Shopify invoice. No Shopify approval screen was reached, nothing was approved. Differences with the dossier and the listing: the app shows the entry step as Basic Plan where the dossier says Launch; the app shows no Free plan among the nine steps although the listing says Free plan available (on a development store the free plan cannot be tested); the listing shows tiers up to $199 while the app shows six more steps up to $999 that are tied to upsell revenue. No price field is changed here. Cancelling: no paid plan exists on a development store, so no cancel route for a plan was seen. Settings, Apps, the menu behind the three dots for UpsellPlus offered Open app, View details and Uninstall (and a help link). The dialog Uninstall UpsellPlus? says that you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. It requires a Reason for uninstalling. Not tested: checkout, thank-you page, post-purchase and POS upsells (Plus or paid, the listing says checkout upsells are Plus only), the free plan on a real paid store, A/B tests, analytics with real data, the cart drawer app block, a real order and any shopper data, so we could not tell whether shoppers would take an offer. Clean up: our own tab was used; the offer was not saved and the theme was not changed. UpsellPlus was uninstalled on 17 Nov through Settings, Apps with the reason Testing multiple apps and left the Installed list. Other apps were not touched and our own tab was closed. The price fields are not changed here. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: Historical test data: these are measurements from 4 September 2026, at that day's free allowance and meters, not today's Free plan or the standard cost of every Bot. We ran the reproducible test BrowserAct's own partner team proposed, on a free account with the 1,500 sign-up credits the card offered at the time. The prompt, verbatim: open books.toscrape.com, collect the first 20 books in listing order, open each detail page and return full title, displayed price, availability and source URL, leave unavailable fields blank, infer nothing. Before touching BrowserAct we fetched the same 20 pages with plain HTTP and saved the four fields as ground truth, so every value below was checked against the source, not against BrowserAct's own claims. Then we built the Bot from the prompt, ran it twice from the published version, and read the credit meter after each step.
findings: Accuracy: 80 of 80 fields correct, three times over. The build's own verification output, run 1 and run 2 each returned 20 rows with title, price, availability and URL identical to our ground truth, including the parenthetical stock counts ('In stock (22 available)') and the currency symbol, which the Bot kept as displayed rather than converting.

The build costs more than the runs. Building the Bot took 4 minutes 59 seconds and 278 credits; the agent inspected the listing and a detail page, wrote a small package (a SKILL.md, a run.py and two DOM helpers), compiled it, and ran it end to end before declaring it ready. On that day's free tier that was about a fifth of the sign-up credits spent before the first real run. The pricing page now estimates 300 to 500 credits for a simple Agent build, and today's free card lists 2 free Agent Builds alongside its 200 credits.

Runs are cheap but not deterministic in cost. Run 1 used 21 credits in 1 minute 56 seconds; run 2, the same Bot on the same 20 pages, used 27 credits in 3 minutes 12 seconds. Identical output, 29% more credits and 65% more wall time. At Basic's 10,000 credits for $13 a month on yearly billing, a run of this size is roughly three cents, so the variance is small in money and worth knowing about in budgeting.

The meter is honest at the account level and confusing at the task level. Balance went 1,500 to 1,222 after the build, 1,201 after run 1 and 1,174 after run 2, which reconciles exactly with the per-task figures in the history list. But the task detail panel showed 'Credits used: 0' for a run that the history list, seconds later, priced at 21. Trust the list and the balance, not the panel.

The agent made one silent design decision. The prompt said 'the first 20 books', and the Bot was built with no parameters and 'first 20' hard-coded; it says so in its own summary and offers to change it on request. Fine for this test, but a Bot you intend to reuse should be built with the count as an input, and you have to ask for that.

Historical: on 4 September the app and the website showed different prices. On first login the app opened a '7-days free trial' panel listing Basic at $16, Essential at $70 and Advanced at $120 a month, with $20, $100 and $200 struck through, while the public pricing page, read the day before, still charged $20, $100 and $200 monthly. That gap closed by 13 September: the public page now shows the same $16, $70 and $120.
not_tested: books.toscrape.com is a static sandbox with no login, no JavaScript rendering and no anti-bot measures, so none of the managed-browser, proxy or CAPTCHA infrastructure in BrowserAct's pitch was exercised. It proves the no-code loop from plain prompt to reusable Bot; it says nothing about hostile sites, where proxy use starts to matter -- free in the cloud for a limited time, 5,000 credits per gigabyte of dynamic proxy traffic on the Local CLI.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Code Bulk Discounts on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: the plan screens, generating 20 unique codes for a 10 percent discount, the CSV download and the delete dialog. Nothing was paid or deleted. The app opens on Select a discount with the text Search and select an existing discount code, so it does not create a discount rule itself; the list showed only existing discounts. We made a 10 percent order discount in Shopify Discounts first; an Amount off products discount asked for products or collections, so an order discount was used. In the app we searched that discount and chose Generate codes (Automatically generate codes, with the counter 0 of 500 allowance). The form has Count (default 1, set to 20), Charset Alphanumeric, Length 8, empty Prefix and Suffix, Include Job ID (recommended) switched on and a Title, and says Free codes remaining: 500 of 500. After Generate the Previous jobs table showed Requested 20, Imported 0, Failed 0 with Importing 0%, and after about 10 seconds Requested 20, Imported 20, Failed 0 with status Complete. Shopify Discounts then showed 21 codes created by the Shopify web app (the 20 generated plus the main code), each customer entering a unique code, and 0 used. Codes have 8 characters plus the job number as a suffix. The Actions menu offers Download CSV, Connect Klaviyo to upload (greyed out), Email QR embed and Delete Set. Download CSV gave a file with the heading Coupon and 20 codes, all unique; that file is not part of the evidence. Delete Set opened the dialog Delete this set? with Cancel and Delete; Cancel was pressed and nothing was deleted. Timing, approximate tester observations: installation at about 14:22 and the first generated codes at about 14:27, mostly spent choosing the plan and making the parent discount by hand; the code generation itself took 3 steps and about 10 seconds of processing. Not tested: more than 20 codes, Pro, Upload codes, the QR code, Klaviyo, using a code in a real checkout, the app Settings screen and uninstalling. No kit records were entered.
findings: Vendor claim "Generate 500 lifetime codes". What we saw: The Free plan card says so and the generator form said Free codes remaining: 500 of 500 before the run of 20 codes. The counter after the run was not read, so the use of the 500 was not seen going down. The Free plan covers 500 codes in total rather than 500 a month, so a larger campaign needs the Pro plan.

Vendor claim "This plan is free. You will not be billed". What we saw: Shopify showed this on the Approve charge screen for the Free plan and the plan was approved at 0 dollars; nothing was paid. Trying the Free plan costs nothing.

Vendor claim "Search and select an existing discount code". What we saw: The app starts by asking for an existing discount, so a parent discount has to be made in Shopify first; an Amount off products discount asked for products or collections and an order discount was used instead. The app then generated 20 codes that Shopify listed as 21 codes with the main code. Plan to create the parent discount in Shopify before generating codes.

Vendor claim "$14,99 / 30 days". What we saw: The Pro plan card shows $14,99 / 30 days with the button Not available because the store is in development. No Pro approval screen, tax, trial or yearly price was seen, so the price could not be checked against a checkout. Pro adds unlimited codes per month at $14,99 per 30 days on the plan card; the amount at checkout is unknown.

sessions.what: On 26 September 2026 we built the same class-booking web app in Lovable, Replit and Emergent from one identical prompt, each on its free plan, and checked every result against 18 tests we wrote down before the first build. We changed no code: the builder only got our prompt. Lovable paid us nothing when we ran the test; it accepted us into its affiliate programme on 28 September 2026, and these findings were recorded before that.
findings: Lovable built and published the app in about ten minutes and used 4 of the 10 credits on a new account. It asked twice, to create the project and to publish, and published to a lovable.app address that stays online on the free plan with an 'Edit with Lovable' badge.

It was the only one of the three whose first version held the limit when ten people booked an eight-spot class at the same moment: eight accepted, two refused with 'Sorry, this class is full.' The other two accepted all ten.

It checked input on the server as well as in the form (a name of only spaces and a bad email were refused), kept the admin password out of the page and scripts, and prefixed CSV values starting with = + - or @ so a spreadsheet does not run them as formulas.
It needed no repair round. After republishing, every test booking was still there.

Taking the code with you works, taking the running app does not. With GitHub connected (access limited to one repository), Lovable created its own repository with the full source and database migrations and committed no secret keys. Outside Lovable, on Node 22, it installed and built without errors, but loaded no classes: the database service key and admin password stay in Lovable, so moving means setting up your own database and bringing the bookings as a CSV or Lovable's full database export.
sessions.not_tested: One run on one day on the free plan. Not a security audit or a load test, we did not measure how fast the 20 monthly Cloud credits run down, and we did not trigger Lovable's full database export.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

Install: the test started at 21:16 (Mac clock) on the App Store listing of Essential Countdown Timer by Essential Apps, which said Free plan available. Free trial available., a rating of 5.0 from 1,736 reviews. The Install button did not work for our test tool: the first submit of the install form landed on the list of apps without an install, and after the form target was set to the same tab the second submit showed the dialog Install app, which said that the app needs access to View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, Online Store, Shopify admin). Install was clicked and the app opened at once on the Free Plan, without a plan screen and without a payment screen. No account on the vendor site, password, card or phone number was asked. The Home of the app also showed a note about a partner programme (Partners earn 30% commission, First payout at $100) and a Q4 offer of 5 apps for $99 a month; neither was clicked. Core action, a top bar timer: Home, Create a new timer, Choose timer type (Product page, Top/bottom bar, Landing page marked Available with Starter plan, Cart page marked Available with Essential plan, Email timer and Checkout deadlines), Select this timer type on Top/bottom bar. After 4 steps and about 2 minutes from the start the editor stood there with the label Not published and a preview Hurry up! Sale ends in: with 23 : 59 : 48 (Hrs, Mins, Secs) and a button Shop now!. The preview also showed a block Combine with Essential Loyalty with a button Install free, which was not clicked. Clean up: the Approve screen was left with Cancel, nothing was approved and the Free Plan stayed active. sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested SalesTarget.ai in the account that we made: a natural language search for marketing agencies with 10-50 employees in the Netherlands set its own filters and showed 532 companies about 2 minutes after the start (real agencies, but also companies that are not agencies), a founders search gave 301, a draft campaign got an AI generated 3 step sequence in about 40 seconds for 1.17 AI credits and was deleted, and the Pricing page was read up to the buy buttons. The Growth plan of Email Outreach lists unlimited email accounts but warms only 5 of them, with extra warmup slots at $2 per account a month. No e-mail or phone was revealed, nothing was connected or sent and no plan was taken. Account and start: we made the SalesTarget.ai account; an earlier attempt on 17 November 2026 stopped on an expired login (the onboarding data could not be saved and the app went back to the login), so it counted for nothing. This test ran on 18 November 2026 with a valid login: our own browser tab was opened at 07:31 on the dashboard of the app (interface already in English). The dashboard offered Earn 20 Free Credits and Continue Onboarding, and the menu listed Lead Explorer, Lists, Campaigns, Email accounts, LinkedIn, Unibox, CRM, Dialer, Validation, Settings and Pricing. The balance before the test was 50 ST credits (a signup bonus of 17 November 2026) and 20 AI credits. Core action, lead search: in Lead Explorer the search bar accepts natural language. The question marketing agencies with 10-50 employees in the Netherlands was entered; after Enter (about 6 seconds, one step) the AI set the filters itself: Company Size 11-50, Country Netherlands and Industry Marketing Services. The result was Total 532 and Showing 1-20 of 532, about 2 minutes after the start. Quality, read by eye: the list holds real agencies, but also companies that are not agencies, such as a flower trade body, a city marketing organisation, a test firm and a marketing training firm. The Country column shows netherlands in lower case, and revenue and other firmographics sit behind a locked View Firmographics button. People mode: the question founders of marketing agencies in the Netherlands with 10-50 employees set Company Size 11-50, Country Netherlands, Industry advertising services and Job title founder, and gave Total 301. It is a mix of agencies and other companies (for example a car-park network and a flyer printer). E-mail and phone are hidden behind View Email (tooltip 2 credits per lead) and View Phone (tooltip 5 credits per lead); neither button was clicked, because that would reveal personal data of third parties and spend credits. No personal name of a lead is kept in the notes or in the images. Campaign and AI sequence: under Campaigns the first campaign Test Project NL Agencies was created (Draft, 0 leads). The editor has the tabs Templates, Leads, Settings and Schedule, a Save button and an AI Sequence Generator that warns This will override current steps created. It asks for the company name, services, target audience, case studies and the number of steps; with test data and 3 steps, Generate showed Generating your personalized sequence and said This usually takes 20-40 seconds. The result appeared after about 40 seconds: 3 steps with Variant 1 and Variant 2, spin options such as Hi, Hello or Hey with a first-name field, and the subject Agency SEO gaps uncovered. Use Sequence was not clicked. No mailbox or LinkedIn account was connected and nothing was sent. The campaign was deleted again through its menu. Credits after the test: ST credits 55 (plus 5 as a bonus labelled Task Completion, Create Sequence) and AI credits 18.83 (the AI Sequence Generator cost 1.17). Lead credits were not used. The test ran from 07:31 for about 10 minutes in all. Plans, read up to the buy buttons: the Pricing page was opened and Buy Now was not clicked, nothing was filled in. Lead Explorer (Launch Credit) is $49 a month with 2,000 credits and 1 user. Email Outreach (monthly, 30% off the first month for new customers): Growth $30 a month with 10,000 emails, 30,000 contacts storage, Unlimited email accounts, 1 user, 100 AI credits a month and Email warmup for 5 email accounts; Hypergrowth $79 a month with 100,000 emails, 3 users and 500 AI credits; Light Speed $299 a month with 500,000 emails, 5 users and 1,000 AI credits. Add-ons: CRM +$40 a month for every user, Dialer +$29 a month, Extra warmup slots +$2 / email account / month, client workspaces +$29 and AI credits +$10 for 400. LinkedIn is $49 per account a month ($39 from 16 to 50 accounts, $29 from 51 to 100), 1 user. All In One: Growth $169 a month (10,000 emails, 2,000 Lead Explorer credits a month, 1 LinkedIn account, Advanced CRM, 100 AI credits, 1 user, warmup for 5 accounts), Scale $319 a month (100,000 emails, 4,500 Lead Explorer credits a month, 2 LinkedIn accounts, 3 users, 500 AI credits, warmup for 20 accounts) and Ultimate $639 a month (500,000 emails, 7,000 credits, 3 LinkedIn accounts, 5 users, warmup for 50 accounts, with a wallet credit applied at purchase). Yearly billing saves 10% on All In One and 15% on Email Outreach. Settings, Subscription said No active subscriptions. Differences with the dossier: the dossier says unlimited email accounts and warm-up included. The Growth plan says Unlimited email accounts, but warmup covers only 5 email accounts and each extra warmup slot is $2 per account a month, so a team that warms many inboxes pays extra. The plan prices that the dossier names (All In One Growth $169 and Scale $319, with 3 users and 4,500 credits on Scale) match the page. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, Buy Now was not clicked and no card, total with tax or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: no plan was taken, so there was nothing to cancel; Settings, Account & Settings, Security Settings has a Delete Account button, which was not clicked, and the account was not deleted. Not tested: LinkedIn automation and the 42 day warmup (no LinkedIn account connected), e-mail warmup and mailbox connection, a real reveal of an e-mail or phone number (2 and 5 credits are confirmed only by the tooltips), CRM, Dialer, Unibox, Validation and sending. Clean up: the draft campaign was deleted; the account stays without a plan and without connected accounts; our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Essential Upsell and Cross Sell on the development store plan: a post-purchase offer, publishing it, a test checkout with the test gateway, the offer after payment, the pricing plans and the uninstall dialog. The offer was declined and nothing was paid or uninstalled. Create offer opens Choose placement type: Product page, Cart page, Pop-up, Post purchase page and Suggest new placement type; Post purchase page was chosen. A yellow bar said that the Essential Upsell app is not activated yet and to click Activate and choose Essential Upsell as the post-purchase app in Shopify, then click Save. An info block lists cases where the post-purchase funnel does not appear: payments requiring CVN, installment plans, missing shipping details and orders under $0.50. The tabs are Content, Offer and Design. Offer: trigger All products, First offer Specific products with The Compare at Price Snowboard ($785.95, compare at $885.95), Discount type No discount and Shipping type Free shipping. Save gave Offer created successfully. and Publish gave Updated successfully. Activate opened Shopify Settings, Checkout, Use an app to add features at checkout after payment, with the choices None, Essential Upsell and Post Purchase Upsell Hero; it stood on Post Purchase Upsell Hero from another test. We chose Essential Upsell and saved (Changes saved.); the funnel of the other app was not touched. A test order through the theme preview (no store password): The Complete Snowboard at $699.95, Buy it now, a made up address and the test gateway with card number 1. After Pay now the page showed an exclusive offer, a countdown Hurry! This exclusive deal expires in: 14:58, The Compare at Price Snowboard at $785.95 with $885.95 struck through, Pay Now and Decline offer. Although the offer was set to No discount, it showed a lower price, because $885.95 is the compare at price of the product. Decline led straight to the thank you page with the $699.95 order. The app dashboard afterwards showed Impressions 1, Conversions 0, Conversion Rate 0.00% and Added revenue $0.00, and the Setup Guide 1 / 3 completed. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 15:04:45 and the offer in view at about 15:08:10, about 3 minutes 25 seconds and about 17 steps (install 2, creating and publishing the offer 8, activating 3, ordering 4). The Settings, Apps row has a menu with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall; the Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: product page, cart page and pop-up offers, the app embed in the theme, paying for the offer, the paid plans and the 14-day trial, the cart drawer placement and real conversion. No kit records were entered.
findings: Vendor claim "Professional, $39.99 a month". What we saw: In the app $39.99 a month is the Growth plan (up to $2,500). Professional is $99.99 (up to $10,000) and the plan without a limit is Unlimited at $149.99 (above $10,000). The listing shows only Free, Starter, Essential and Growth. A store expecting more than $2,500 of added revenue pays $99.99 or $149.99 and not $39.99.

Vendor claim "Free plan available. Free trial available.". What we saw: The Free plan exists (up to $100 at $0/month). The 14-day free trial that the listing names for the paid plans was not shown in the app, where development stores are free anyway. Whether a paid plan starts with a 14-day trial could not be checked, because no Select plan button worked.

Vendor claim "Essential Upsell is free for development stores.". What we saw: The app says so on the Pricing plans screen, and every Select plan button was greyed out, so no Shopify approval screen was reached and nothing was approved. The prices are said to apply once the store moves to a paid Shopify plan. Testing on a development store costs nothing; the real price only shows when the store goes live.

Vendor claim "orders under $0.50". What we saw: An info block on the offer screen lists payments requiring CVN, installment plans, missing shipping details and orders under $0.50 as cases where the post-purchase funnel does not appear. A normal test order of $699.95 with the test gateway did show the offer; the listed cases were not tried. The post-purchase funnel does not run for some payments; the normal case worked.

Vendor claim "No discount". What we saw: With Discount type No discount the offer still showed $785.95 with $885.95 struck through, because $885.95 is the compare at price of the product. An offer set to No discount can still show a visible price cut if the product has a compare at price.

Vendor claim "Essential $19.99/month". What we saw: The listing and the in app Pricing plans table both show Essential at $19.99 per month (up to $1000 on the listing, $1,000 in the app), and Starter $9.99 and Growth $39.99 match as well. Every Select plan button was greyed out on the development store, so no approval screen, tax or renewal term was seen. The listed prices agree with the app; the amount at checkout is unknown.

On 17 November 2026 the session tested Koala Upsells & Gifts (listed as Koala Upsell Free Gift & BOGO) on a Shopify development store: the install through the install form, the plan wall (no free plan), the Basic Monthly test charge (approved without a card, billed 0 dollars), one free gift offer (Demo Shirt for Demo Mug) that stood in the cart as Demo Shirt $19.00 $0.00 FREE GIFT in an unsaved theme preview about 3 minutes and 9 steps after the install, the contradiction on the offer screen (Not visible, activation needed and Great job - your offer is live!), and the uninstall with a required reason. The gift picker, upsells, the Advanced and Plus plans and the real checkout were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing is apps.shopify.com/upsell-koala-gift, titled Koala Upsell Free Gift & BOGO, by ProfitKoala, with From $9.99/month. Free trial available. and a rating of 5.0 from 396 reviews; the address apps.shopify.com/koala-gifts does not exist. In the Shopify admin the app is called Koala Upsells & Gifts. The app was installed through the install form with the target set to the same tab, in our own tab, at 21:38. The screen Install app said that the app needs access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data (Products, orders, discounts, Online Store); Install was clicked. There was no separate account or password: the app opened at once on Choose your plan. Plan wall: there is no free plan and nothing could be built before a plan was chosen. The plan was activated at 21:39 after the Shopify approval screen (see Checkout); the dashboard then said Plan activated successfully!, with Theme status 0/3 app blocks added to theme and a Setup guide at 0 / 4 steps completed. Core action, a free gift added automatically: Create a Gift Offer, then Select gift offer exposure with four options, of which Add a gift to customer's cart automatically was chosen, then New gift offer with the default name Buy One Product to get a Free Gift!. The trigger was Specific Product, Demo Mug ($9.50), and the reward was Demo Shirt ($19.00) at Free. Save gave Offer created successfully!. Visibility: right after saving, the same screen showed the status Not visible, the warning Koala Upsells & Gifts app needs activation in theme settings with Your offers aren't available on your product page, and at the same time a card saying Great job - your offer is live!. These contradict each other: the offer is only visible once the app embed is switched on in the theme. In the theme editor (preview with the app embeds) the embed Koala Gifts was switched on and NOT saved. In the unsaved preview, adding Demo Mug to the cart gave a cart with Demo Shirt $19.00 $0.00 FREE GIFT and Demo Mug $9.50. The editor was left with Leave page, so nothing was saved. No gift widget was seen on the product page itself, only in the cart. From the install at 21:38 to the free gift in the cart at 21:41 took about 3 minutes and about 9 steps (choose and approve the plan, choose the offer type, trigger, gift, save, switch on the embed, open the product, add to cart). The checkout of the store was not opened. Plans in the app (Choose your plan, with the line The price for your plan will be based on your Shopify plan): Basic Monthly, $19.99 struck through and $9.99 a month, Start 14-day free trial, with the badge Save up to 50%; Basic Annual, $19.99 struck through and $7.99 a month, Billed yearly, with the badges Save up to 60% and Priority support. Both say You won't be charged before your trial ends. Cancel anytime. The features listed are pop-up upsells on add to cart click, product add-ons and gift banners, gifts added to the cart automatically, rules by customer location and historical purchases, block designs, unlimited gifted products and upsell revenue, and live chat. The Advanced and Plus prices were not seen because the development store is on Basic. Checkout: Start 14-day free trial on Basic Monthly opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the notice You will not be billed for this test charge., Basic Monthly, $19,99 struck through and $9,99 USD every 30 days, a label $10,00 off all charges, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Subtotal $19,99 plus any applicable taxes, Discount $10,00 off, Total $9,99 Due 1 Dec, and a row Add payment method that did not have to be filled in. Approve worked without a card and was clicked: a test charge was approved, no card was entered and no payment method was added, and nothing was billed. The Basic Annual screen was not opened. Cancelling: the route in the app was not looked for. In Shopify, Settings, Apps, the menu next to the app has Uninstall; its dialog says You'll no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason for uninstalling is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled at 21:44 (You've successfully uninstalled Koala Upsells & Gifts) and the subscription lapses with it. Differences from the review: the listing and the dossier say the app is free for development stores, but the app asked for a plan and a test charge before anything could be built. The strikethrough $19.99 on both plans is not in the dossier, and the annual plan is shown as $7.99 a month billed yearly, which makes $95.88 a year. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: the gift picker (Give customers a choice of products), gift banners, upsells, the Koala Bundles tab, Kopa AI, the Advanced and Plus plans, the real checkout, analytics and live chat. Clean up: the embed was not saved. The offer and the plan went with the uninstall. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session set up a trial of the Create site builder. The first attempt with the template Thread stayed on a loading screen for more than 4 minutes and ended with You don't currently have access to any sites, so no site was made. The second attempt, through the Create New Site wizard of 3 steps, gave a first page about 18 seconds after the template choice (18:44:07 to 18:44:25), and a changed heading, an added block and a stock photo from Unsplash were saved at 18:46:36, about 2.5 minutes in all. The trial lasts 30 days, but the site cannot be published in it: Publish says that a plan is needed, and no card field or domain question appeared. The in-app prices are 12.09, 24.19 and 48.39 euro a month, which are the dossier monthly prices with VAT added (the public page shows 8.33, 16.66 and 33.33 euro billed yearly, excluding VAT). Nothing was published, bought or cancelled.
findings: Text we checked: "No credit card needed". What we saw: No card field was shown at the template choice, in the wizard or in the app up to the plan dialog, and no Choose button was clicked.

Text we checked: "Oh yes... no-obligation free trial". What we saw: The trial exists and has no obligation, but the dialog of the Publish button says that on a free trial the site cannot be published to the web or use advanced features yet.

Text we checked: "You have 29 days remaining on your trial. Upgrade now to enable your website". What we saw: The bar on the dashboard shows 29 days left on the first day, so the trial lasts 30 days. The pricing page does not state the length.

Text we checked: "You're currently on a free trial, so you won't be able to publish your site to the web or access advanced features just yet". What we saw: Publish opened a dialog with this line and the button Upgrade Now. It was not possible to publish, also not on a free subdomain of the builder, and nothing was published.
Text we checked: "Business €33.33/mo, Professional €16.66/mo, Portfolio €8.33/mo". What we saw: The public pricing page shows these yearly prices excluding VAT, the same as the dossier yearly prices.
not_tested: Publishing the site, which needs a paid plan.
Connecting or buying a domain.
Branding on the trial site and the shop with products.
A payment screen, a tax amount and a total.
Cancelling; the dashboard has Manage Subscription but there is no paid plan.
Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session set up a trial of the Create site builder. The first attempt with the template Thread stayed on a loading screen for more than 4 minutes and ended with You don't currently have access to any sites, so no site was made. The second attempt, through the Create New Site wizard of 3 steps, gave a first page about 18 seconds after the template choice (18:44:07 to 18:44:25), and a changed heading, an added block and a stock photo from Unsplash were saved at 18:46:36, about 2.5 minutes in all. The trial lasts 30 days, but the site cannot be published in it: Publish says that a plan is needed, and no card field or domain question appeared. The in-app prices are 12.09, 24.19 and 48.39 euro a month, which are the dossier monthly prices with VAT added (the public page shows 8.33, 16.66 and 33.33 euro billed yearly, excluding VAT). Nothing was published, bought or cancelled. Account and start: we created the account (app.create.net, Create, Brighton UK, 25 years) and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser from 18:40 (Amsterdam). The interface was already in English and the first screen was Choose your website template. The dossier name is Create and the review is on AIBM (the b2b section, review page of Create). Audience: the request named Beginners building a first site (pain: I want a site without a designer and without a card). The dossier has no group for beginners; the best fit is UK makers and small shops selling physical goods, whose pain is a hosted site instead of a builder learned alone. Attempt 1: the template Thread was chosen at 18:40:22. The page new-site-loading stayed on the loading screen for more than 4 minutes, with the messages Customising your design..., Adding the finishing touches..., Applying your options... and Almost there... in a loop. Afterwards the sites list said You don't currently have access to any sites, so no site had been made. Attempt 2: Create New Site started a wizard of 3 steps (What's your site called?, What's your site about? with Crafts, and What content do you need? with Home, Services, Shop, Blog, Contact, About and Gallery as standard), begun at 18:43:33. The wizard fills the first part of the site name itself; that was not typed and is not shown. The template Thread was chosen again at 18:44:07 (Choose Template). Core action: at 18:44:25, about 18 seconds after the choice, the dashboard Home stood there and the homepage of the template already had a heading, a button, texts, testimonials and a footer. The page was edited through Content, Pages and the edit icon (an intro dialog Introducing Content Pages in 60 Seconds was closed): the heading was replaced by My first test site, and a new block Heading Text (Add Block, 322 blocks to choose from) with the heading Hello from my test page was added at the bottom; the message Save successful appeared. Image: Block Settings, Style, Background, Select Image opened the Image Library, which said You do not currently have any images in your library. So Import Stock Images (Unsplash, Photos supplied by Unsplash) was used with the search term yarn; the message Successfully imported into your images and Image uploaded followed, and the photo was set as the background of the first block. Nothing was uploaded from the laptop. Time: template chosen at 18:44:07, first page at 18:44:25, heading, image and extra block edited and saved at 18:46:36, so about 2.5 minutes in all; attempt 1 took more than 4 minutes without a result. Upgrade now to enable your website. with the button Upgrade Now; the task list offers Get a discount for your first subscription payment (15 percent), The Design area, Add an image, Create a holding page, Register a Domain and Publish your website. Public pricing page (billed annually, excluding VAT; the page says Prices displayed are exclusive of VAT): Business 33.33 euro a month, Professional 16.66 euro, Portfolio 8.33 euro. Inside the app, after Upgrade Now (monthly view): Business 48.39 euro a month (Pay yearly to save 96.78 euro), Professional 24.19 euro (marked most popular, Pay yearly to save 48.38 euro), Portfolio 12.09 euro (Pay yearly to save 24.18 euro). The session notes read these as the monthly prices including VAT at 21 percent, which equals the dossier monthly prices (9.99, 19.99 and 39.99 euro) with VAT added; the difference with the dossier is VAT, not a price change. Not tested: publishing (needs a paid plan), connecting or buying a domain, branding on the trial site, a payment screen, cancelling and a shop with products. sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Essential Preorder (reviewed as Essent Preorder Back in Stock) on a Shopify development store: the install through the install form, the app opening without a plan choice or a card, a preorder campaign for The Out of Stock Snowboard (0 available) published in the app, then the badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and the button Preorder in an unsaved theme preview after the app embed was switched on by hand (about 3 minutes and about 12 clicks from the install; the embed was switched off again), the plans screen with four paid plans and a 30% first month discount, the Shopify approval screen for Lite (a 14-day trial; it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence; nothing approved), after which the campaign was deleted and the app uninstalled. The back in stock alert, mixed carts and deposits were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the app was installed from its App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/essential-pre-order, called Essential Preorder in the admin) through the install form with the target set to the same tab, in our own tab, from 21:45:24; the first submit only showed the Apps page, the second showed the dialog Install app, and Install was clicked. The app opened without a plan choice and without a payment step, with a Setup Guide at 0 / 3 completed. No separate account, password, card or phone number was asked. Core action, a preorder campaign for a product with no stock: Create preorder campaign, the tab Preorder products, Add specific products, The Out of Stock Snowboard (0 available), Publish. The message was Campaign created successfully., the status was Live, and a banner said Essent Preorder Back in Stock app is not activated yet. The app preview showed a sample product (White T-shirt) with a badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and a button Preorder. In the theme editor (unsaved preview of the product) the product showed, without the app embed, a choice One-time Purchase $885.95 and Preorder $885.95 (a selling plan) with Add to cart. With the embed Essential Preorder switched on, the preview showed a badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and a button Preorder, with an overlay Click "Save" to enable the app embed. The embed was switched off again, nothing was saved (Leave page) and the store itself was not looked at (it has a password). The first result, the Preorder button in the preview, came at about 21:48:15, about 3 minutes and about 12 clicks after the install, including the plans page and choosing the product. Plans in the app (the plans screen, each with Start FREE 14 days trial and 30 day money back guarantee, and a label -30% first mo): Lite $3.47 first month, then $4.95 a month, 100 preorders and 1000 back in stock notifications a month; Starter $6.27 first month, then $8.95, 300 preorders and 2500 notifications, with mixed cart validation; Essentials $17.47 first month, then $24.95, 500 preorders and 10000 notifications; Professional $41.3 first month, then $59, unlimited. Using the app was free by default: it opened without a card. The free limits of the listing (25 preorders, 300 notifications) were not seen in the app, because the plans screen has no Free card. Checkout: Start FREE 14 days trial on Lite opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the plan LITE, $4,95 $3,47 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Total $3,47 due 1 Dec, an App spending limit of a maximum of $500,00 USD per 30 days, a row Add payment method and a greyed Approve button. The screen did NOT say that a test charge would not be billed, and a payment method was needed, so the plan was not approved. No card was entered. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was no cancel button to look for. The uninstall dialog (Uninstall Essential Preorder?) says that you can no longer use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and asks for a Reason for uninstalling, which is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled (You've successfully uninstalled Essential Preorder). Differences from the review: the listing names the Lite price as $4.95; the app shows the same regular prices and a 30% discount on the first month. The free limits of the listing were not seen. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: the back in stock alert and restock e-mails, mixed carts, deposits and split payment, the real checkout, the store itself (it has a password), the paid plans and their approval, and any contact with the vendor. Clean up: the campaign was deleted (the confirmation was Yes, turn off Continue selling); our notes say that the stock was never changed and that no test product was made, the existing product was used. The embed was not saved. The app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Brandye on a Shopify development store: the install, the onboarding, one AI generated product quiz saved and set live, the Recommendation tab, the Shopify plan page that offered no plans and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no approval screen was reached; the app embed was saved in the theme. Install: the install form was sent at 12:52:43; the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data and was approved. The app opened on Welcome to Brandye with the question What do you want to set up first? (AI Shopping Assistant, AI Product Questions, Product Finder Quiz), followed by an optional question How did you hear about Brandye? that we skipped. The dashboard said On your store 0 of 3 live. No separate account, card or phone number was asked. The buttons on the onboarding screen only reacted after a few seconds, and a first click on Create a quiz seemed to do nothing. Core action: from the dashboard, Quiz Set up, Create your quiz, Create quiz (Quiz 1) and Generate Quiz with AI. The dialog Generate quiz with AI had a prefilled Quiz goal and Target customers. The first Generate gave Couldn't generate your quiz and Try again. If it keeps failing, add more detail to the goal. The second try with our own goal (help shoppers pick the right snowboard for their riding level, terrain and budget) worked in about 10 seconds. Result: a flow diagram with 7 questions and branches (among them What's your current snowboarding experience level? and What is your target budget for the board?, and as last question an email request for a stance setup guide) that ends in a results node. We saved it with Save (Questions got a green tick), chose Placement Full-page quiz and saved it; the placement editor shows a style and a Gallery preview but no real shopper view. The dashboard then said Quiz Live with Quiz submissions 0 and Revenue influenced US$ 0, and the Recommendation tab said All products are currently eligible for recommendations. Timing, approximate tester observations: install at 12:52:43, quiz generated and saved at about 12:57 (about 4 minutes and 12 steps including the onboarding), Live on the dashboard at about 12:59. The shopper view was NOT seen: the theme editor showed the added Quiz app block (handle quiz-1, Embedded) empty in the preview, although the Brandye app embed was on. Plans: the app has no plan screen (its menu has AI Product Questions, Quizzes, AI Knowledge, MCP and Settings, and Settings holds only email summaries). The Shopify plan page for the app said Select a plan, No plans are available for your store and Contact the app developer for help choosing a plan. The App Store listing says Free plan available. Free trial available. and the dossier names Starter at $19, but nothing could be chosen or paid in our store. There was no Approve subscription screen, so nothing was approved and no card was asked. Cancelling: no plan or trial existed, so there was nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the app menu and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Brandye? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Testing multiple apps). The uninstall was confirmed at about 13:01 and the app is gone from the installed apps. Not tested: the AI Shopping Assistant, AI Product Questions, French or other languages, the quiz in the store preview, a recommendation result, integrations such as Klaviyo, any plan or paid feature and a data export. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test. In the theme the Brandye app embed was switched on and saved, and the Home page got an empty Apps section because the Quiz app block was not kept after a reload; this stays in the theme and was not changed further. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
findings: Text we checked: "Generate Quiz with AI". What we saw: The first Generate gave an error (Couldn't generate your quiz); the second try with our own goal worked in about 10 seconds and gave a flow of 7 questions with branches, saved and set live as a full-page quiz about 4 minutes and 12 steps after the install. The quiz was not seen as a shopper sees it.

Text we checked: "All products are currently eligible for recommendations". What we saw: The Recommendation tab says that by default all products are eligible and no exclusions are configured; no recommendation result was produced because the quiz was never answered.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Brandye on a Shopify development store: the install, the onboarding, one AI generated product quiz saved and set live, the Recommendation tab, the Shopify plan page that offered no plans and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was paid and no approval screen was reached; the app embed was saved in the theme. Install: the install form was sent at 12:52:43; the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data and was approved. The app opened on Welcome to Brandye with the question What do you want to set up first? (AI Shopping Assistant, AI Product Questions, Product Finder Quiz), followed by an optional question How did you hear about Brandye? that we skipped. The dashboard said On your store 0 of 3 live. No separate account, card or phone number was asked. The buttons on the onboarding screen only reacted after a few seconds, and a first click on Create a quiz seemed to do nothing. Core action: from the dashboard, Quiz Set up, Create your quiz, Create quiz (Quiz 1) and Generate Quiz with AI. The dialog Generate quiz with AI had a prefilled Quiz goal and Target customers. The first Generate gave Couldn't generate your quiz and Try again. If it keeps failing, add more detail to the goal. The second try with our own goal (help shoppers pick the right snowboard for their riding level, terrain and budget) worked in about 10 seconds. Result: a flow diagram with 7 questions and branches (among them What's your current snowboarding experience level? and What is your target budget for the board?, and as last question an email request for a stance setup guide) that ends in a results node. We saved it with Save (Questions got a green tick), chose Placement Full-page quiz and saved it; the placement editor shows a style and a Gallery preview but no real shopper view. The dashboard then said Quiz Live with Quiz submissions 0 and Revenue influenced US$ 0, and the Recommendation tab said All products are currently eligible for recommendations. Timing, approximate tester observations: install at 12:52:43, quiz generated and saved at about 12:57 (about 4 minutes and 12 steps including the onboarding), Live on the dashboard at about 12:59. The shopper view was NOT seen: the theme editor showed the added Quiz app block (handle quiz-1, Embedded) empty in the preview, although the Brandye app embed was on. Plans: the app has no plan screen (its menu has AI Product Questions, Quizzes, AI Knowledge, MCP and Settings, and Settings holds only email summaries). The Shopify plan page for the app said Select a plan, No plans are available for your store and Contact the app developer for help choosing a plan. The App Store listing says Free plan available. Free trial available. and the dossier names Starter at $19, but nothing could be chosen or paid in our store. There was no Approve subscription screen, so nothing was approved and no card was asked. Cancelling: no plan or trial existed, so there was nothing to cancel. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the app menu and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Brandye? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (Testing multiple apps). The uninstall was confirmed at about 13:01 and the app is gone from the installed apps. Not tested: the AI Shopping Assistant, AI Product Questions, French or other languages, the quiz in the store preview, a recommendation result, integrations such as Klaviyo, any plan or paid feature and a data export. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test. In the theme the Brandye app embed was switched on and saved, and the Home page got an empty Apps section because the Quiz app block was not kept after a reload; this stays in the theme and was not changed further. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The first AI generation failed, the onboarding buttons reacted slowly, the quiz block showed empty in the theme preview and was not kept after a reload, and the plan page of Shopify said that no plans were available for the store.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Seele in our free account: one prompt for a small cat game, which gave a game brief, 9 concept assets and a playable prototype in about 10 minutes for 45 Koins, the Pro badge on the button for the full game, the plans window on the Monthly and Annually tabs, and the cancel text in the FAQ. The full game, the checkout and the coupon were not reached. Nothing was paid. Start and account: the test started at 16:21:53 (Dutch time) with a prompt sent at the workspace of the vendor site, in the free Seele our account (plan Free, 360 Koins), already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English. The model was Seele02-flash (Fast, affordable, perfect for basic games, Current); the Pro and Ultra models showed Unlock this model and were locked. The balance before was 360 Koins. Core action, a small game from one prompt: the prompt was A simple 2D game where a cat jumps over boxes; arrow keys to move, space to jump, score counter. After about 1 minute the app asked 3 questions: Engine (Three.js, Godot, Unity or Unreal, where Unreal was locked), Art style and Run length; we chose Three.js, Pixel arcade and Endless score chase (the recommended default), which took 5 extra clicks. Seele then made a Game brief (Concept, Full game not built yet), 9 concept assets (covers, three cats and three scenes) and a playable prototype, with the message Worked for 9m 34s. The result stood at the latest at 16:32:41, about 10 minutes after the start. The balance after was 315 Koins, so 45 Koins were used; the page Usage and Koin said 29 spent this month and 315 current balance. The prototype (TRY THE BOXES) says that the shapes are drawn in code, so the art is not final. We clicked Start and pressed Space: the cat jumped and the score rose (SCORE 11, BOXES 1 / 26, COMBO 1.1x); after that the screen said THE BOX WON. with a button RUN AGAIN. So the result is playable, but it is a prototype with shapes and not a finished game. The full game: the button Make the full game with AI carries a Pro badge and so does the line LET AI BUILD THE FULL GAME in the brief; the text says the full game is built to commercial quality, with upgraded visuals, levels and audio. We did NOT click it, so no second generation was made and the full game was not seen. On the plan card Standard says it unlocks full game generation, so the Pro badge on the button and the Standard card do not match; this stays an open point. A survey (how did you find us?) appeared and was closed without filling it in; the offer Rate SEELE +100 Koins was not used. Plans: the Upgrade button opened the window One subscription, from games to 3D. Monthly: Standard $20 / mo (Unlocks full game generation, the Pro model and project downloads; 2,000 Koins / mo), Pro $100 / mo (Most popular; Flagship model plus a commercial license, best value; 10,000 + 2,000 Koins / mo) and Ultra $200 / mo (20,000 + 5,000 Koins / mo with the choices 25k, 37.5k, 62.5k and 125k; All-channel commercial use and Mini-game publishing). Annually (Save 22%): Standard $17 / mo (billed $200 / year), Pro $78 / mo (crossed out $100, billed $936 / year) and Ultra $167 / mo (billed $2,000 / year). The card in the sidebar said Upgrade to Pro $100 / mo with 12,000 Koin a month. Koin packs: 2,000 for $20, 5,000 for $50, 20,000 for $200 and 50,000 for $500. Differences with the dossier: Pro is $100 a month and $78 a month billed annually, where the dossier has $50 and $39; Pro has 10,000 + 2,000 Koins a month, where the dossier has 6,000; Standard ($20 and $17) and Ultra ($200 and $167) agree; the dossier says about 120 to 140 Koins give a playable game on the Flash model, and we used 45 Koins for the brief and a playable prototype, which is not the full game; the dossier says the upgrade page applies a 50% first month coupon by default, and we saw no such offer on the plans window or in the sidebar. Checkout: NOT reached. The click on Subscribe to Standard was refused by the permission layer of the session, so we did not go on to the Stripe payment screen, and the coupon could not be checked there. Cancelling: the FAQ in the plans window says Cancel anytime from your billing settings and that paid plans stay active until the end of the current billing period (the text was cut off). The account is Free, so there was nothing to cancel. The account menu has Profile, Usage and Koin, API Keys, Affiliate program, Creator Center, Preferences, Terms and account (User Agreement, Privacy Policy, Subscription and refund policy), Feedback and Log out; no Delete account button was found in Profile or in Terms and account, and nothing was deleted. Not tested: the full game, publishing or sharing, revisions and their Koin cost, the Pro and Ultra models, commercial use, the Stripe checkout and the coupon, the claimed 120 to 140 Koins for a playable game, and cancelling. Clean up: the account and the test project (Cat Jumping Over Boxes Game) were left as they are, with 315 Koins. All our tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested iubenda on the Free plan of an account we created, with a made-up site. After the site scan a plan window offered the Free plan or Advanced, and the Free plan went on without a card. A privacy policy was generated and a cookie banner previewed; the free banner shows the label Created with iubenda, and GDPR stood on manual configuration with a warning for Denmark and Greece. Terms and Conditions need the paid Advanced plan. Upgrade was not clicked, so no payment page was seen; the public page lists Advanced at EUR 19.99 per site a month on yearly billing. Account and start: we created the account and confirmed the e-mail address; our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab, on 19 November 2026; the start time was not recorded and the session ended at about 10:20 CET. The interface was in English. No phone number was asked anywhere. The dossier name is iubenda and the review is on AIBM (b2b/iubenda-review). Core action, a privacy policy and a cookie banner for one site: the made-up site test-shop-example.com was added. The scan gave 0%, Passed 0, Attention required 0, Needs your input 19 and Not applicable 3, with Proceed with assisted configuration. After the scan the window Choose a plan showed the Free plan at 89% (Limited configuration, missing Terms and Conditions and Premium Features) and the Advanced plan at 100% with Upgrade to Advanced and a 14 days money-back guarantee; Continue without recommended features kept the Free plan, and no card was asked. The site console showed FREE, an Upgrade button, Languages EN (US) and the checklist Step 1 Activate (0/3), Step 2 Configure and Step 3 Embed; Activate Terms & Conditions said the current plan does not include it. The privacy policy generator was run with a made-up owner and the services Contact form, Google Analytics 4 and Mailing list, and a policy was generated; it was not activated or embedded. The cookie solution was set up with GDPR, LGPD, Switzerland and US State Laws on. The preview on desktop, tablet and mobile showed a black banner with Learn more and customize, Reject and Accept and the label Created with iubenda. GDPR and LGPD stood on Manual configuration, and GDPR said Not configured according to the requirements of Denmark, Greece. Format and position, Text, Theme and the Privacy widget are options. The banner was not saved and not embedded anywhere. Plans: On iubenda.com/en/pricing, per site per month when billed yearly: Essentials EUR 4.99 (up to 25K pageviews, Standard Privacy & Cookie Policy, Mild branding capability), Advanced EUR 19.99 (Most popular, up to 50K pageviews, Complete legal documents, all available languages) and Ultimate EUR 79.99 (up to 150K pageviews, Advanced legal documents, Full branding capability, all available languages). In the app the plan window after the scan offers the Free plan (89%, Limited configuration, without Terms and Conditions and Premium Features) or the Advanced plan (100%, Monthly or Yearly, Save up to 10% with annual billing, 14 days money-back guarantee); no amounts are shown there. Checkout: no checkout was reached. Upgrade to Advanced was not clicked, so no payment page, card field, tax or total was seen; on the Free plan no card was asked at any point. Cancelling: Account, Account & Billing info, Subscription details offers payment information and cancellation options for each purchased plan; Manage opened Manage Subscriptions with only Payment Methods, so on the Free plan there is nothing to cancel. Account & Security has Delete your account, which was not clicked. Not tested: the consent database, the free pageview limit from the dossier, activating or embedding the policy or the banner, Terms and Conditions, other languages, a paid plan and cancelling it. Clean up: nothing was placed on a real site; the account and the made-up site stay on the Free plan. The own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The free banner carries the label Created with iubenda. GDPR stays on manual configuration and warns that the setup does not meet the rules of Denmark and Greece until you change it. Terms and Conditions and the remaining 11% of the checklist need Advanced. The plan window inside the app shows no amounts, only the saving on yearly billing.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 5 November 2026 on the free trial: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We went through sign-up, opened the Cloud editor and sent our test prompt to the built-in AI assistant. The request was blocked, so no page was built. We did not publish, export or open checkout.
findings: Sign-up asks four required survey questions (business type, company size, role, how you found Brizy), then shows a member dashboard with 'Start free trial Cloud'. No card was requested.
The trial banner read 'Your trial ends in 14 days! Upgrade to publish your website.' The new project card was labelled PRO PROJECT.
'Create New Website' offers four starting methods: From Scratch, Start with a template, Generate with AI 1.9 and Generate with AI 2.0 (Beta).

Our first prompt in the AI panel ended in 'Out of AI credits - AI credits limit reached', with top-ups of $10, $25 and $50 on offer, plus 'Couldn't finish your request'. The plan cards say 'AI Builder Included', so the trial's AI allowance is unclear.

The plan page had Yearly -20% preselected: Personal $19/mo (1 website), Agency $69/mo (10 websites), White Label $159/mo and a custom Enterprise plan with API access and SSO. We did not look at monthly prices.
not_tested: A completed AI or manual page, and Save Draft: the AI request was blocked and we did not build by hand
Export, re-import, roles, API settings, downgrade and cancellation
